Common questions

## Buying a home in Myrtle Beach: FAQ

### How much do I need for a down payment to buy a home in Myrtle Beach?
Often less than you expect. VA and USDA loans allow zero down, FHA asks for a small down payment, and South Carolina down payment assistance programs can cover much of the rest. Our down payment assistance guide lists the current programs and amounts.

### What are the steps to buy a house in Myrtle Beach?
Get pre-approved for a loan, tour and choose a home, make an offer, complete inspections, and close with a South Carolina attorney, which the state requires. Our buying in Myrtle Beach guide walks through each step and the local costs.

### How much are property taxes on a Myrtle Beach home?
Your legal residence is taxed at the 4 percent rate and is exempt from the school operating tax; a second home or rental is taxed at 6 percent, three to four times more. Our Horry County property tax calculator shows the exact bill for any price.

### Do I need flood insurance to buy in Myrtle Beach?
It depends on the flood zone, and the zone alone does not settle it, since many homes outside the high-risk zones have still flooded. Our coastal insurance guide explains how to check before you offer.

Choosing a neighborhood

# What are the best neighborhoods in Myrtle Beach? Pick by what you love.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated October 22, 2026
Thirteen neighborhoods near Myrtle Beach, grouped by what each does best.

The short answer
For a walk to the beach, the best neighborhood near Myrtle Beach is Cherry Grove. For a golf course neighborhood, Tidewater. For a new house, Deerfield. For a boat, Plantation Lakes. For a town center you can walk, The Market Common. For a lower price, Avalon.

## What does each neighborhood do best?

### Walk to the beach
Cherry Grove : a record shark
Surfside Beach : a free pier

### Golf course neighborhoods
Pine Lakes : golf since 1927
Tidewater : houses on the fairways
Barefoot Resort : a waterway course
Prince Creek : where pros played
Wild Wing : a Monday night league

### A boat or a paddle
Plantation Lakes : pontoon boats
Waterbridge : kayaks from a dock

### A town center you can walk
Market Common : a Saturday market

### New houses
Deerfield : new on old golf land

### More house for the money
Avalon : ball fields inside
The Farm : 280 acres of open land

## 1. Cherry Grove: a fishing pier with a world-record shark
In 1964 a 1,780-pound tiger shark was landed from Cherry Grove Pier, a world record at the time. The pier is about a 12-minute walk, about half a mile, from the middle of Cherry Grove.

U.S. government aerial photo
Cherry Grove Pier from above, running out past the surf, with beach houses behind the sand.

A public beach access is about a tenth of a mile from the center of the neighborhood. North Myrtle Beach allows leashed dogs on the beach all year, except at midday in summer.
Away from the condo towers on the ocean, Cherry Grove's streets hold about 1,700 houses. Most of the houses listed for sale here are raised beach houses.
Plan on flood insurance. Almost every home here is in a high-risk flood zone, where a lender usually requires it.
Houses in Cherry Grove usually sold for about $695,000 last year. More than half of the homes for sale here are listed with no homeowners association (HOA) fee.

## 2. Surfside Beach, ocean side: a free concrete pier with two restaurants
The ocean side of Surfside Beach has its own town pier, and walking onto it is free . The concrete pier runs 814 feet into the ocean, with two restaurants, an ice cream shop and a bait and tackle shop.

U.S. government aerial photo
The Surfside Beach Pier from the air, with streets of beach houses behind the sand.

The pier and the sand are about a nine-minute walk from the center of the neighborhood. A summer evening can end out on the pier, which stays open until one in the morning from April through October.
Surfside Beach began as part of a rice plantation called The Ark. The name Surfside Beach came from a Florida town. Its streets mix older one-story ranch houses with raised beach houses.
About one home in four on the ocean side is in a high-risk flood zone, where a lender usually requires flood insurance.
Houses on the ocean side of Surfside Beach usually sold for about $705,000 last year, and condos for about $405,000. Most homes for sale here are listed with no HOA fee.

## 3. Pine Lakes: where Sports Illustrated was planned
Sports Illustrated was planned at Pine Lakes . In 1954 a group of Time-Life executives came to play the course and plan a new weekly sports magazine.

Photo: Pubdog
The 1927 clubhouse at Pine Lakes Country Club, on the National Register of Historic Places.

Pine Lakes Country Club opened in 1927 as Myrtle Beach's first golf course. Robert White, a native of St. Andrews, Scotland, and the first president of the PGA of America, designed it. The club is known as The Granddaddy.
Beside the club, in Myrtle Beach, The Preserve at Pine Lakes and Pine Lakes Estates hold houses much newer than the course. Most of the houses listed for sale there have the primary bedroom on the main floor. Owners in The Preserve share their own pool.
Few of the houses are on the course itself: only 13 of their 250 house lots border it.
Houses here usually sold for about $600,000 last year, and a house in The Preserve pays an HOA fee of about $95 a month.

## 4. Tidewater Plantation: houses on the fairways
About seven of every ten houses in Tidewater Plantation have lots that border the golf course, and many streets curve between two fairways.

U.S. government aerial photo
Tidewater from above: houses under the trees, with golf fairways on both sides of them.

The neighborhood is on a neck of land between the Intracoastal Waterway and Cherry Grove Inlet, with salt marsh along its edges. Many of the houses stand under tall trees, and some streets carry sailing names, such as Spinnaker Drive and Topsail Lane.
The course is public, so golfers who do not live here play past the back yards.
Houses in Tidewater usually sold for about $625,000 last year, and the HOA fee for a house is about $230 a month.

## 5. Barefoot Resort: a golf course along the waterway
For a golfer, the Greg Norman course has seven holes along the waterway and wide fairways. Barefoot sells a second round the same day at a lower rate, booked when the first round ends.

Barefoot Resort's road to the shops crosses a swing bridge from the 1930s, moved here from Edenton, North Carolina. Barefoot Landing's shops and restaurants are on the far side of the Intracoastal Waterway, about six minutes from the condos by car.
In the Yacht Club Villas, North Tower, Dye Townhomes and the Retreat, most homes are condos, about 390 of them, with about 80 houses. Owners in two of the resort's associations share the North Tower pool beside the waterway.
With so few houses, a buyer who wants a yard of their own has little to choose from here.
Homes in these four Barefoot sections, mostly condos, usually sold for about $430,000 last year, and the condo fee is about $680 a month.

## 6. Prince Creek: a course where the pros played
Prince Creek's sections border TPC Myrtle Beach, a Tom Fazio course. Tom Watson won the Senior PGA Tour Championship there in 2000, and Lee Trevino and Gary Player have played it too.

U.S. government aerial photo
Prince Creek from above: streets of houses beside the TPC Myrtle Beach golf course.

From the middle of Prince Creek, the entrance to Huntington Beach State Park is about 12 minutes by car. The park has a wide beach, Atalaya, a Moorish-style winter home, and a freshwater lake where alligators are easy to spot.
Prince Creek mixes houses and townhomes, in sections of their own, and builders have also sold new homes here for about $320,000. The HOA fee is about $100 to $390 a month, depending on the section. Our agents check which section a home is in before you make an offer.
Most of the houses are not on the course itself: of about 640 houses in Prince Creek outside the Seasons section, about 19 have lots that border it.
Homes in Prince Creek usually sold for about $490,000 last year.

## 7. Wild Wing Plantation: a Monday night golf league
On summer Monday nights, Wild Wing runs a community golf league . Teams play nine holes on its Hummingbird course, with a playoff at the end of the season.

Wishbones Bar and Grill, at the club, has a full bar and two indoor TrackMan golf simulators. The main course, the Avocet, was designed by Jeff Brauer and Larry Nelson.
Many streets are named for water birds, such as Wood Stork Drive and Black Skimmer Drive. The lots along them are big, more than a third of an acre in a typical case.
Wild Wing is inside the city of Conway, and a beach day starts with a drive of about 20 minutes.
Houses in Wild Wing usually sold for about $600,000 last year, and the HOA fee is about $135 a month.

## 8. Plantation Lakes: pontoon boats on a lake with 15 miles of shoreline
In Carolina Forest, owners at Plantation Lakes take pontoon boats out on a lake with about 15 miles of shoreline. About two of every three houses have lots that border the water, and some have a dock of their own.

U.S. government aerial photo
Plantation Lakes from above: houses along the lake, and the boat docks at the owners’ amenity area.

An owner can take the boat to the amenity area, which has day and overnight docks and a boat ramp. On a cool evening, the clubhouse has a great room with a fireplace and a reading and card room.
A house lot here is typically about half an acre.
Boats on the lake are limited to 19 feet, with small motors.
Houses in Plantation Lakes usually sold for about $740,000 last year, and the HOA fee is about $125 a month.

## 9. Waterbridge: kayaks from a floating dock, and potluck Thursdays
In Carolina Forest, Waterbridge owners can launch a kayak on the neighborhood's lakes from a floating dock. The lakes take only boats with no motor or an electric one.

Walking paths cross the water on bridges. The HOA's calendar holds card nights, bunco, mahjong, a book club and potluck Thursdays, and the fitness center at the clubhouse is open around the clock.
Owners also have a storage area for boats and jet skis. It is full now, so we ask about a space before you offer.
Builders are still selling new houses on the newest streets.
Resale houses in Waterbridge usually sold for about $630,000 last year, and new ones from builders for about $550,000. The HOA fee is about $150 a month.

## 10. The Market Common: a Saturday market you can walk to
From the middle of The Market Common, the farmers market at Valor Park is about a five-minute walk. It is held on Saturdays from April to mid-December.

U.S. government aerial photo
The Market Common from the air: its homes, outlined, Valor Park, where the Saturday market is held, and Grand Park.

The neighborhood stands on the old Myrtle Beach Air Force Base, which closed in 1993. Three Air Force jets, among them an A-10 Warthog, stand in Warbird Park, on loan to the city.
Grand Park, with seven ball fields, picnic shelters and a playground, is a two-minute walk from the middle of the neighborhood. The houses and townhomes are close together, beside a district of shops and offices.
Houses in The Market Common usually sold for about $540,000 last year, and townhomes for about $398,000.

## 11. Deerfield Plantation area: new houses on old golf land
Deerfield is built around the old Deer Track golf courses near Surfside Beach. A typical lot in the older streets is about a third of an acre, and new houses now stand on the old South Course.

The owners' association owns about 14 acres of lake and canals among the homes. The beach is about seven minutes away by car, and at the closest access all three parking spaces are for golf carts.
On the old North Course, building has only begun, so homes near it are beside a building site.
Homes in the older streets of the Deerfield Plantation area usually sold for about $355,000 last year, and the HOA fee is under $90 a month.

## 12. Avalon: ball fields in the middle of the neighborhood
In the middle of Avalon, the owners' association holds about nine acres of amenity land with a baseball field, soccer fields and a beach volleyball court. A ball game needs no drive.

The same grounds have a playground, and the association holds a second, smaller amenity area too. Avalon is in Carolina Forest, about a 20-minute drive from the beach.
The houses are a mix of one-story and two-story, and almost every one is outside the high-risk flood zone. The ones for sale have about 1,700 square feet.
The ones for sale were built between 2000 and 2006, so our agents check the roof and the air conditioner for you.
Houses in Avalon usually sold for about $290,000 last year, and the HOA fee is about $84 a month.

## 13. The Farm at Carolina Forest: open land next to most houses
About two of every three houses at The Farm border land the HOA owns: ponds, woods and open space, about 280 acres of it.

The houses are on curving streets, with townhomes and condos in sections of their own. Houses listed here in recent years usually have about 1,900 square feet. A beach morning starts with a drive of about 12 minutes from the middle of the neighborhood.
Our guide to The Farm at Carolina Forest has its pools, its schools and its HOA rules.
Houses at The Farm usually sold for about $350,000 last year, and the HOA fee for a house is $107 a month.

Common questions

## Best neighborhoods in Myrtle Beach: FAQ

### Which Myrtle Beach neighborhoods are closest to the beach?
Cherry Grove is closest, with a public beach access about a tenth of a mile from the middle of the neighborhood. On the ocean side of Surfside Beach, the sand is about a nine-minute walk. The Market Common is about five minutes from the beach by car.

### Is Carolina Forest or Myrtle Beach better to live in?
The city of Myrtle Beach is better for being close to the beach, and Carolina Forest for big neighborhood pools and lakes. Plantation Lakes, Waterbridge, Avalon and The Farm, all in Carolina Forest, are 12 to 20 minutes from the beach by car.

### Which neighborhoods near Myrtle Beach have no HOA?
Most homes for sale on the ocean side of Surfside Beach, and more than half in Cherry Grove, are listed with no HOA fee. Most other neighborhoods on this page have an HOA fee of under $250 a month for a house.

### Are there 55+ communities near Myrtle Beach?
Yes. Del Webb North Myrtle Beach, Del Webb at Grande Dunes, Seasons at Prince Creek West and Myrtle Trace are 55+ communities, and our 55+ guide compares them.

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated October 22, 2026
Two of these gated communities sit on the ocean, and ten have golf.

The short answer

### North Myrtle Beach , 1 to 3

## 1. Tidewater Plantation: nine holes along Cherry Grove Inlet
Tidewater, in North Myrtle Beach, has one of the best public courses in South Carolina: Golf Digest ranks it No. 38 in the state. Nine of its holes play along the tidal inlet at Cherry Grove.

Photo: USDA Farm Service Agency, NAIP
Tidewater Plantation from above, with its golf holes along the inlet labelled. Houses line the street above the fairways.

The course opened in 1990. Golf Digest named it the best new public course in America that year. Golf Magazine put it first on its list of 1990's top 10 new public courses. About seven in ten of the house lots touch the course. Golf membership is sold to residents and property owners of Horry, Georgetown and Brunswick counties.
Tidewater is inside North Myrtle Beach's city limits, with city services. It is on the Intracoastal Waterway, not the ocean, but the neighborhood keeps its own beach cabana, with parking, at Cherry Grove Beach.
Tidewater has about 580 houses and one master association, with six smaller associations under it, so a house may answer to two associations. We check both for any home you like.
Homes at Tidewater usually sell for about $625,000. The HOA fee is about $230 a month.

## 2. Seaside Plantation: Main Street by golf cart
From the south end of Seaside Plantation, Main Street in North Myrtle Beach is about two-thirds of a mile by road. The way runs on two side streets, with no main highway to cross. The city lets a golf cart with a state permit use secondary roads posted at 35 mph or less, from sunrise to sunset.

Each spring and fall the Society of Stranders brings its shag dance festivals, the Spring Safari and the Fall Migration, to Main Street and Ocean Drive. The ocean is a quarter to three-quarters of a mile from the houses, and some houses look onto the neighborhood's lakes.
Festival weeks bring crowds to Main Street.
Homes here usually sell for about $720,000, with an HOA fee of about $210 a month.

## 3. Barefoot Resort: the course that hosts the Monday After the Masters
Dye Estates, a gated neighborhood inside Barefoot Resort in North Myrtle Beach, surrounds the Dye Course, home of the Monday After the Masters. Hootie & the Blowfish host the charity pro-am each spring, and it brings celebrities and PGA Tour players to the course. Many of its houses are large custom homes, on lots of about two-thirds of an acre.

Its gate is staffed. A guard works the main gate 24 hours a day, and owners drive through a resident lane with a barcode on the car. A guest gets in only when the owner has given the guard the guest's name and the date. At the second gate, an owner who has set up a gate code can let a guest in by phone. The guest calls from the keypad, and the owner presses 9.
Leatherleaf, the other gated neighborhood here, has 62 houses with the Love Course on every side. Davis Love III designed that course with Pinehurst No. 2 in mind, and Leatherleaf's Residents' Club has a lifestyle director who plans events.
In summer a free shuttle runs to the owners' beach cabana, which has key-fob parking, showers and a pet-washing station. In these two neighborhoods you call the driver 15 minutes ahead. At Barefoot a golf membership stays with certain houses. The seller gives it up at closing, and the buyer can take it over by enrolling within 60 days.
Most of Barefoot Resort has no gate. In Dye Estates no one may swim, boat or fish in the ponds. Lots there are still for sale with no deadline to build, so a house can go up next door at any time.
Leatherleaf homes usually sell for about $700,000 to $975,000, with an HOA fee of about $390 a month. Two Dye Estates homes resold this past year, for about $1.4 million and about $2.5 million.

### Myrtle Beach , 4 to 6

## 4. Grande Dunes: an oceanfront club and a marina for big boats
In Myrtle Beach, many Grande Dunes homes come with a household membership to the Ocean Club, a private club on the beach. It has towel and bar service at its pool and cabanas on the sand. We confirm it for each home you look at.

The private Members Club is a separate membership from the home. Its course was designed by Nick Price, a member of golf's Hall of Fame, with Craig Schreiner. The clubhouse has golf simulators, and the calendar includes themed dinners, wine tastings and a Fourth of July cookout.
Grande Dunes Marina, on the Intracoastal Waterway, has 126 slips and takes boats up to 120 feet long, with fuel and a store. A two-mile trail along the waterway is open to the public. In Calais, Palermo and Villa Venezia, most houses are one-story Mediterranean-style homes, and many have a private pool.
Grande Dunes has a security company on contract, with a main guard house, a north guard house and a guard house at the Ocean Club. This page covers three of its gated sections: Calais, Palermo and Villa Venezia.
Homes in those three sections usually sell for about $1.5 million, and the HOA fee is about $200 to $400 a month.

## 5. Waterway Palms Plantation: a Charleston-style plan around a lake
Waterway Palms Plantation, in Carolina Forest, was planned to echo Charleston's Battery district. At its center the association owns a lake parcel of about 15 acres. The clubhouse stands on a point in the lake, with water on three sides.

Most houses sold here lately were built since 2020, and they are large: many are custom homes of about 3,000 to 3,800 square feet. Many rise two or three stories, some have an elevator, and lots on the Intracoastal Waterway often have a private dock. The neighborhood also has its own boat ramp on the waterway, so a boat can go in without a trip across town.
The lots are small, and about one in five has no house on the county roll yet.
Homes usually sell for about $780,000, and the HOA fee is about $150 a month.

## 6. The Bluffs on the Waterway: a boathouse clubhouse on the waterway
The Bluffs on the Waterway, in Carolina Forest, has two clubhouses, and one of them is a boathouse on the Intracoastal Waterway. Its boat ramp sits on a waterfront lot of more than 6 acres. Grande Dunes Marina is about 2.5 miles away by water.

Many of its houses are custom Mediterranean-style homes in stucco. Black Creek runs through the woods along the west side, and the county's bike park is less than a mile away.
The Carolina Bays Parkway (S.C. 31) runs along one side; the nearest lots are about 280 feet from it.
Homes here usually sell for about $850,000; the HOA fee is about $150 a month.

### Socastee, Surfside Beach and Murrells Inlet , 7 to 12

## 7. Myrtle Beach Golf and Yacht Club: room for the boat and the camper
At Myrtle Beach Golf and Yacht Club, off Bay Road in Socastee, the association keeps storage for RVs, trailers and boats, for a fee when space is open. Enterprise Landing, a public boat ramp on the Intracoastal Waterway, is about a 4-minute drive from the entrance.

The owners' association owns about 62 acres of open land, most of it the wide strips of grass and woods between the streets. Its Community Watch desk is covered 24 hours a day, and the HOA fee is about $95 a month.
Despite the name, there is no golf or yacht club anymore; Heron Point, its golf club, closed years ago. Sandpiper Place, where D.R. Horton is building new houses, shares the entrance but has its own owners association. We look up the association for any home you like.
In the older part, homes usually sell for about $225,000.

## 8. Prestwick: a Pete and P.B. Dye course named Course of the Year
Prestwick, near Surfside Beach, has a course by Pete Dye and his son P.B. Dye that was named the 2025 Myrtle Beach Area Golf Course of the Year. It carries several of Dye's marks: wooden bulkheads along many water banks, deep-faced bunkers around greens that are often raised, and fast greens.

Photo: USDA Farm Service Agency, NAIP
Prestwick from above, with its Dye golf course labelled: houses among the fairways, with a long lake at the left and an RV lot at the lower right.

Prestwick opened in 1989 as a private club, founded by the Jackson family, who also created Ocean Lakes. The Gatlin Brothers once lived here and held a charity golf tournament each year, and about half the lots are on the course. When the club ended its memberships, the owners association took over the pools and the tennis center. Owners have two pools and two hard courts, and the eleven clay courts take their own membership.
The course is fully public now, so you share the fairways with visiting golfers.
Homes usually sell for about $480,000, and the HOA fee is about $190 a month.

## 9. Seasons at Prince Creek West (55+): a clubhouse, indoor and outdoor pools and bocce
At Seasons at Prince Creek West, in Murrells Inlet, the builder listed a ballroom, a card room, an art studio and a billiards room in the clubhouse.

Today the community has a clubhouse, indoor and outdoor pools, a fitness center, tennis and bocce. The Murrells Inlet MarshWalk is about a 10-minute drive.
Every occupied home must have a resident 55 or older . Most are one-story builder homes, about half of them 1,750 to 2,350 square feet. They sit on lots of about a fifth of an acre, so the yards are small. The county roll shows a house on every lot.
Homes usually sell for about $500,000, and the HOA fee, about $340 a month, includes internet, trash pickup and lawn care.

## 10. Bellwood Landing: big lots on Collins Creek, with TPC beyond the woods
In Bellwood Landing, in Murrells Inlet, about a dozen lots back onto Collins Creek, which runs through a wide band of woods. Beyond the woods lies TPC Myrtle Beach, a Tom Fazio design that has hosted the PGA Tour's Monday qualifier for the Myrtle Beach Classic.

The lots are big, many of them nearly half an acre, and seventeen are an acre or more. Many houses are custom, often two stories.
For tennis, pickleball or a cookout, owners drive about 4 minutes to the Park at Prince Creek West. It has courts and a covered pavilion with grills. The park is shared with the other Prince Creek West neighborhoods, not Bellwood's own.
Homes here usually sell for about $810,000, and the HOA fee is about $160 a month.

## 11. Wachesaw Plantation: a members' club on a bluff above the river
Before the neighborhoods were planned, archaeologists dug at Wachesaw, on the Waccamaw River in Murrells Inlet. Their University of South Carolina study of Wachesaw and the neighboring Richmond Hill plantation found more than half a million artifacts. Some finds are on display in the clubhouse.

The members own the Wachesaw Plantation Club. Its Tom Fazio course has hosted Carolinas Golf Association championships. Each March the members host the Can-Am Junior Team Matches.
From the best lots you look down a Fazio fairway or out over the Waccamaw River.
Kimbels, the club's restaurant, is on the bluff above the waterway and the 18th green, with a Tavern Room, open decks and an enclosed porch. Wachesaw's eight clay tennis courts and its book clubs and card groups fill the rest of the week. The main gate has a guard, and Wacca Wache Marina, outside the gates, has about 100 wet slips and indoor racks.
The club is rebuilding its pool and its Magnolia's restaurant, so part of the club is a work site for now.
Homes usually sell for about $700,000, and the HOA fee on most homes is about $150 a month.

## 12. Wachesaw East: where the LPGA played four years
Wachesaw East, in Murrells Inlet, has a course that hosted four televised LPGA Tour events, from 1997 to 2000. Karrie Webb won the first two.

Clyde Johnston laid out the course on a former rice plantation, past freshwater lakes and wetlands. Houses line the fairways behind the gate, most of them one story and from the early 2000s. The club's grill, the Toasted Tee Pub & Grub, has hosted happy hours with live music.
The course and its grill are a business of their own, not the homeowners': Festiva Real Estate Holdings bought them in 2017.
Homes usually sell for about $500,000, and the HOA fee is about $145 a month.

### Pawleys Island , 13 to 18

## 13. The Reserve: Greg Norman's private course and a marina with dry storage
Near Pawleys Island, The Reserve's marina sits at the southern tip of Sandy Island, where Thoroughfare Creek meets the Waccamaw River. Staff launch and haul boats from a dry storage building that holds about 200. The marina also has a fuel dock, and a boardwalk runs through a cypress forest to the river.

The Reserve Golf Club is a private Greg Norman course of up to 7,200 yards, set among 160 acres of wetlands. It has hosted the Carolinas Mid-Amateur twice, and a golf membership includes the club's dining and social events.
Each fall the Pawleys Island Festival of Music & Art puts up its tent at the golf club, and the neighborhood has private beach access with parking.
Dry storage takes boats up to 27 feet. A bigger boat needs a wet slip or a side tie.
Homes usually sell for about $1.3 million, and the HOA fee on most homes is about $320 a month.

## 14. Willbrook Plantation: a neighborhood on three rice plantations
Willbrook, near Pawleys Island, was built on the land of three rice plantations, Willbrook, Oatland and Turkey Hill, and its golf course crosses two of them. Five markers along the course tell that history hole by hole. Under the live oaks by the 5th hole are brick remains at the site of the plantation house, which burned in 1895 and was rebuilt that year.

Photo: USDA Farm Service Agency, NAIP
Willbrook Plantation from above: its houses are in the middle and at the upper right, beside golf fairways. The houses at the lower left are in Litchfield Plantation.

By the 8th hole is the Oatland cemetery of enslaved people, protected inside the community. After rice, the land was used for duck and quail hunting.
Willbrook is a gated neighborhood of about 250 houses inside Litchfield by the Sea, with its own clubhouse and social calendar. Its residents have Litchfield by the Sea's private beach and Beach Club, and one car barcode is issued for both. Golf membership is separate, and the club accepts applications from any golfer.
Homes usually sell for about $840,000, and the HOA fee is about $340 a month.

## 15. Litchfield Plantation: the owners own the plantation house
Near Pawleys Island, at the end of the Avenue of Live Oaks, stands Litchfield Plantation's house, and the owners own it. For about 50 years the developer controlled the association. In 2018 the owners took control after court challenges, and the house, its pool and about 7 acres passed to the association.

The house and its avenue of oaks appear on a map of the land drawn in 1794. After taking it over, the owners repaired it and set up a club room, and it has hosted weddings to help pay for its upkeep. A terrace off the main room overlooks the old rice fields.
The gatehouse stands on the avenue. The association also owns a beach house on Pawleys Island, about 4 miles away by road. A private marina on the river is an optional extra.
The old rice fields beside the community, about 330 acres, still belong to the original development company, not to the owners.
Houses here usually sell for about $800,000 to $1.8 million. The HOA fee on most homes is about $230 a month.

## 16. Litchfield by the Sea: a mile of beach and a guard around the clock
Litchfield by the Sea, near Pawleys Island, has about a mile of its own beach, with an oceanfront Beach Club, a deck and a pavilion.

Photo: USDA Farm Service Agency, NAIP
Litchfield by the Sea from above: homes around a lake, large buildings by the beach and the Atlantic Ocean at the right.

A guard works the main gate day and night. Owners' cars come in with a barcode, and each guest must be registered by the owner before the visit.
A normal week can include Tai Chi on Wednesday and yoga on Thursday at the Beach Club. In between there is crabbing off the docks on Osprey Lake and a walk on the paved paths through the marsh.
Many homes are condos and villas from the 1980s to the 2000s, and the Beach Club comes with the home. The association also lists single-family homes in Charlestowne Grant, Compass Point and River Club, and freestanding villas in Oystercatcher Island. Many of Charlestowne Grant's houses are raised beach houses.
It is many neighborhoods inside the gates, each with its own sub-association, and the HOA fee differs from section to section and from unit to unit. In the sections whose sales we read, condo and villa fees range from about $620 a month to about $1,880 for an oceanfront condo.
One-bedroom condos in Summerhouse usually sell for about $200,000, and four villas in Breakers Reef sold last year for about $1.5 million to $2.2 million.

## 17. Heritage Plantation: a dock master and a crow's nest over the river
Heritage Plantation, near Pawleys Island, has a marina with a full-time dock master. Its dock house is built over the Waccamaw River, with a crow's nest and a swing on its roof. The marina also has a deck over the water, bordered by cypress trees, that serves as a daily sunset gathering place.

The HOA fee includes cable TV, home internet, the dock master and 24-hour security, and the association lists a separate phone line for the main gate.
Many mornings are reserved for league play on four green-clay Har-Tru courts and four pickleball courts. The Heritage Club, a public par-71 course by Dan Maples, lies among the live oaks on land that was once the True Blue and Midway plantations.
A few lots look over the old rice fields toward the river.
Trash pickup costs extra, and boat slips are rented by the day, the month or the year.
Homes usually sell for about $710,000, and the HOA fee is about $325 a month.

## 18. DeBordieu Colony: a planters' colony with a Dye course and a private beach club
Before the Civil War, rice planters built a colony of summer homes at DeBordieu, on the ocean south of Pawleys Island. Later owners of the land included Isaac Emerson, the Bromo-Seltzer maker, and the Vanderbilt family. Locals say "Debidue".

Photo: U.S. Geological Survey
DeBordieu Colony from over the ocean in 2011: large houses behind the dunes, with walkways over the dunes to the beach, and the salt marsh beyond.

Only DeBordieu owners can join the DeBordieu Club. It has a Pete and P.B. Dye course that has hosted the Carolinas Mid-Amateur, and eight Har-Tru tennis courts. Its places to eat include the Beanery cafe and the Beach Club, with three dining spaces. On the Fourth of July the colony holds a parade.
Many houses are raised beach houses with an elevator, and some stand right on the ocean. Every car comes through one gate. Guests are registered online, in an app or by phone, and a guest pass lasts up to a week. The colony covers 2,700 acres, and at least 600 of them are a nature preserve.
South Carolina spends public money to rebuild a beach only where the public has full access to it, and DeBordieu does not qualify. Its owners pay for their beach themselves, through assessments to a beach fund they voted to set up. Boats cannot stay at the community dock overnight.
Homes here usually sell for about $2 million, and the HOA fee is about $300 to $400 a month.

## What are the pros and cons of a gated community?

### Pros

- Most of these neighborhoods are built around something you use: a golf course, a marina, a boat ramp or a beach club.

- Some HOA fees cover more than the gate, such as security, cable or internet.

- Some gates have a guard on duty day and night; others have a gatehouse or a watch desk.

### Cons

- Every guest, contractor and delivery has to get through the gate, so a party or a repair takes some planning.

- Only two of the 18 are on the ocean, so from most of them a beach day starts in the car.

- Owners pay for big projects through their association. Outside city limits in Horry County the HOA, not the county, maintains the private streets , and DeBordieu's owners pay assessments to rebuild their beach. Our agents check for special assessments before you make an offer.

Common questions

## Gated communities FAQ

### Does a gate make a neighborhood safer?
We do not rate any neighborhood as safe or unsafe. The price table shows which gates have a guard, a gatehouse, a keypad or a call box.

### How do guests get through the gate?
By a guard with a guest list, a call box at the gate, or a code from the owner. When you tour homes with us, we set up the visit with the gate before we go.

### Is there a gated community in Surfside Beach?
No, not inside the town. Prestwick, about a mile outside it, is the gated neighborhood on this page nearest Surfside Beach.

### Are there 55+ gated communities near Myrtle Beach?
Yes. Seasons at Prince Creek West in Murrells Inlet is the 55+ community on this page, and visitors use a call box at its main entrance.

### Are there gated golf communities near Myrtle Beach?
Yes. Most of the places on this page are golf communities, from Tidewater in North Myrtle Beach to DeBordieu Colony.

### Is Barefoot Resort a gated community?
Only in part. Barefoot Resort in North Myrtle Beach is mostly open, with a few gated neighborhoods inside it.

### Is Grande Dunes a gated community?
Only in part. Grande Dunes in Myrtle Beach is a large planned community, and only some of its sections have gates.

## Homes With No HOA Near Myrtle Beach: 16 Areas, Boats, Prices

Summary: The 16 areas around Myrtle Beach where all or most homes have no HOA fee, what each is like, the town rules for a boat or work truck, and what homes cost.

Buying a home

# Where can you buy a home with no HOA near Myrtle Beach? 16 areas where most homes have no fee.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated October 22, 2026
Room for a boat, a truck and a shed, from Little River to Aynor.

The short answer
Almost every house for sale outside a named subdivision is listed with no homeowners association (HOA) fee, and so are about three in four built before 1990. Most are in the areas below, from beach streets and river towns to country land.

## 1. Downtown Myrtle Beach: the boardwalk on foot
Listed with no HOA fee: nearly 9 in 10 homes for sale
From the older streets downtown, you can walk to the oceanfront boardwalk . From Collins Street it is about a quarter hour on foot. From the day after Labor Day through April, you can ride a bike or walk a dog on it at any hour.

Photo: Pubdog
The Pleasant Inn, a wood guest house from about 1927, under the live oaks on Broadway Street, in the old town by Withers Swash.

Most of these houses are within half a mile of the beach. All of them are outside the high-risk flood zones, where the federal rule makes a lender require flood insurance.
Plyler Park on the oceanfront has free live music and a fireworks show on Wednesdays in summer. The older houses are on Collins, Chester and Dunbar Streets, and Spivey Park and the New Town Bark Park are on Collins Street too.
A trail with a wooden boardwalk is beside Withers Swash, one of the city's oldest waterways , from Third Avenue South to Broadway and Collins Street.
Lots are modest, about 9,000 square feet in a typical case. Inside the city, a camper may not be kept in the front yard, so it has to fit beside or behind the house.
Houses with no HOA fee here are listed at about $435,000.

## 2. Myrtle Heights: a beach path at the end of each avenue
Listed with no HOA fee: every home for sale
In Myrtle Heights, the plan of the mid-1930s carried the avenues through to the beach, and those ends now give public access to the sand. From every house for sale here, a beach access is less than 5 minutes away on foot.

Photo: Pubdog
An older two-story house with columns on North Ocean Boulevard, in the Myrtle Heights-Oak Park Historic District.

The same plan set a minimum setback of 75 feet for oceanfront houses. The district is on the National Register of Historic Places , which calls the Myrtle Heights-Oak Park district the largest intact group of historic properties in Myrtle Beach.
The houses, built from about 1925 to 1945, are mostly two-story frame homes, many with a garage or a garage apartment. You will see porches and wood awnings painted solid or striped to look like canvas. A few houses keep old walls of coquina rock or brick.
Back yards along Ocean Boulevard often have native wax myrtles, the plant the city is named for, along with red cedars, palmettos and windswept oaks.
Sea Captain's House, a restaurant in a 1930 beach cottage, is about a 9-minute walk from the middle of Myrtle Heights.
On an oceanfront house, a change to the outside, including its color, needs the city's Community Appearance Board . Ordinary repair does not.
Houses with no HOA fee here are listed at about $1.6 million.

## 3. Pine Lakes' older streets: almost half an acre in the middle of the city
Listed with no HOA fee: every home for sale on the older streets
The older Pine Lakes streets have big lots in the middle of the city: typically almost half an acre, more than twice a downtown lot. There is room for a workshop or a boat beside the house.

The streets are around the golf course, which is less than half a mile from the ocean , on rolling land. The beach is about 0.6 mile on foot, at the Seaside Place street end, one of the city's fully accessible beach paths.
Ocean Forest Memorial Park , with a walking path, is at the Haskell Circle beach access, about half a mile on foot. North Ocean Boulevard has bike lanes.
A resident whose car is registered and taxed in the city gets a free parking decal. With it, you park free at city meters, at beach street ends and at Pelicans baseball games .
The city picks up trash, recycling and yard waste at the curb each week, for about $34 a month.
The Preserve at Pine Lakes, the newer section, has an HOA fee and is not counted here.
You pay for the room: houses here are listed at more than twice the downtown price, for more than twice the land.
Houses with no HOA fee here are listed at about $930,000.

## 4. Windy Hill: free day docks at Barefoot Landing
Listed with no HOA fee: 6 in 10 homes for sale
Windy Hill is 3 minutes by car from Barefoot Landing on the Intracoastal Waterway. Come by boat, and you can use the finger docks free for the day while you shop or eat.

The Alabama Theatre and House of Blues are on the same grounds. Barefoot Landing welcomes leashed pets all year, and many of its shops let them inside.
Most houses for sale here are within a 10-minute walk of a public beach access. Inside North Myrtle Beach, a work truck up to 18,500 pounds may park at home.
On 41st Avenue South, a pocket park with garden plantings, two pergolas and a walking path is on the site of the old water tower. Conway investors developed Windy Hill after World War II, and in 1968 it joined Cherry Grove, Ocean Drive and Crescent Beach to form North Myrtle Beach.
Flood is the cost here. About half of these houses are in a high-risk flood zone, and with a mortgage your lender will almost always require flood insurance.
Houses with no HOA fee here are listed at about $745,000.

## 5. Crescent Beach: half a mile on foot to a beach access
Listed with no HOA fee: nearly 9 in 10 homes for sale
Most houses for sale in Crescent Beach are less than half a mile on foot from a public beach access. From 6th to 27th Avenue South, the beach is one of the city's three surf zones . From mid-May to mid-September, boards are banned from 9 to 4 on the rest of the beach, but you can surf here.

Photo: U.S. Geological Survey
Crescent Beach from over the ocean in 2011: streets of beach houses behind the oceanfront.

Ingram Dunes Nature Preserve , on Hillside Drive, is the city's last remaining maritime forest. It has native dunes 30 feet tall and an interpretive half-mile nature trail.
Most are older beach houses, on streets such as Hillside Drive, Holly Drive, Perrin Drive and Strand Avenue. Few of them need flood insurance for a mortgage. In Cherry Grove, almost every home does.
In the middle of Crescent Beach, the 18th and Edge pocket park has benches and a fountain. Central Park , 20 acres with lighted tennis courts, pickleball courts and a paved walking path, is about 0.7 mile away.
City beach lots charge for parking from March through October. Residents register their plates each year for free passes.
Lots are small, about 7,600 square feet. Under the city's rule, a trailer or camper goes behind the front of the house or under a carport. That takes a carport, or room beside or behind the house.
Houses with no HOA fee here are listed at about $755,000.

## 6. Ocean Drive: Main Street and the shag
Listed with no HOA fee: more than half the homes for sale
On Main Street in Ocean Drive, you can learn the shag free on Tuesday nights. Fat Harold's Beach Club calls itself the Home of the Shag and teaches the dance.

In the Ocean Drive and Crescent Beach area, a pavilion and amusement park drew crowds who danced the shag.
A Saturday here can start with breakfast at Hoskins Restaurant on Main Street, which opened in 1948.
The North Myrtle Beach Area Historical Museum is free, and its exhibits include beach music artists and shag dancing. McLean Park , a quarter mile from Hoskins on foot, has a two-acre lake and a half-mile paved walking path.
Each summer, the city holds free Music on Main concerts on Thursdays at the Horseshoe. Each December, a nighttime Christmas parade comes up Main Street. Few of the houses for sale here with no fee need flood insurance for a mortgage.
Crowds come with it: on concert nights Main Street closes to cars in the afternoon, and the St. Patrick's festival draws about 40,000 people.
Houses with no HOA fee here are listed at about $665,000.

## 7. Cherry Grove: a boat on the canals
Listed with no HOA fee: more than half the homes for sale
Cherry Grove's canals were created as early as the 1950s. The city has dredged canals there twice since 2016 , to give owners boat access to House Creek and the Intracoastal Waterway at high and low tide.

Photo: U.S. Geological Survey
Cherry Grove from over the ocean in 2011: houses on the canals, many with their own docks, and the marsh behind.

The city's boat ramp at 53rd Avenue North reaches both the marsh and the open ocean through Hog Inlet. It has a two-lane boat launch, a kayak launch, a fishing pier, a floating boat dock and a fish cleaning station.
North Myrtle Beach residents park free at the ramp when they register with the city. It is also the way in to Heritage Shores Nature Preserve, an island in the marsh reached on elevated boardwalks.
Many of the canal houses have their own docks, so the boat stays behind the house. Across Hog Inlet, Waties Island has almost three miles of undeveloped beach.
Each July 4, the city's free fireworks go up at the Cherry Grove Pier. The homes here with an HOA fee are all in named subdivisions.
Two costs come with the canals: flood insurance and a dredging fee. Almost every home here is in a high-risk flood zone. Owners of about 415 properties in the canal district pay the city about $1,700 a year for the dredging, on the county tax bill.
Houses with no HOA fee here are listed at about $850,000.

## 8. Little River: the old fishing village on the waterway
Listed with no HOA fee: every home for sale
The houses on Little River's old waterfront streets are less than a mile from the docks on Mineola Avenue, on the Intracoastal Waterway. Local boatmen began taking visitors fishing for a fee there, probably in the early 1920s. They ran the first organized offshore fishing trips for visitors in South Carolina.

U.S. government aerial photo
The old Little River waterfront from the air: streets of houses beside the salt marsh and the Intracoastal Waterway.

Hurricane Juel's , with a view of the waterway, has been family owned since 1945.
The waterfront holds the Blue Crab Festival each May, on the weekend after Mother's Day; a TV station reported more than 30,000 people there in 2026. ShrimpFest follows each October. On the Saturday after Thanksgiving, a lighted boat parade leaves Little River Inlet and heads down the waterway.
The county's T. Craig Campbell boat landing is on the waterway in town. After the inlet's jetties were finished in 1983, boats could cross the bar at any time of day. The state keeps an artificial fishing reef off the inlet.
Vereen Memorial Historical Gardens , a county park on the waterway, has about 3 miles of trails and boardwalks through its gardens and along the water. Some of the houses for sale are new, on Mineola and Ellis Avenues; others are on McCorsley Avenue and Bayshore Drive.
The beach takes a drive: none of these houses is within a mile of the ocean.
Houses with no HOA fee here are listed at about $420,000.

## 9. Socastee: a county boat ramp 2 minutes away
Listed with no HOA fee: most homes for sale
Rosewood Landing , a county boat ramp on the Intracoastal Waterway, is 2 minutes by car from these streets. Socastee Landing and Park has a second ramp and a new accessible playground. The swing bridge at Socastee, finished in 1935, marked the completion of the Intracoastal Waterway in South Carolina. The waterway's opening celebration was held in Socastee in April 1936.

These streets are outside any town, so the county's rules apply. County zoning names no limit on where you park a boat. Outdoor storage may not be in front of the house, and a small shed can go 5 feet from the line.
Most are 1980s houses in Rosewood Estates and Cimerron Plantation.
Socastee Recreation Park has fields, picnic areas, disc golf, trails and a playground. Market Common and Coastal Grand Mall are each about 10 minutes away, and the beach at Surfside is about 15 minutes by car.
Flood insurance is the extra cost to plan for: about a third of these houses need it if you buy with a mortgage.
Houses with no HOA fee here are listed at about $250,000, the lowest on this page.

## 10. Surfside Beach: two boats at home and golf carts on the streets
Listed with no HOA fee: nearly 9 in 10 homes for sale
In Surfside Beach, the town allows up to two boats or trailers at a home, and only one over 21 feet. A permitted golf cart may be driven in daylight within four miles of home, on streets posted at 35 miles an hour or less.

The town has live oaks well over a century old and 36 public beach accesses . In 2016 Surfside Beach became the first town certified autism-friendly through the Champion Autism Network.
The town holds a farmers market on Tuesdays from spring into December in Memorial Park, and free Sunday afternoon concerts there from late May through August. Each July 4, a golf cart parade goes down Ocean Boulevard.
Each October, the fall festival has more than 100 craft vendors. Fireworks may be set off on the sand from sunset on July 4 and on New Year's Eve, but not within 500 feet of the pier.
The town picks up trash at the curb, and it has more than nine miles of sidewalk.
One cost to know on the ocean side: about 1 in 4 homes there needs flood insurance if you buy with a mortgage.
Houses with no HOA fee here are listed at about $940,000.

## 11. Garden City Beach: a free pier walk and free beach parking
Listed with no HOA fee: most homes for sale
The Pier at Garden City is always free to walk, and every oceanfront beach access in Garden City has free parking all year . On summer nights, live bands play at both ends of the pier.

Photo: U.S. Geological Survey
Garden City Beach from over the ocean in 2011: rows of houses between the beach and the marsh, with docks on the creeks behind.

A pier pass covers fishing, so you need no state license. Its Hugo burger is named for the 1989 hurricane that destroyed the pier.
Most of the houses for sale here are within half a mile of the shore. The county's Stanley Drive landing is a 5-minute drive.
Each July 4, decorated boats start at the point of Garden City Beach and parade through Murrells Inlet.
Budget for flood insurance: with a mortgage, a lender will almost always require it on most of these houses.
Houses with no HOA fee here are listed at about $1.4 million.

## 12. Murrells Inlet's north end: by the creeks and the county boat ramp
Listed with no HOA fee: almost all homes for sale
At the north end of Murrells Inlet, some of the houses for sale are on the creeks of the inlet, and the rest are a few streets back. The county's boat landing on Stanley Drive is a 4-minute drive, and several houses on the market lately have their own floating dock.

People first came to the inlet for oyster roasts and fried shore dinners, and seafood restaurants followed. The MarshWalk , a half-mile wooden boardwalk along the salt marsh with a row of restaurants, is about 6 minutes away by car. The writer Mickey Spillane made Murrells Inlet his home for decades.
The free pier walk and free beach parking at Garden City Beach are a 6-minute drive across the marsh. Brookgreen Gardens , with its sculpture gardens on four former rice plantations, is about 15 minutes away by car.
Murrells Inlet is not a town, so the county's rules apply on most of these streets. The south part is in Georgetown County. There, a vehicle or travel trailer without current plates has to be kept in a closed building.
Flood is the honest cost: more than half of these houses are in a high-risk flood zone.
Houses with no HOA fee here are listed at about $820,000.

## 13. Conway: live oaks and the Waccamaw River
Listed with no HOA fee: nearly 9 in 10 homes for sale
Conway's older streets were designed around its live oaks , on a bluff of the Waccamaw River. The Riverwalk follows the river downtown, and the Waccamaw is a federal National Water Trail .

Photo: Pubdog
The Riverwalk in downtown Conway, on the Waccamaw River.

In town, lots are about 15,000 square feet. Inside the city, a camper or a trailer can go in the side or back yard or under a carport. A shed goes in back, with a permit.
The oldest streets form a National Register district . Its houses range from Greek Revival and Carpenter Gothic through Queen Anne to 1920s bungalows, one of them with a porch around three sides. City Hall is the old Horry County courthouse, finished in 1825 to a design credited to Robert Mills. Its courtroom still holds city court every week.
Photo: Pubdog
An older house behind a big oak in Conway's residential historic district.

The Horry County Museum is in the restored 1905 Burroughs School, about a quarter hour on foot from downtown. Riverfest brings music and fireworks to the river on the Saturday before the Fourth of July weekend, and the Celebration of Lights opens each December.
Billy Witherspoon Landing , a county ramp on the Waccamaw, is a 6-minute drive. Conway Medical Center is a 12-minute drive.
The beach is a 25-minute drive.
Houses with no HOA fee here are listed at about $285,000.

## 14. Loris: a small town with its own hospital
Listed with no HOA fee: almost all homes for sale
Loris is a small town with its own hospital: McLeod Loris, with an emergency room, is in town. The older houses were built from the 1940s to the 1970s, on lots of about 0.4 acre. By 1914 Loris was known as the Gate City, because it was the first town on the railroad south of the North Carolina line.

Photo: Pithon314
Main Street in downtown Loris.

City zoning allows up to two buildings beside the house, a garage or carport included, so there is room for a workshop. A work truck up to 2 tons may park at home.
The Main Street library lends cake pans, state park passes and Wi-Fi hotspots.
On the third Saturday in October, the city holds the Loris Bog-Off downtown, with vendors, a car show and live music. The festival's dish is chicken bog: chicken, rice and sausage.
You drive more from here: the beach is about 35 minutes by car.
Houses with no HOA fee here are listed at about $320,000.

## 15. The country around Loris: new houses on large lots
Listed with no HOA fee: most homes for sale
Around Loris, most houses for sale are new, built in 2024 or later, outside any town limits. Many of the new houses are on lots of about 0.7 acre, with room for a camper, a trailer and a shop under the county's rules.

The Waccamaw River Heritage Preserve protects 28 miles of the Waccamaw River, with riverside camping on its land.
For a work truck, the county lets a business run from home keep three service vehicles on a farm-zoned lot under an acre and a half. McLeod Loris hospital is about 9 minutes away by car.
Outside the towns, a small shed can go 5 feet from the line, and fences can be 8 feet tall. The Solid Waste Authority provides no curbside trash pickup there, so you hire a hauler or use a county drop-off center.
Houses with no HOA fee here are listed at about $415,000.

## 16. Aynor: an acre and a river landing
Listed with no HOA fee: most homes for sale
Around Aynor, lots are typically about an acre, with room beside the house for a boat or a camper. More than half of the houses for sale here are new.

U.S. government aerial photo
Houses on lots of about an acre along a country road outside Aynor, from the air. The orange line is one lot.

Galivants Ferry Landing, a county ramp on the Little Pee Dee River , is about 6 minutes from the center of town. The Little Pee Dee is popular with canoes, kayaks and small powerboats .
At Galivants Ferry , the old farm houses have full-width front porches on brick piers. Some were built from wood cut on the farm itself, and the district has log tobacco barns. Galivants Ferry has also held a political speaking, the Stump, since 1880.
Each September, almost 25,000 people come to the Aynor Harvest Hoe-Down, a festival the Pilot Club of Aynor started. In the town of Aynor, zoning does not limit a camper or a work truck at home. Most of these houses are outside the town, under county rules.
You will drive more: about 45 minutes to the beach, and about 30 to the nearest hospital, Conway Medical Center.
Houses with no HOA fee here are listed at about $370,000.

## What can you do at home with no HOA?
With no HOA, the limits on parking, rentals and buildings on your lot are the town's, or the county's outside the towns, along with any deed restriction. Most of the homes with no HOA fee around Conway, Loris and Aynor are outside the town limits, under the county's rules.

Before you make an offer, we check the town or county rules for that lot, the deed for restrictions and the county records for an HOA.
In Myrtle Beach , North Myrtle Beach and Surfside Beach , renting out a home needs a business license. In the towns, you can leave a boat in the driveway for a day to load and unload. On county roads, the county bans parking only where it posts a sign.
Example: Teresa wants a home with no HOA and room for her 20-foot boat. She likes a house on a small lot with a Myrtle Beach address.
Her Chapter3 agent finds the house on the county map, inside the city of Myrtle Beach. The city's front-yard rule applies to her boat, and that lot has no other room for it.
The agent shows her houses outside the city limits, under the county's rules. Teresa makes an offer on one with a wide side yard.

- About 60 houses for sale under $250,000, most of them built before 1990 and about half in and around Conway.

- About 130 from $500,000 to $750,000, a third of them within half a mile of the beach.

- About 220 at $750,000 and up, about 2 in 3 of them within half a mile of the beach.

## What do you give up with no HOA?
No HOA means no shared pool, clubhouse or gate, and no HOA rules for your neighbors' houses either. A home with no HOA can still have deed restrictions on what you build or keep there.
If you want a pool, a clubhouse or a gate, you pay an HOA fee for them. Our guides to the best neighborhoods for what you want nearby and to gated communities around Myrtle Beach show where to look. Our guide to The Farm at Carolina Forest shows one Carolina Forest neighborhood, and our guide to what HOA fees cover explains each part of a fee.

Common questions

## Homes with no HOA FAQ

### Can I park a boat at my house in Myrtle Beach?
Yes, on your own lot, within the rule of the town it is in; the table under What can you do at home gives each one.

### Which areas near Myrtle Beach almost always have an HOA?
Carolina Forest, the Grande Dunes, the Market Common and Burgess: almost every home for sale there has an HOA fee. Almost all homes for sale in Little River's named subdivisions have an HOA fee too. Longs and the country around Conway look rural, but most homes for sale there have an HOA fee too.

### Are there homes with no HOA in Murrells Inlet?
Yes, but only a little more than 1 in 4 homes for sale with a Murrells Inlet address is listed with no HOA fee. At the north end of the inlet, by the creeks and the Stanley Drive landing, almost every house for sale has none.

### Are there homes with no HOA in North Myrtle Beach?
Yes. More than half of the homes for sale with a North Myrtle Beach address are listed with no HOA fee. Almost all of them are in Cherry Grove, Crescent Beach, Windy Hill and Ocean Drive.

### What is a typical HOA fee in Myrtle Beach?
About $95 a month on a house. A condo fee is much higher because it includes the building's insurance, water and sewer, trash and a pool.

### Can you buy a condo with no HOA fee in Myrtle Beach?
Almost never. Of about 2,700 condos for sale around Myrtle Beach, only one was listed with no HOA fee. South Carolina law makes condo owners share the cost of the building.

### Does a listing with no HOA fee mean the home has no HOA?
Not always. A blank fee means no fee was listed. We check the deed and the county records for an HOA before you make an offer.

### Is a campground home with no HOA fee a no-HOA home?
No. A campground home has no HOA fee, but it sits on leased land, and you pay a yearly lease for the land under it.

Buying on a budget

# Where are the most affordable places to buy a home near Myrtle Beach? Twelve neighborhoods, and the best thing about each.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated October 22, 2026
Affordable places near Myrtle Beach, with what the price buys in each: the house, the land and the drive.

The short answer
Within about 20 minutes of a beach, these twelve neighborhoods near Myrtle Beach had the lowest prices last year. Homes in them usually sold for about $190,000 to $255,000, against about $420,000 for a Myrtle Beach home that is not a condo. Four of the twelve are neighborhoods of houses; the rest are townhomes.

## What does each neighborhood do best?
About half the price of a Myrtle Beach home Place, best feature Usually sold for

2. Fairways at Wild Wing · golf, lawn care $215,000
3. Sawgrass East · garage, lawn care $225,000
4. Birchwood · paddle the Waccamaw $225,000
5. Golf and Yacht Club · gated, one story $225,000

10. Indigo Grove · 22 acres open space $245,000
11. Wynbrooke · MarshWalk 5 min away $250,000
12. Polo Farms · fenced yards, $20 fee $255,000

Tap a name to read about it.

## 1. Parkview: townhomes by the city's golf course, near the beach
Parkview is a four-minute drive from the beach. Its townhomes are off 17th Avenue South, inside the city of Myrtle Beach, around ponds and a pool for owners.
Built in the mid-2000s, the townhomes have about 1,050 to 1,350 square feet and two or three bedrooms. Many have vaulted ceilings and a front porch, and some have a screened porch.

Photo: USDA Farm Service Agency, NAIP
Parkview, beside 17th Avenue South, with Whispering Pines Golf Course, from above.

Whispering Pines, the city's own 18-hole golf course , is less than a quarter mile from Parkview. It was originally part of the Myrtle Beach Air Force Base, and its tee markers feature the squadron emblems. Residents of Horry, Georgetown and Brunswick counties play a round there for $45 plus tax, with a cart.
There are about 200 townhomes here, and the HOA fee includes water, sewer, grounds care and the pool. For dinner and a movie, The Market Common has shops, restaurants and a theater.
Few of these townhomes come up for sale in a year, so one of our agents watches for each new listing.
Townhomes here usually sold for about $190,000 last year, with an HOA fee of about $325 a month.

## 2. The Fairways at Wild Wing: townhomes in a golf community
Fairways townhomes usually have two stories and three or four bedrooms. Most have their own garage, some with room for two cars, and some put the main bedroom downstairs.

They are inside Wild Wing Plantation, a golf club, and some are near the course. The HOA fee usually includes the lawn care, the pool and the internet, so a Saturday can go to golf instead of yard work.
The Fairways is inside Conway's city limits, where the yearly tax is higher than outside a town.
Fairways townhomes usually sold for about $215,000 last year, and the HOA fee is about $390 a month.

## 3. Sawgrass East: townhomes where the fee covers the insurance and the lawn
At Sawgrass East, the HOA fee usually pays the insurance on the buildings, the lawn care, and the water, sewer and trash. In most townhomes here, an owner has no water or trash bill of their own, and the HOA cares for the lawns.

Many of the townhomes have three bedrooms, often with a one-car garage and the main bedroom downstairs.
There are about 255 of them, built in the mid-2000s, around three small lakes that the HOA owns, with a pool and a clubhouse for owners. The county's Carolina Forest library and recreation center are on the boulevard that leads in.
The beach is about ten miles away by road, so a beach day means a drive.
Sawgrass East townhomes usually sold for about $225,000 last year, and the HOA fee is about $425 a month.

## 4. Birchwood: a new house on a quarter acre
Birchwood is small: 77 lots, with new Lennar houses on lots of about a quarter acre and about 12 acres of open space. A quarter acre gives a new house a real backyard at this price.

Chris Anderson Landing, a county boat ramp on the Waccamaw River, is about 7 minutes from Birchwood by car. From there you can paddle the state's Waccamaw River trail downriver through bald cypress woods, about 20 miles to Red Bluff Landing.
FEMA maps every lot in Birchwood as an area of minimal flood hazard. High-speed internet is included in the monthly dues.
A new house here sells for about what a 1980s house does in the Golf and Yacht Club, closer to Myrtle Beach. Birchwood is off SC 905, southwest of Longs, and North Myrtle Beach and its beaches are about 20 minutes by car.
The long drive is to Myrtle Beach: Coastal Grand Mall is about a forty-minute drive, by the Carolina Bays Parkway.
New houses in Birchwood usually sold for about $225,000 last year; the HOA fee is about $120 a month.

## 5. Myrtle Beach Golf and Yacht Club: one-story houses behind a gate
The older part of Myrtle Beach Golf and Yacht Club has about 470 houses inside a gate, most of them one story. For a boat, Osprey Marina has wet slips and dry boat storage on the Intracoastal Waterway, about four miles away by road.

Most houses there were built in the 1980s, with two or three bedrooms and two baths. They typically have about 1,200 square feet, on about an eighth of an acre, and many have a porch or a patio.
Owners share a pool and hot tub, tennis courts and a community center.
Age matters here. Insurers may require an older home to have an updated roof, wiring, plumbing and heating, so we have the home inspector look at each before you buy.
Houses in the older part usually sold for about $225,000 last year, and the HOA fee is about $95 a month.

## 6. Forestbrook Village: new townhome plans up to 2,400 square feet
At Forestbrook Village, Lennar has four townhome plans, from about 1,450 up to 2,400 square feet. Lennar is still building here, so some of these townhomes are brand new.

The townhomes are off Forestbrook Road, south of US 501, beside the older Forestbrook neighborhood. Owners have a pool and a playground, and internet and grounds care are included.
Near Forestbrook Village, Arrowhead Country Club has 27 holes of golf along the Intracoastal Waterway. Water comes into play on 24 of them.
Some lots here are in a high-risk flood zone, where a lender usually requires flood insurance, so the lot can matter as much as the plan.
Lennar's townhomes here usually sold for about $230,000 last year, with an HOA fee of about $170 a month.

## 7. Victory Point: new townhomes on part of the old speedway
Victory Point is built on part of the old Myrtle Beach Speedway. The track opened in 1958 as RAMBI Raceway, and cars ran their last laps there in 2020 . Several streets have racing names: Speedway Street, Talladega Drive and Pit Crew Drive.

Photo: USDA Farm Service Agency, NAIP
The old Myrtle Beach Speedway beside US 501, before Victory Point was built on part of its land.

The townhomes are new, three-bedroom and about 1,450 square feet. Lennar built them off US 501, by Tanger Outlets, with a pool, a playground, a picnic area and a pond.
Lennar lists Victory Point as sold out for now, so we watch for resales.
Expect more building. Another owner plans 194 townhomes for rent on about 20 acres of the old speedway land beside it.
Townhomes in Victory Point usually sold for about $235,000 last year, and the HOA fee is about $235 a month.

## 8. The Townes at Amber Bluff: smart-home townhomes about 6 minutes from the football stadium
Every townhome at Amber Bluff came with a smart-home package: you can control the front door lock, the thermostat and the video doorbell from your phone.
Off Savannah Bluff Road, D.R. Horton builds one plan , the Pearson. It has two stories and a one-car garage, in about 1,420 square feet.
On game days, Brooks Stadium, where the Chanticleers play football, is about a six-minute drive. Coastal Carolina University and Horry-Georgetown Technical College are about as close, for a class or a job.
Downtown Conway, with its shops on Main Street and its riverwalk on the Waccamaw River, is about a seven-minute drive.

Photo: Pubdog
Main Street in downtown Conway, the downtown closest to Amber Bluff.

Each owner will also pay a yearly insurance assessment that is not yet set. We find out what it will be for any home you like.
These townhomes usually sold for about $240,000 last year, with an HOA fee of about $100 a month.

## 9. Villas at Sandridge: townhomes five minutes from a cable wake park
At Shark Wake Park, a five-minute drive from Villas at Sandridge, a cable pulls wakeboard riders across the water. It is inside the North Myrtle Beach Park and Sports Complex , which also has walking trails, two dog parks and an accessible playground.

Villas at Sandridge is a small community of 79 townhomes off SC 90 near Little River, with about 8 acres of shared open space. Dream Finders Homes built them with two stories and a one-car garage, and some plans have the main bedroom on the first floor.
The city's new section of the park has added soccer and baseball fields, ponds, trails and two more playgrounds. The nearest beach is a seven-minute trip by car.
Expect higher dues here than at the other new communities on this list.
These townhomes usually sold for about $245,000 last year, and the dues are about $300 a month.

## 10. Indigo Grove: new houses on open land, 13 minutes from the beach
Most of Indigo Grove's new houses back onto about 22 acres of open space that the HOA owns. The beach is about 13 minutes away by car.

The open land holds three new ponds, one with a small island of trees, and strips of woods along a creek. The neighborhood is off SC 90, and its homes are zoned for Riverside Elementary and North Myrtle Beach Middle and High.
Most of the houses are Lennar's, which sells them as The Overlook. Lennar lists nine floor plans with three to five bedrooms, some of them one story, on lots of about a fifth of an acre.
Every lot is outside the high-risk flood zone, so a lender usually will not require flood insurance on a home here.
New houses here usually sold for about $245,000 last year, with an HOA fee of about $80 a month.

## 11. Wynbrooke: townhomes five minutes from the Murrells Inlet MarshWalk
At the Murrells Inlet MarshWalk , five minutes from Wynbrooke, the restaurants on the marsh have live music every night, and there is never a cover charge.

Huntington Beach State Park , with three miles of beach, is 10 minutes away.
The townhomes, built in the early 2000s, are off SC 707, around ponds, and some back onto the water. Many have a screened porch and a loft.
Wynbrooke's HOA fee is the highest of the twelve, though it usually pays for the insurance on the buildings and for the grounds care.
Townhomes in Wynbrooke usually sold for about $250,000 last year, with an HOA fee of about $450 a month.

## 12. Polo Farms: one-story houses with fenced yards
Many backyards in Polo Farms are fenced, and several have their own pool. That is room for a dog to run and a swim at home, in a house of your own for about the price of a townhome in Wynbrooke.
Most of the houses are one story, with three bedrooms, on lots of about a fifth of an acre. They are off SC 905, west of Longs, and were built in three phases, from the mid-2000s on.

Photo: USDA Farm Service Agency, NAIP
Polo Farms off SC 905, with Simpson Creek along its southwest side.

Flood is a concern here. After Hurricane Florence in 2018, the Waccamaw River rose to historic heights; floodwater filled the streets and gutted homes across the neighborhood. More than four in ten of its lots are in a high-risk flood zone. Before you make an offer, we look up the lot on FEMA's flood map.
Houses in Polo Farms usually sold for about $255,000 last year, and the HOA fee is about $20 a month.

## How much property tax will you pay?
Take a $240,000 home that is your main home. Its yearly tax depends on where it is:

- Outside a town, or in Myrtle Beach: about $970.

- In Polo Farms: about $980. In Wynbrooke: about $1,030.

- Inside Conway : about $1,570.

When you buy, the county values the home at about what it is worth that year, and the new value shows up on the next year's bill. These figures use the county's lower rate for a home you live in, which our property tax guide explains.

## What help can you get with a down payment?
SC Housing, the state's housing agency, gives buyers in Horry and Georgetown counties $10,000 toward the down payment and closing costs. It is forgivable: you do not pay it back if you stay in the home long enough. The program is called the Homebuyer Program .
You do not have to be a first-time buyer. The program has these limits:

- You must not own a home when you close.

- Household income must be under about $115,000 for one or two people, and under about $134,000 for three or more.

- The home price can be up to $450,000.

You apply through a lender that works with SC Housing. Our page on down-payment help programs explains the Homebuyer Program step by step, including the credit score it needs.
Example: Dana rents an apartment in Myrtle Beach and wants a house of her own in Conway. She thinks she must save for years before she can buy.
Her Chapter3 agent shows her SC Housing's Homebuyer Program, which helps buyers here pay the down payment. The agent puts her in touch with a lender that works with the program.
Dana takes the homebuyer class and starts looking at houses, instead of saving for years first.

Condo buyer mistakes

## 3 mistakes condo buyers make on the Grand Strand.

01

Mistake

### Ignoring HOA financials on condos

Myrtle Beach condo HOAs vary wildly. Some have $400/month fees with funded reserves. Others have $600/month fees with a pending $15,000 special assessment you inherit at closing.

The fix

Request the HOA financial statements, reserve study, and meeting minutes going back 24 months before making any offer on a condo.

02

Mistake

### Assuming any condo can be Airbnb'd

Not every condo allows short-term rentals. Many HOAs prohibit rentals under 30 days. Buying an "investment condo" without checking STR rules is one of the most expensive mistakes we see. Litigation matters too: see when you can buy a condo in litigation .

The fix

Verify STR eligibility in the HOA bylaws before writing the contract, not during due diligence. We check this upfront on every investment inquiry.

03

Mistake

### Buying without a local lender pre-approval

Out-of-state online lenders often don't understand condotel financing restrictions, SC attorney closings, or DSCR loan requirements. A DSCR loan qualifies on the property's rent, not your tax returns. Deals fall apart at the finish line because of lender issues, not property issues.

The fix

Chapter3 is affiliated with BrickWood Mortgage (NMLS #189497), a Grand Strand lender that has been providing mortgages locally for over 18 years and knows every building, every HOA warrantability issue, and every financing quirk in this market.

Appreciation

## Why Grand Strand homes keep appreciating.

Typical home value, Myrtle Beach metro

Estimated typical home values for the Myrtle Beach metro, drawn from the Federal Housing Finance Agency home price index and scaled to today's typical value near $310,000. Values dipped after 2008, drifted through the 2010s, then climbed steeply from 2021. The typical home has more than doubled since its 2012 to 2013 low. The dotted line projects values to 2030 if the long-run appreciation rate continues. It is an estimate, not a guarantee. Hover any year for its value.

Source: FHFA All-Transactions House Price Index for the Myrtle Beach metro (public data), indexed to current market value. A typical, blended figure. Single-family homes, condos, and individual neighborhoods each vary.

+131% since the 2012 low
+85% since 2019

Five forces push in the same direction, and they are structural rather than seasonal:

In-migration. Myrtle Beach is the second fastest-growing metro area in the country (U.S. Census Bureau, latest estimates), and North Carolina is the top source of buyers.

Constrained supply. Coastal land is finite and building has not kept pace with arrivals. More buyers than homes pushes prices up.

Affordability. Named the 4th most affordable beach town in America by House Beautiful, so out-of-state buyers arriving with home-sale equity stretch further here and keep demand high.

Unique SC tax breaks. South Carolina does not tax Social Security income, taxes a primary home at a 4% assessment ratio, fully exempts 100% disabled veterans from property tax on their home, and gives owners 65 and older a Homestead exemption on the first $50,000 of value (SC Department of Revenue).

Rental income. A year-round tourism economy lets many homes earn short-term-rental income, adding investor demand on top of buyers.
