Certifications and awards

## What the hospitals hold, from the bodies that award it
We do not grade hospitals. The awarding bodies publish who holds what, and that record speaks for the system here.
Grand Strand Medical Center is an adult Level I trauma center and a pediatric Level II trauma center, with heart surgery on site. Healthgrades placed it among America's 250 Best Hospitals in 2023 and 2024, and among America's 100 Best for stroke care and for critical care in 2023, 2024 and 2025. It also holds the American Heart Association and American Stroke Association Get With The Guidelines Stroke Gold Plus award.
Tidelands Waccamaw and Tidelands Georgetown are both certified by the Joint Commission as advanced primary stroke centers. Waccamaw is a designated baby-friendly hospital and an adult Level IV trauma center, and Tidelands Health is an affiliate of MUSC Health.
Conway Medical Center runs an accredited family medicine residency program sponsored by Campbell University, which means new doctors do part of their training here, and it has been an independent, locally governed non-profit since 1928.

Veterans

## The VA clinic here is outpatient
The Myrtle Beach VA Clinic at 1800 Airpark Drive is a community-based outpatient clinic within VA Charleston Health Care, open weekdays, with primary care, mental health, geriatrics, laboratory, imaging and telehealth. The nearest full VA medical center is the Ralph H. Johnson VA Medical Center at 109 Bee Street in Charleston. There is no VA clinic in Conway, North Myrtle Beach or Georgetown. If you are buying with a VA loan , check that drive at the same time.

An estimate, not a fact. Rates, brackets and retirement rules come from each state's own department of revenue and statutes for 2026, and the Myrtle Beach property tax uses Horry County's 2026 certified millage for an owner-occupied home outside the city limits, with the 4 percent residential ratio, the school operating exemption and the 65 and older homestead exemption. Left out on both sides: federal tax, car taxes, insurance, and any credit that depends on your own return. Where a state rule is too detailed to model we leave it out, and almost every one of those left out would RAISE the bill in the state you are leaving, not lower it: Connecticut's tax recapture, New York's supplemental tax, and the exemption phase-outs in Maryland and Ohio. Three would LOWER it, and we name them: Pennsylvania's tax forgiveness and the Massachusetts senior circuit breaker are low-income credits we do not apply, and Florida caps how fast a homesteaded home's assessed value can rise, so a long-held Florida home's real bill is below our estimate. If one of those is you, your bill in the state you are leaving is lower than we show. Insurance is a separate cost to check on this coast, usually higher here than in the states up north; coming from coastal Florida it is priced address by address, in both directions. The coastal insurance page has the real numbers. Your accountant gives you the final answer, and we will sit down and go through it with you.

The county tax

## You stop paying the county income tax
Maryland is unusual. Every county and Baltimore City charges an income tax on top of the state rate, and you pay it based on where you live rather than where you work. On the Comptroller's own 2025 rate chart those local rates run from 2.65 percent to 3.30 percent, and the great majority of counties sit at 3.20 percent. Two moved for 2026: Allegany rose to 3.20 percent and Kent to 3.30 percent.
South Carolina has no local income tax anywhere, in any county or town. A Maryland household earning here keeps that entire amount, and it applies to the first dollar of income rather than the last.
The state rates themselves are closer than people expect. Maryland runs 4.75 percent on most middle incomes, up to $150,000 of taxable income on a joint return. South Carolina charges 1.99 percent on the first $30,000 and 5.21 percent above it, with a deduction that shrinks as joint income climbs from $80,000 to $190,000. Compare the state lines and it is not obvious. Add the county tax and it is.
Two Maryland rules bite harder at the top. The 2025 legislative session added brackets of 6.25 and 6.5 percent above $600,000 and $1,200,000 of taxable income on a joint return. It also imposed an additional 2 percent tax on net capital gains for anyone with federal adjusted gross income over $350,000. Maryland itemized deductions also phase out above $200,000 of federal AGI. If you are selling a business or a large position in the same year you move, the timing of that sale matters and it is a question for your accountant before you list the house.

Retirees

## Check which exclusion you are relying on
Social Security is untaxed in both states, so that part of the move is neutral. Everything else needs looking at, because Maryland's pension exclusion is generous and it is age-gated.
Maryland excludes up to $39,500 of qualifying pension and retirement income for tax year 2024, and up to $41,200 for tax year 2025. The exclusion applies if you were 65 or older on the last day of the year, or if you or your spouse were totally disabled. The figure is indexed, so always check the year on any number you are quoted, including this one. Military retirees at least 55 may subtract up to $20,000 of military retirement income.
South Carolina exempts military retirement fully at any age. Other retirement income is sheltered by a retirement deduction of up to $3,000 before 65 and up to $10,000 from 65. From 65 there is also an age-65 deduction of up to $15,000, and the retirement deduction counts toward it. A Maryland retiree already over 65 and drawing a large pension may find the income tax comparison closer than expected, while the county tax, the property tax and the estate tax all still move in their favor. Run it both ways before you decide, and the retiree page covers what else changes.

The estate

## Maryland is the only state that charges both
Maryland levies an estate tax and an inheritance tax. The estate tax applies above a $5 million exemption at rates reaching 16 percent. The inheritance tax applies to property passing to heirs who are not direct lineal relatives, so children and grandchildren are exempt from it while a niece, a nephew or a friend is not.
South Carolina has neither. For a household with a paid-off house and retirement accounts, and for anyone whose plan leaves property to someone other than their children, this is a larger number than the annual tax lines above it. Your domicile at death sets which state taxes the estate, so if a move is part of that plan, do it properly rather than halfway. We are not tax advisers and this is a conversation for your own; what we can tell you is that it comes up on this page more than any other.

The rest of the bill

## Property tax drops, sales tax rises, and the car is new

### Property tax
Maryland averages about 0.92 percent effective statewide with a median bill of $4,144. South Carolina averages about 0.49 percent, and Horry County about 0.38 percent on a primary home, where the primary rate also removes the school operating tax. The median bill here is $1,337. You apply for the primary rate yourself, and the property tax page has the calculator and the deadline.

### The car tax is new
This is the one that surprises Maryland movers, because Maryland does not bill you for your car every year. Here every vehicle is taxed on its value annually, the county bill must be paid before the plate renews, and a vehicle titled elsewhere pays a one-time $250 fee at first registration. You have 45 days from the move. Boats and campers work the same way. The steps in order are on the new resident checklist .

### Sales tax goes up
Maryland charges 6 percent with no local add-on, and exempts groceries. Here it is 8 percent in the county and 9 percent inside the City of Myrtle Beach, and groceries are untaxed in Horry County. On everything that is not food, you will pay more.

First hand

## What a Howard County transplant noticed here
A colleague of ours made this exact move from Clarksville and then Columbia, in Howard County. Three of his observations hold up and are worth having before you arrive.
The organic food moved from the store to the farm. He finds the grocery stores here carry less of what he bought off the shelf in Maryland. The answer turned out to be the farm stands and butcher shops, which are more common here and closer to town than the ones he knew in Maryland.
Summer is motorcycle season. He counts far more bikes here than he ever saw in Maryland, and another of our team rides one too: the roads are flat and straight, and the riding season is most of the year.
There is construction everywhere, because the growth statistics on our jobs page are visible from the road. New neighborhoods, new stores and three new hospitals at once. Coming from a settled Maryland suburb, that is the change he says you notice first.

Common questions

## Maryland to Myrtle Beach FAQ

### Is South Carolina cheaper than Maryland?
On tax, yes for most households, and the county income tax is the reason. Every Maryland county and Baltimore City charges one on top of the state rate, and most sit at 3.20 percent. South Carolina has no local income tax anywhere. Property tax and a typical house both cost less here too.

### Does Maryland have a local income tax?
Yes. Every county and Baltimore City levies one on top of the state rate. On the Comptroller’s 2025 chart the rates run from 2.65 percent to 3.30 percent, with most counties at 3.20 percent. Two changed for 2026: Allegany rose to 3.20 percent and Kent to 3.30 percent. South Carolina charges none.

### Does Maryland tax my retirement income?
Social Security is not taxed in Maryland. Other pension and retirement income is taxed, with a pension exclusion for taxpayers who are 65 or older or totally disabled: $39,500 for tax year 2024 and $41,200 for tax year 2025, indexed each year. Military retirees at least 55 may subtract up to $20,000.

### What is the Maryland estate and inheritance tax?
Maryland is the only state with both. The estate tax applies above a $5 million exemption at rates up to 16 percent, and a separate inheritance tax applies to property passing to non-lineal heirs. Direct lineal heirs are exempt from the inheritance tax. South Carolina has neither.

### Will I pay a new tax on my car in South Carolina?
Yes, and for most movers it is the surprise. South Carolina taxes every vehicle on its value each year, and the county bill must be paid before the plate renews. A car titled elsewhere also pays a one-time $250 fee at first registration, and you have 45 days from the move to register.

### How much does a house cost in Myrtle Beach compared with Maryland?
A typical home here costs about $342,000, against a Maryland statewide average of about $433,000 on the same July 2026 Zillow measure. Your own county can sit far from that average, so compare your city with here on our cost of living calculator.

## Myrtle Beach Hurricanes: Every Damaging Storm Since 1989
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/relocating/hurricanes/
Summary: Every hurricane and tropical storm that damaged the Grand Strand since 1989, from weather service records, with a first person account of Hugo from our broker.

Home / Buyers / Relocating / Hurricanes
The storm record

# Hurricanes in Myrtle Beach: every damaging storm since 1989.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 1, 2026
Every hurricane to reach the Grand Strand since Hugo in 1989 and what each one did, plus what to check on any Myrtle Beach address before you buy.
Ask about the storms Call 854.333.2135

The short answer

## Myrtle Beach can have hurricanes
Start with the comparison, because it is the fairest way to frame the risk. Of the five states hurricanes hit most, South Carolina is hit the least. Since 1851 the federal count of direct hurricane hits is 120 for Florida, 64 for Texas, 56 for North Carolina and 54 for Louisiana, against 30 here. The last major hurricane to come ashore on this coast was Hugo, in 1989.
We are not going to tell you hurricanes are not a thing here, because they are, and we are not going to tell you they are constant, because the record says otherwise. Since 1989, eight tropical systems have done real damage on the Grand Strand. Most seasons pass without a direct hit. Every damaging storm in that record arrived between August and early October.
The Atlantic season runs June 1 to November 30. Government climatology puts the peak at September 10, with most activity between mid August and mid October. What follows is each storm and what it did here, from National Weather Service storm reports. You can then judge the risk from facts instead of from a brochure in either direction.

The record

## Every damaging storm since 1989, and what it did here

Storm When What happened on the Grand Strand

Hugo, Category 4 September 1989 13 foot surge at Garden City destroyed many homes there; three Myrtle Beach piers destroyed; dunes washed away

Floyd, Category 2 September 1999 16.8 inches of rain in Myrtle Beach; chest deep water near Pine Lakes; the largest peacetime evacuation to that date

Matthew, Category 1 October 2016 74 mph gust at the airport; Springmaid Pier destroyed; the Waccamaw River crested at 17.87 feet ten days later; 170 roads closed

Florence, Category 1 September 2018 Landfall in North Carolina; up to 23.63 inches of rain; record river flooding near Conway and Socastee days afterward

Dorian, offshore September 2019 Stayed 30 miles off Cape Fear; an EF0 tornado in North Myrtle Beach; 15.21 inches of rain at Pawleys Island

Isaias, Category 1 August 2020 Landfall just over the state line; middle of the Cherry Grove pier destroyed; a foot of flooding a block inland in North Myrtle Beach

Ian, Category 1 September 2022 Landfall near Georgetown; part of the Pawleys Island pier collapsed; two more piers damaged; three feet of sand across a Garden City road

Debby, tropical storm August 2024 15 to 19 inches of rain across the county; three tornadoes in the region; river flooding that continued well after the storm

Each row is from the National Weather Service Wilmington office's report on that storm. Categories are at landfall. Dorian and Florence made landfall elsewhere; their damage here came from rain, surf and tornadoes.

Hugo, first person

## Tim was here for Hugo. This is what he remembers.
Tim Nash, our Broker-in-Charge, has sold real estate on this coast for more than 30 years. In September 1989 he was here as Hugo came in. This is his recollection, as he told it to us.
His family left for Augusta, Georgia, around 3 or 4 in the afternoon, about five hours ahead of the outer bands. The eye came ashore near Charleston about midnight, and the north side of the eye, the worst side, went over McClellanville, about fifty miles south of here. They waited the storm out in a hotel and started back at checkout time.
At the Socastee bridge the traffic was stopped: the National Guard was turning returning residents around. His father worked in emergency medical services, so the family was let through. At the house, power, water and telephone were all out. His father had filled the bathtubs and two 50 gallon barrels in the yard before they evacuated. Power stayed out for about two weeks, and the family collected drinking water at town hall each day for about as long.
His father let him take his dirt bike up the beach to check on his grandmother's house, five miles north, oceanfront on the south end of Myrtle Beach. Pieces of houses and piers were strung down the length of the beach, with dead fish everywhere. Her house stood. Flood water had filled it and drained back out, and campers sat in piles in her front yard. The National Guard sent him home.
The record backs his memory of the geography. Weather service reports put Hugo's landfall winds near 140 miles an hour at midnight on September 22. Storm surge was up to 20 feet near Cape Romain and 16 feet at McClellanville, where six feet of seawater entered the school gymnasium. Gusts at Myrtle Beach were about 76 miles an hour. In his words: We were lucky. One shift north of 50 miles and nothing would have been left here.

The fact buyers miss

## Where storm water went: inland, days later
People shopping from out of state usually picture hurricane risk as an oceanfront problem. The last decade here says something different. Florence made landfall in North Carolina in September 2018, and the wind on the Grand Strand stayed below hurricane strength. The damage came from rain. It kept falling for days, and the Waccamaw River rose for almost two weeks, reaching a record 21.16 feet at Conway on September 26. Weather service records count about 1,000 flooded homes and businesses near the river, severe flooding along the Intracoastal Waterway in Socastee, and 1,580 more damaged homes in rural parts of the county. Two years earlier, Matthew had pushed the same river to what was then its record.
The question that matters when you buy is not how close the ocean is. A house two blocks from the beach on high ground and a house twelve miles inland beside the river carry different risks, and neither one is obvious from the photos of the home.
That is what the maps are for. Every address has a FEMA flood zone, and the insurance page explains why the zone named X still does not mean zero risk. Every address also has a county evacuation zone, covered next.

After the rain

## Streets here drain fast, and there is a reason
One of our team remembers noticing it during Tropical Storm Debby. There were days of rain, a few inches of water standing on some streets, and driving was slow but possible. Then the main roads dried almost as soon as the rain stopped. He moved here from Ohio and expected the water to sit. On the main roads, it did not.
Part of the reason is built and paid for. Myrtle Beach has spent close to $75 million on four deepwater ocean outfalls. These are large underground pipes that collect street runoff and carry it more than 1,000 feet offshore, past the breakers. That keeps it from standing in town or pouring across the sand. North Myrtle Beach has built six of its own since 2002 and states the purpose plainly: better inland drainage keeps streets and properties dry, and moving the discharge offshore keeps bacteria out of the surf where people swim. More outfalls are planned in both cities.
When heavy rain lands on a high tide, the drains have nowhere to send the water for a few hours. The lowest streets in places like Cherry Grove and Garden City hold water until the tide drops. River flooding is the opposite of street flooding: near the Waccamaw and the Intracoastal, water rises over days and stays, as the section above describes. Fast-draining streets are a beach-town fact, not a county-wide one.

No storm required

## King tides, and the few low streets they reach
A king tide is the informal name for the highest tides of the year. They arrive on predictable dates, mostly around fall full moons, with no storm attached. On those days salt water can come up through the storm drains on the lowest streets until the tide turns.
Pawleys Island is the local example. On the biggest tides the island's low streets flood, and the causeways have been closed at the peak until the water dropped. The town says so itself: officials call flooding their first public safety issue, and the island is funding a drainage and flood plan. People who live there check the dates and plan around them. If you are shopping on Pawleys, the tide calendar comes with the island; ask us and we will time a showing to a high tide so you see the street at its worst before you offer.
Cherry Grove and the lowest streets of Garden City see the same tides.

From our team

## What we do when a warning goes up
For a tropical storm or a low-end hurricane, our team stays home and waits it out. Many houses here have window protectors that fold down over the glass in a few minutes, and you will see the mounts beside the windows when you tour. Debby in 2024 was that kind of storm for us: days of rain and flooded rivers rather than destructive wind on the beach.
During one stronger storm, someone we know boarded up his house and took his family to sleep at his office for the night, because the building is newer commercial construction and he trusted it more than his house. Calm and specific. Water, fuel, the shutters down, and a decision made early about staying or going.
When the county orders an evacuation for your zone, you go. That is what the lettered zones below are for, and the county announces orders zone by zone on its own channels. Everything above is our experience, not safety instruction. The county's emergency division decides.

Before you buy

## Three things to check on any address, before you fall for the house

### The flood zone
Look the address up on the federal flood maps. The zone decides whether a lender requires flood insurance and is the single best public clue to where water has gone before. We pull it for every address our buyers consider.

### The evacuation zone
Horry County uses lettered evacuation zones, A, B and C, and the state orders evacuations by zone. The Know Your Zone map shows any address in seconds. Knowing your letter before a storm is the difference between following one clear instruction and refreshing the news.

### Insurance can pause while a storm approaches
An insurance company may place a moratorium on issuing new policies in an area where a hurricane is expected. That pause matters most when you are under contract: the loan cannot close without a bound policy, so a buyer who leaves insurance to the week of closing can end up waiting out a storm instead. Bind the policy early in the process, and we get estimates on the exact address as part of any offer we write. A storm plan you made in February beats one you make in September.

Common questions

## Myrtle Beach hurricane FAQ

### Do hurricanes hit Myrtle Beach?
Yes. Since 1989, seven hurricanes and one tropical storm have done real damage on the Grand Strand, from Hugo through Tropical Storm Debby in 2024. Most seasons pass with no direct hit. The Atlantic season runs June 1 to November 30 and peaks around September 10.

### When was the last hurricane to hit Myrtle Beach?
Hurricane Ian made landfall near Georgetown as a Category 1 on September 30, 2022, damaging three piers here and pushing sand over roads in Garden City. Tropical Storm Debby followed in August 2024 with 15 to 19 inches of rain and river flooding that lasted well after the storm.

### What was the worst hurricane in Myrtle Beach history?
Hugo, September 22, 1989, a Category 4 that came ashore near Sullivan's Island. Weather service records show a 13 foot storm surge at Garden City that destroyed many homes there, and three piers destroyed in Myrtle Beach. Nothing since has matched it. Our Broker-in-Charge was here for Hugo; his first person account is on this page.

### Does Myrtle Beach flood?
Two different ways. Storm surge floods low ground near the ocean during a storm. River flooding comes days later and reaches inland: after Florence in 2018 the Waccamaw River crested at 21.16 feet and flooded about 1,000 homes and businesses near Conway, plus 1,580 more in rural parts of the county. Check the flood zone of the address, not the town name.

### When is hurricane season in Myrtle Beach?
June 1 to November 30, the Atlantic season. Government climatology puts the peak at September 10, with most activity from mid August to mid October. Every damaging storm in the local record since 1989 arrived between August and early October.

### What is my hurricane evacuation zone in Myrtle Beach?
Horry County uses lettered Zones A, B and C, and evacuations are ordered by zone. Look up any address on the state's Know Your Zone map before you buy, the same way you check its flood zone. We pull both for every address our buyers consider.

### Do streets flood in Myrtle Beach when it rains?
During hard rain some streets hold a few inches of water, and the main roads usually drain within hours of the rain stopping. Myrtle Beach and North Myrtle Beach have spent tens of millions on deepwater ocean outfalls that carry street runoff offshore. The exceptions: the lowest streets near the beach when a high tide blocks the drains, and river neighborhoods, where flooding can last days.

### What is a king tide in Myrtle Beach?
The informal name for the highest tides of the year, on predictable dates around fall full moons. A few low streets flood with no storm at all, most visibly on Pawleys Island, where the causeways have been closed at peak tide and the town is funding a drainage plan. If you are buying on a low street, ask us for the tide dates before you tour.

# Myrtle Beach weather, season by season: it snows about an inch a year.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 1, 2026
Myrtle Beach weather by month: summer highs, mild winters, the ocean temperature month by month, and when the swim season runs, from the nearest long-term weather station.

The short answer

## The four seasons, from the official station
These are 1991 to 2020 normals from the North Myrtle Beach airport station, the one the National Weather Service uses for this coast's official records. A normal is a thirty year average, so a given week will run above or below it.

Season Normal high / low What the record adds

Winter, January 55.7 / 36.7 About 34 nights a year at or below freezing

Spring, April 71.8 / 53.3 Ocean already in the upper 60s by late April

Summer, July 87.6 / 73.7 About 21 days a year reach 90; almost none reach 100

Fall, October 75.6 / 56.3 Ocean still averages in the low 70s

The averages do not show storms. Hurricane season runs from the start of June to the end of November, and the largest single rain totals here have come from tropical systems. Every storm that reached the Grand Strand since 1989 is on our storm by storm record .

Annual normals at the same station: 72.7 high, 55.2 low, 48.47 inches of rain across about 122 days with measurable precipitation. Station USW00093718, NOAA 1991 to 2020 monthly normals.

The ocean

## How warm the water is, month by month
This is the federal water temperature gauge at Springmaid Pier in Myrtle Beach, averaged by month across 2024 and 2025. Nobody has to guess.

Months Water temperature

January and February around 50

March and April upper 50s to upper 60s

NOAA Springmaid Pier gauge, station 8661070, hourly readings averaged by us across 2024 and 2025. The bracket marks May into October, when the water is at or above 70 degrees, the low end of what the federal coastal water temperature guide calls comfortable for most swimmers.

Humidity and sun

## The two numbers people argue about, sourced

### The humidity, in numbers
Myrtle Beach itself has no long term government humidity record, so the honest numbers come from the nearest stations that do. Wilmington's long term record shows morning humidity around 85 to 88 percent in July and August, and the closest hourly station puts July dew points around 73 degrees. That combination is why an 87 degree afternoon here asks more of you than the same number inland. Summers are air conditioned, and the cost of living calculator carries the real electricity bills that go with that.

### The sunny days number you see everywhere is not a government number
Websites repeat that Myrtle Beach gets about 215 sunny days a year. That figure comes from commercial estimates, not from NOAA, and no government station publishes it. What the nearest long term government station does show: 62 percent of possible sunshine and about 111 clear days a year. On that same government measure, Buffalo records 54 clear days, Pittsburgh 59 and Cleveland 66. The honest version is still a large difference; it just is not 215.

Snow

## It snows about an inch a year, and twice lately it mattered
The weather service keeps a snowfall database for Myrtle Beach going back to 1940. The total across those 85 years is 87.4 inches, an average of about one inch a year, and most years record none at all. The record is 14 inches, December 1989.
Recent years have been livelier than the average suggests. Five inches fell in January 2025, which the weather service called the city's largest snowstorm in 35 years, and another five fell at the turn of February 2026. Plows are not a municipal habit here, so a snow day mostly means the town closes and children see the beach white, briefly.
One of our team moved here from Ohio expecting to leave snow behind. It snowed his first winter, and he jokes that he brought it with him. His real measure of winter is his motorcycle: he rides into late November or early December, what finally stops him is the cold night ride home rather than the daytime, and the bike stays parked for about three months. He is back on it around the middle of March. Winters here are mild next to Ohio, and still not shorts weather unless the sun is out and you have some tolerance.

Common questions

## Myrtle Beach weather FAQ

### How hot are Myrtle Beach summers?
The normal summer high is about 86 degrees, with about 21 days a year reaching 90 and almost none reaching 100. July normals at the North Myrtle Beach station are 87.6 for the high and 73.7 for the low. The heat is humid, so it reads hotter than the number.

### Does it snow in Myrtle Beach?
About an inch a year on average, and most years none. The weather service snowfall database shows 87.4 total inches since 1940. The record is 14 inches in December 1989, and the 5 inch storm of January 2025 was the biggest in 35 years. Another 5 inches fell in early 2026.

### What is winter like in Myrtle Beach?
January normals are a 55.7 degree high and a 36.7 low at the North Myrtle Beach station, with about 34 nights a year at or below freezing. The beach stays open, the boardwalk stays open, and the tourist crowds are gone.

### How warm is the ocean in Myrtle Beach?
On the government pier gauge, roughly 50 degrees in January and February, upper 60s by late April, and upper 70s to mid 80s from June through September. October still averages in the low 70s, and November falls to the mid 60s.

### How many sunny days does Myrtle Beach get?
The 215 sunny days figure that circulates online is a commercial estimate, not a government one. The nearest long term government station shows about 111 clear days a year and 62 percent of possible sunshine, well above Great Lakes and inland Northeast cities on the same measure.

### How humid is Myrtle Beach?
Humid in summer. The nearest station with long term humidity records shows morning humidity around 85 to 88 percent in July and August. July dew points at the closest hourly station average around 73 degrees, which is what makes 87 feel heavy.

## Getting Around Myrtle Beach: The 4 Road Names to Learn

Planes, roads and the bus

# Getting around Myrtle Beach: learn these four road names first.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 1, 2026
Drive times between Grand Strand towns, the Myrtle Beach airport with ten airlines and nonstop service to more than 50 cities, summer traffic, the bus, and the I-73 project.
Ask a local Call 854.333.2135

The airport

## The airport is in town, and the family can fly straight here
Myrtle Beach International sits inside the city, minutes from most of the Grand Strand rather than an hour out. As of August 2026 it lists ten airlines and nonstop service to more than 50 cities, and the airline list changes several times a year, so check the current route map for your own city. The terminal was expanded in December 2025, and the airport took top national rankings in USA Today's 10Best readers' choice awards in October 2025.

### What that is worth when you live here
You can get back to where you came from without a connection, and the people you left can get to you. One of our clients works his New York job in alternating weeks from here, which the jobs page covers. It also shapes where to buy. The airport sits at the south end of Myrtle Beach beside Market Common, so Surfside Beach and Socastee are about 15 minutes from a departure. Even North Myrtle Beach or Pawleys Island is about half an hour. Tell us which trips you make most and we will keep the airport run in mind when we build your showing list.

### Notes from our own trips
An hour is enough with no checked bag. With real luggage plan on two and a half hours, because bag check closes out well before departure and same day ticket sales stop roughly two hours before takeoff, in our experience. Allegiant's own fee schedule lists a $22 per passenger, per segment charge on bookings made on the website or call center. Buy at the airport counter instead and that charge does not apply. The counter is staffed around departures, which is workable once you live here. Some of our clients hold Frontier's GoWild all you can fly pass : as of August 2026 Frontier's nonstops from here are Cleveland and Long Island, and the pass also books connecting routes.

The roads

## Two US 17s and two freeways: learn these four names first

### US 17 Business is Kings Highway
The old road, closest to the ocean, running through the beachfront strip with stoplights and driveways. Slowest, most scenic, most tourist traffic.

### US 17 Bypass carries the most traffic
The divided highway just inland. Its busiest stretch, between SC 707 and US 501, counted 82,200 vehicles a day in 2025, the highest figure in the county.

### SC 31 and SC 22 are the roads locals use
Two limited access freeways further inland, built under the county's road sales tax. SC 31 runs behind the beach from Little River to Socastee; SC 22 connects the Conway area to the north strand. Almost no stoplights on either. The county's own planning document says many returning tourists avoid or are unaware of these roads. That is why a ten mile drive on them is quicker than the same ten miles on the beach highway, measured on the town by town page .

### US 501 is the road inland
The main road to Conway and onward toward I-95. A surface road with lights, not a freeway, and it carries up to 65,900 vehicles a day near the beach. If your life will run between Conway and the coast daily, drive your exact commute once before you offer on a house.
One concrete commute, from one of our team: US 17 from Murrells Inlet to Surfside Beach at 7 a.m. is wide open. The run up to Carolina Forest near 5 p.m. is a little busy. The only place he reliably waits is the traffic lights entering and leaving Carolina Forest. In three years of daily driving he has yet to sit in traffic on SC 31.

The interstate

## The honest status of I-73
Myrtle Beach is one of the largest US metros with no interstate connection, and the planned fix is I-73, which would link the coast to I-95. As of 2026 the truthful status is this: no segment is open, no segment is under construction, and no construction contract has been signed. The state has bought about 99 percent of the right of way between I-95 and US 501 and most of the next stretch. The county has set aside 450 million dollars of conditional matching money that is only paid out when the state signs construction contracts. There is no opening date yet.
Separately, the two Carolinas are studying an extension of SC 31 north across the state line to US 17 near Shallotte. Hearings were held in autumn 2025; construction, if it happens, was reported as unlikely to begin before 2029. Until either project moves, the practical routes to the wider world are US 501 to I-95, and US 17 along the coast.

The bus, honestly

## The bus, and why households here run on cars
The public bus, Coast RTA, runs ten fixed routes, seven days a week, 362 days a year, reaching Myrtle Beach, Conway, Surfside Beach, Garden City, Murrells Inlet, Pawleys Island, Georgetown, Loris and more. Every bus is wheelchair accessible. The fare is about a dollar a ride with a daily cap when you tap a card; the operator's posted tables vary, so check the current fare on their site before you rely on it.
It is not a system you can build a commute around in most of the county. The main Conway to Myrtle Beach route starts about 6 a.m. and finishes its last runs by about 9 p.m., and its express version runs twice a day each way. Households here run on cars, and many neighborhoods add a golf cart for local streets, which takes a five dollar permit covered on the new resident checklist .

Common questions

## Getting around Myrtle Beach FAQ

### Does Myrtle Beach have an airport?
Yes, inside the city. Myrtle Beach International had ten airlines and nonstop service to more than 50 cities as of August 2026, and 3.8 million passengers in 2024, the last full year it has published. A terminal expansion opened in December 2025.

### Do you need a car in Myrtle Beach?
Plan on one. The public bus runs seven days a week and covers the main towns, but routes are limited and most daily life here is built around driving. Many neighborhoods also allow golf carts on local streets, with a permit.

### Is there public transportation in Myrtle Beach?
Coast RTA runs ten fixed bus routes seven days a week, 362 days a year, serving Myrtle Beach, Conway, Surfside Beach, Garden City, Murrells Inlet, Pawleys Island, Georgetown, Loris and more. Fares are about a dollar a ride; check the current table on their site. Every bus is wheelchair accessible.

### Is I-73 to Myrtle Beach built yet?
No. As of 2026 no segment of I-73 in South Carolina is open or under construction. The state is buying right of way between I-95 and the coast, and the county has set aside conditional matching money, but no construction contract exists. Treat any completion date you hear as a guess.

### What is the difference between US 17 Business and US 17 Bypass?
Two parallel roads. Business is Kings Highway, the older road near the ocean with stoplights and driveways. The Bypass is the divided highway inland of it, carrying much more traffic: its busiest stretch counted 82,200 vehicles a day in 2025, the highest in the county. SC 31 runs even further inland with almost no lights.

### How far is Myrtle Beach from Charleston or Charlotte?
Measured on the road network with no traffic: Charleston is about 98 miles and 2 hours 15 minutes, and Wilmington about 74 miles and 1 hour 45. Charlotte is about 170 miles and 3 hours 40, Raleigh about 186 miles and 3 hours 45, and Columbia about 138 miles and 3 hours 5.

An estimate, not a fact. Rates, brackets and retirement rules come from each state's own department of revenue and statutes for 2026, and the Myrtle Beach property tax uses Horry County's 2026 certified millage for an owner-occupied home outside the city limits, with the 4 percent residential ratio, the school operating exemption and the 65 and older homestead exemption. Left out on both sides: federal tax, car taxes, insurance, and any credit that depends on your own return. Where a state rule is too detailed to model we leave it out, and almost every one of those left out would RAISE the bill in the state you are leaving, not lower it: Connecticut's tax recapture, New York's supplemental tax, and the exemption phase-outs in Maryland and Ohio. Three would LOWER it, and we name them: Pennsylvania's tax forgiveness and the Massachusetts senior circuit breaker are low-income credits we do not apply, and Florida caps how fast a homesteaded home's assessed value can rise, so a long-held Florida home's real bill is below our estimate. If one of those is you, your bill in the state you are leaving is lower than we show. Insurance is a separate cost to check on this coast, usually higher here than in the states up north; coming from coastal Florida it is priced address by address, in both directions. The coastal insurance page has the real numbers. Your accountant gives you the final answer, and we will sit down and go through it with you.

What the sale buys

## What a Virginia sale buys at the coast
A typical Virginia home costs about $418,000 on the statewide Zillow average, against about $342,000 here, on the same July 2026 measure. That statewide number hides the split that matters: Northern Virginia sits far above it and much of the rest of the state below it. See how much further every dollar goes here compared with your hometown on the cost of living calculator . The property tax on whatever you buy drops from a $2,872 median bill to a $1,337 one.
Two parts of the map speak Virginia's language. Market Common is built on the old Myrtle Beach Air Force Base, and the street grid and parade ground still carry its history, with the airport next door. The beach towns run from North Myrtle Beach to Pawleys Island , each at a different price, and appeal to different types of people. Check the town by town page to see what differs.

Retirees

## Deductions here come with no income test
Social Security is untaxed in both states, so start from level ground. The difference is what each state does with the rest of retirement income, and Virginia's headline number has a condition that surprises people who have never run it.
Virginia's age deduction is up to $12,000 at 65 and over. It then shrinks a dollar for every dollar that adjusted federal AGI exceeds $50,000 for a single filer or $75,000 for a married couple, and it is gone entirely at $62,000 and $99,000. A couple drawing a pension and two Social Security checks crosses those lines quickly. Pensions, 401(k) and IRA withdrawals are otherwise fully taxed at Virginia's rates.
South Carolina's retirement and age-65 deductions have no income test: up to $3,000 of retirement income before 65, and from 65 up to $15,000 per person against any income, with the retirement deduction counted inside it. The numbers are smaller than Virginia's $12,000; the difference is that you keep them no matter what you earn.
Military retirement is its own line. Virginia lets you subtract up to $40,000 of military benefits on 2025 and later returns, with no age requirement, which is generous. South Carolina exempts every dollar of military retirement pay, at any age, with no cap. Below $40,000 of military pension the states match; above it, this is the only one of the two that never taxes it. The VA loan page covers the buying side for veterans.
Retiring on a pension and not sure which state wins?
Talk it through with an expert Call 854.333.2135

The income tax

## More of your income is never taxed here
Virginia's top rate of 5.75 percent begins at just $17,000 of taxable income, so nearly everyone with a working income pays it on most of their dollars. South Carolina charges 1.99 percent on the first $30,000 and 5.21 percent above it.
The bigger difference is what gets taxed at all. South Carolina's deduction is up to $15,000 single and $30,000 joint, against Virginia's $8,750 and $17,500. South Carolina's shrinks as income rises. It is larger than Virginia's up to about $63,000 of income single and $126,000 joint, and smaller above that. This is a modest cut, not a New York one, and we would rather tell you that plainly. Where the move pays for itself is the property tax and the house price.

The familiar one

## The car tax will not surprise you
Every other state page we have written warns the mover about South Carolina's annual vehicle tax, because Ohio, Maryland, New York and the rest do not bill you yearly for a car. You do not need the warning. Virginia's personal property tax on vehicles works the same way, so the only thing to learn is the local numbers.
Here every vehicle is taxed on its value each year and the county bill is paid before the plate renews. A $30,000 car is taxed about $362 a year in unincorporated Horry County, about $458 inside the City of Myrtle Beach, plus a $50 county road fee. A car titled elsewhere pays a one-time $250 fee at first registration, and you have 45 days from the move to register. Boats and campers are taxed the same way.
The order of operations matters here: insurance first, county tax second, DMV third. The new resident checklist walks it step by step with the deadlines.

The rest of the bill

## Property tax drops by more than half

### Property tax
Virginia averages about 0.78 percent effective statewide with a median bill of $2,872. South Carolina averages about 0.49 percent, and Horry County about 0.38 percent on a primary home, where the primary rate also removes the school operating tax. The median bill here is $1,337. You apply for the primary rate yourself, and the property tax page has the calculator and the deadline.

### Sales tax
Virginia charges 5.3 percent in most places. Here it is 8 percent in the county and 9 percent inside the City of Myrtle Beach, and we would rather be honest with you about that: on most purchases the tax is higher. Groceries are the exception: untaxed in Horry County, and everyday goods price lower here than in Virginia on the federal price index, so the grocery run itself usually costs less.

First hand

## What our Virginia clients tell us
One of our buyers came down from Virginia Beach, and his comparison stuck with us because it was fair in both directions. Virginia Beach is a much bigger city than Myrtle Beach, and he would tell you its entertainment scene runs many times the size of ours. Nobody should move here expecting a bigger boardwalk than the one they left.
What our Virginia clients say they come for instead: a smaller place that is growing quickly, where the money they bring goes further and getting ahead does not require a Northern Virginia income. Most of them leave with real respect for Virginia and the military and government careers it gave them, and they want more of the year outdoors than Virginia weather allows.
Nobody here parties like Miami, one client put it, but people here are enjoying their money. That is as fair a one-line summary of the Grand Strand as we have heard, and the pros and cons page carries the rest of the honest picture, including the parts people leave over.

Common questions

## Virginia to Myrtle Beach FAQ

### Is South Carolina cheaper than Virginia?
On most lines, modestly. The state income tax is close. South Carolina's deduction is larger than Virginia's for a couple earning up to about $126,000. Property tax on a primary home runs less than half, and a typical house costs about $76,000 less on the statewide averages. Sales tax is the line that goes up.

### Does Virginia or South Carolina tax military retirement?
Virginia lets you subtract up to $40,000 of military benefits on 2025 and later returns, with no age requirement. South Carolina exempts every dollar of military retirement pay at any age, with no cap. Below $40,000 of military pension the two match; above it, only South Carolina exempts it all.

### What happens to the Virginia age deduction when I move?
It stays behind, and for many retirees it was already gone: Virginia's $12,000 age deduction shrinks a dollar for every dollar of adjusted federal AGI over $50,000 single or $75,000 married, and is gone entirely at $62,000 and $99,000. South Carolina's retirement and age-65 deductions have no income test.

### Will I still pay an annual car tax in South Carolina?
Yes, and you already know the routine. Every vehicle is taxed on its value each year and the county bill is paid before the plate renews. A $30,000 car is taxed about $362 a year in unincorporated Horry County plus a $50 road fee, and a car titled elsewhere pays a one-time $250 fee at first registration.

### How much does a house cost in Myrtle Beach compared with Virginia?
A typical home here costs about $342,000 against a Virginia statewide average of about $418,000, on the same July 2026 Zillow measure. The statewide number hides the split between Northern Virginia and everywhere else. See how much further every dollar goes here on our cost of living calculator.

### Does South Carolina tax Social Security?
No, and neither does Virginia, so that part of the move is neutral. The differences are in how each state treats the rest of retirement income, and in the property tax.

Rates, brackets and retirement rules come from each state's own department of revenue and statutes for 2026, and the Myrtle Beach property tax uses Horry County's 2026 certified millage for an owner-occupied home outside the city limits, with the 4 percent residential ratio, the school operating exemption and the 65 and older homestead exemption. Left out on both sides: federal tax, car taxes, insurance, and any credit that depends on your own return. Where a state rule is too detailed to model we leave it out, and almost every one of those left out would RAISE the bill in the state you are leaving, not lower it: Connecticut's tax recapture, New York's supplemental tax, and the exemption phase-outs in Maryland and Ohio. Three would LOWER it, and we name them: Pennsylvania's tax forgiveness and the Massachusetts senior circuit breaker are low-income credits we do not apply, and Florida caps how fast a homesteaded home's assessed value can rise, so a long-held Florida home's real bill is below our estimate. If one of those is you, your bill in the state you are leaving is lower than we show. Insurance is a separate cost to check on this coast, usually higher here than in the states up north; coming from coastal Florida it is priced address by address, in both directions. The headline

## The property tax falls by more than half
Connecticut's effective property tax rate of about 1.54 percent is among the highest in the country, and the median bill is $6,573. Horry County's primary-home rate works out near 0.38 percent, the median South Carolina bill is $1,337, and the primary rate also removes the school operating tax from your bill entirely.
Put real numbers on it: a $450,000 Connecticut house near the state average carries a bill most owners here would associate with a house three times the price. Buy a $342,000 home here as your primary residence and the bill lands near a tenth of many Fairfield County bills, and the savings repeat every year you own it.
You apply for the primary rate yourself after you move, by May 31, or your first bill arrives at the higher 6 percent second-home rate. The property tax page has the calculator and the deadline, and the new resident checklist puts it in order with the rest.

A typical Connecticut home costs about $453,000 on the statewide Zillow average, against about $342,000 here, on the same July 2026 measure. Fairfield County sits far above that average and the northeast corner below it. See how much further every dollar goes here compared with your hometown on the cost of living calculator . Retirees

## Your Social Security is never taxed here
Start with the number Connecticut watches and South Carolina ignores. Earn more than $75,000 as a single filer or $100,000 as a couple and Connecticut begins taxing part of your Social Security, and the pension, annuity and IRA exemptions shrink toward zero over the same stretch of income. South Carolina never taxes Social Security, at any income, and its retirement deductions have no income test at all.
$75,000 in Myrtle Beach spends like about $83,000 in Connecticut, and $100,000 spends like about $110,000, from our cost of living calculator .
The specifics for your accountant: At 65 and older South Carolina deducts up to $15,000 of income per person, and the retirement income deduction of up to $10,000 counts against that same $15,000 rather than adding to it. Every dollar of military retirement is exempt. One side note that stays true in either state: a single large IRA withdrawal raises your income for that year, so plan withdrawals with your adviser. The retiree page covers what else changes.

The income tax

## How the two income taxes are built
Connecticut's rates run 2 to 6.99 percent, which looks ordinary next to South Carolina's 1.99 and 5.21. Two design choices make Connecticut's bill bigger than its brackets suggest. There is no standard deduction, only a personal exemption that itself phases out as income rises. Connecticut also applies benefit recapture. Past certain income levels the lower brackets are clawed back, so a high earner pays the top rate on all income rather than just the top slice above the threshold.
South Carolina gives a couple a deduction of up to $30,000. It shrinks once income passes $80,000 and is gone at $190,000. The first $30,000 of taxable income is taxed at 1.99 percent and the rest at 5.21 percent. This particular difference is modest for most households; for high earners the recapture rule makes it larger than the rate gap implies. See how much further every dollar goes here on the cost of living calculator .

The car and the register

## The car bill shrinks here

### The car tax you already know
You will not need the warning we give Ohio and Maryland movers, because Connecticut already taxes cars yearly: 70 percent of a depreciated value at the town mill rate, capped at 32.46 mills. Here the county taxes vehicles on value too. The working numbers: about $362 a year on a $30,000 car in unincorporated Horry County, or about $458 inside the City of Myrtle Beach, plus a $50 road fee. A car titled elsewhere pays a one-time $250 fee when it first registers. For most movers that is a smaller bill than the one they left. The steps and deadlines are on the new resident checklist .

### Sales tax rises
Connecticut charges 6.35 percent statewide. Here it is 8 percent in the county and 9 percent inside the City of Myrtle Beach, and we would rather be honest with you about that: on most purchases the tax is higher. Groceries are the exception: untaxed in both states, and everyday goods price lower here than in Connecticut on the federal price index, so the grocery run itself usually costs the same or less.

The estate advantage

## No estate tax here, at any amount
Connecticut's estate and gift exemption tracks the federal amount, $15 million for 2026. Most families will never reach it. We would rather tell you that plainly than sell you a benefit you would not receive.
Above $15 million, Connecticut charges 12 percent of the amount over the line. That is $120,000 for every million dollars above it. An estate of $20 million owes about $600,000 to Connecticut. An estate of $25 million owes about $1.2 million. South Carolina charges none of it, at any size.
Connecticut is also the only state with its own gift tax, at the same 12 percent above the same $15 million, on large gifts you make while you are alive. South Carolina has no estate tax, no inheritance tax and no gift tax. For an estate above $15 million, moving here saves you twelve cents on the dollar in taxes.

Common questions

## Connecticut to Myrtle Beach FAQ

### Is South Carolina cheaper than Connecticut?
On the recurring bills, yes. Property tax averages about 1.54 percent effective in Connecticut against about 0.38 percent on a primary home in Horry County, and the median bill drops from $6,573 to $1,337. The car tax falls for most movers, and a typical house costs about $111,000 less. Sales tax at the register is the line that rises.

### Does Connecticut tax Social Security?
Not below $75,000 of AGI single or $100,000 married filing jointly. At those thresholds the exemption changes at once rather than phasing gently. South Carolina never taxes Social Security at any income.

### What happens to my pension and IRA exemption when I leave Connecticut?
Connecticut fully exempts pension, annuity and, from 2026, IRA income below $75,000 AGI single or $100,000 joint, sliding to nothing by $100,000 and $150,000. South Carolina's retirement and age-65 deductions are smaller as numbers but have no income test, and military retirement is fully exempt.

### Does South Carolina have a gift or estate tax?
Neither. Connecticut is the only state with its own gift tax, but its estate and gift exemption now tracks the federal amount, $15 million for 2026, so it reaches almost nobody. For most movers this line is no longer the reason to move; the property tax is.

### Will my car tax go up in South Carolina?
For most Connecticut movers it goes down. Both states tax vehicles yearly on value. Connecticut assesses 70 percent of a depreciated value at your town's mill rate, capped at 32.46 mills. Here a $30,000 car is taxed about $362 a year in unincorporated Horry County, plus a $50 road fee and a one-time $250 registration fee on arrival.

### How much does a house cost in Myrtle Beach compared with Connecticut?
A typical home here costs about $342,000 against a Connecticut statewide average of about $453,000, on the same July 2026 Zillow measure. Fairfield County sits far above that average and the northeast corner below it. See how much further every dollar goes here on our cost of living calculator.

The estate

## Massachusetts taxes your estate when you die. South Carolina does not.
Massachusetts taxes estates above $2 million, one of the lowest thresholds in the country. For deaths on or after January 1, 2023 the state allows a credit of $99,600, which is what makes the first $2 million pass untaxed; above the line, the estate itself owes the tax before anything reaches your heirs.
Two million arrives faster than people expect. A paid-off house near the state's $669,000 average, retirement accounts built over two working lifetimes, and life insurance can cross the line together without anyone in the household ever feeling rich. South Carolina has no estate tax and no inheritance tax at any amount.
Most people have never been told this part, and it is worth reading twice. What Massachusetts can reach after you move depends on the kind of asset. Once you are domiciled in South Carolina, your investment accounts, retirement accounts, and other intangible assets are out of the Massachusetts estate tax entirely, wherever the brokerage sits. Real estate is different: a house you keep in Massachusetts stays taxable there even after you become a South Carolinian. The filing trigger is still your total worldwide estate over $2 million, with the tax computed on the Massachusetts property. The move itself protects the accounts; keeping the old house keeps it taxable there.
What decides all of it is where you are domiciled at death, so if this is part of why you are moving, move properly: license, registration, voting, the primary-home application, all of it. We are not tax or estate advisers and the details belong with yours; the part we handle is making you a South Carolinian, and the checklist is where that starts.

What the sale buys

## What a Massachusetts sale buys at the coast
A typical Massachusetts home costs about $669,000 on the statewide Zillow average, against about $342,000 here, on the same July 2026 measure: close to double, the widest spread of any state page we publish. Greater Boston averages more than that statewide number. Sell near the average there, buy near the average here, and the difference funds the move, the furniture and a margin that changes what retirement looks like. See how much further every dollar goes here compared with your hometown on the cost of living calculator .
The coast itself will look structurally familiar: Surfside Beach and Garden City run on compact ocean-block grids of cottages and beach houses, Pawleys Island pairs historic cottages with creek docks, and North Myrtle Beach adds the wide-beach neighborhoods. The water is warmer for longer, which the weather page shows month by month, and the town by town page compares all ten areas.

The income tax

## Five percent flat sounds close to ours. It mostly is.
Massachusetts charges 5 percent on nearly everything, plus 4 percent more on income above about $1.08 million. South Carolina's top rate is 5.21 percent. On rates alone this is the closest matchup of any state we cover.
South Carolina gives a couple a deduction of up to $30,000 where Massachusetts has none, only an $8,800 personal exemption. The South Carolina deduction shrinks above $80,000 of income and is gone at $190,000, so a middle income keeps more here before any rate applies. Massachusetts taxes short-term capital gains at 8.5 percent where South Carolina treats them as ordinary income. The 9 percent top combined rate above the million-dollar line has no counterpart here.
If a business sale, vested stock or a large short-term gain falls in the same year as your move, the timing of the sale against the change of domicile could mean large savings. That is a question for your accountant before you sign anything.

Retirees, both directions

## Check your pension type before you decide
Most of this page runs in South Carolina's favor, so read this section twice, because it does not. Massachusetts does not tax its own contributory public pensions: a retired Massachusetts teacher, police officer or state worker collects that pension free of Massachusetts income tax. South Carolina treats it like any other pension. The deduction reduces it: once you are 65, up to $15,000 of income per person is deducted, and the retirement income deduction of up to $10,000 counts against that same $15,000 rather than adding to it. Above that amount, the pension is taxed here.
For a couple with one large Massachusetts public pension, that single line can offset much of what the property tax gives back. It does not usually make South Carolina the more expensive state, because the house, the heat and the property tax all still cost less here. It narrows the saving, and nobody should discover that in April. Run both states against your actual pension before you list the house; the calculator takes a minute and we will happily check the arithmetic with you.
Everything else lands the usual way. Social Security is untaxed in both states. Private pensions, 401(k) and IRA withdrawals face the Massachusetts flat rate with no senior exclusion, against South Carolina's deductions. Military retirement is fully exempt here at any age, which Massachusetts also honors. The retiree page covers what else changes at this stage of the move.

The rest of the bill

## The property tax and the car excise both fall here

### Property tax
Massachusetts averages about 1 percent effective with a median bill of $6,080, the bill pushed up by the values underneath it. Horry County's primary-home rate works out near 0.38 percent and the median South Carolina bill is $1,337. You apply for the primary rate yourself by May 31; the property tax page has the calculator and the deadline.

### The car excise you already pay
No warning needed here either. Massachusetts bills $25 per $1,000 of valuation, the same 2.5 percent in every town. Horry County taxes vehicles on value too, and the working bill is smaller for most movers. It is about $362 a year on a $30,000 car in the unincorporated county, or about $458 inside the City of Myrtle Beach, plus a $50 road fee. A one-time $250 fee applies when an out-of-state title first registers. The checklist has the 45-day order of operations.

### Sales tax rises
Massachusetts charges 6.25 percent and exempts groceries and clothing under $175. Here it is 8 percent in the county and 9 percent inside the City of Myrtle Beach, and we would rather be honest with you about that: on most purchases the tax is higher. The grocery run is the exception both ways: groceries are untaxed in Horry County and everyday goods price lower here than in Massachusetts on the federal price index, so the cart itself usually costs less. Clothing loses its exemption, which is fair to know before the first back-to-school shopping.

First hand

## What one Boston retiree did with a $450,000 sale
A friend of ours ran a Boston hotel for years. He retired with about $100,000 saved, sold his Massachusetts house for about $450,000, and bought three condos in one oceanfront building here. Then he decided to manage the rentals himself instead of hiring it out.
The three units grossed over $120,000 a year, and about half of that came through as profit after dues, cleaning and the rest. Those are his own numbers, and they are not a promise. The market-wide ranges, from five data vendors, are on our Airbnb income page , and his units sit at the strong end of them. The part worth translating is what $60,000 of profit means here: on the same index our cost of living calculator runs, $60,000 in Myrtle Beach spends like about $69,000 in Boston.
He works fewer hours than the forty he left behind, and he spends them where he lives: mornings on the sand, afternoons at the pool deck of the building he owns in, evenings with friends he made here. His friends up north saw how well he was doing and how happy he was, and it changed their plans too. Several bought oceanfront condos of their own through us, some moved down themselves, and today he helps manage fourteen units. He came here to retire quietly and built a business he loves instead. We helped him learn this market and introduced him around when he landed, and he became a friend well beyond the work. We are proud of what he has built.
His figures as he shared them, rounded. Condo buildings differ on rental use and financing; the building directory and condotel financing page show how.

Common questions

## Massachusetts to Myrtle Beach FAQ

### Is South Carolina cheaper than Massachusetts?
On housing, dramatically: a typical home costs close to half. The income tax rates are nearer than people expect, 5 percent flat there against 5.21 percent top here. South Carolina's deduction of up to $30,000 for a couple, the property tax at less than half the bill, the smaller car excise and no estate tax all move the total the same direction.

### If I move to South Carolina but keep a house in Massachusetts, does the Massachusetts estate tax still apply?
To the house, yes. Massachusetts taxes real estate and tangible property located in Massachusetts even when the owner dies domiciled elsewhere, and the $2 million filing trigger counts your total worldwide estate. Your investment and retirement accounts, once you are domiciled in South Carolina, are outside the Massachusetts estate tax. Selling the old house completes the exit.

### What is the Massachusetts estate tax and does South Carolina have one?
Massachusetts taxes estates above $2 million, one of the lowest thresholds in the country, with a $99,600 credit for deaths on or after January 1, 2023. A paid-off house plus retirement accounts crosses $2 million without anyone feeling rich. South Carolina has no estate tax and no inheritance tax; where you are domiciled at death decides which rules apply.

### Does Massachusetts or South Carolina tax Social Security?
Neither taxes Social Security. The difference is everything after it. Massachusetts taxes private pensions, 401(k) and IRA withdrawals at its flat rate with no senior exclusion. South Carolina deducts up to $15,000 of income per person at 65 and older, with the retirement income deduction of up to $10,000 counting against that same $15,000. Military retirement is fully exempt in South Carolina.

### I have a Massachusetts government pension. Should I know something first?
Yes, and it runs against the move: Massachusetts does not tax its own contributory public pensions, but South Carolina taxes them like any pension past its deductions. For a retired Massachusetts teacher or state worker, that single pension line can offset the other savings. Run both states' math on your actual pension before you list the house.

### What happens to my car excise tax?
It gets smaller for most movers. Massachusetts charges a fixed $25 per $1,000 of valuation, 2.5 percent, everywhere in the state. Horry County taxes vehicles on value too, at an effective bite closer to half that: about $362 a year on a $30,000 car in the unincorporated county, plus a $50 road fee and a one-time $250 fee at first registration.

### How much does a house cost in Myrtle Beach compared with Massachusetts?
A typical home here costs about $342,000 against a Massachusetts statewide average of about $669,000 on the same July 2026 Zillow measure, close to double. Greater Boston averages more than that. See how much further every dollar goes here compared with your hometown on our cost of living calculator.

# Why everyone is moving to Myrtle Beach: four reasons, told with numbers.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 1, 2026
About 15,000 households a year move to the Myrtle Beach area: a typical home near $342,000, low taxes on a primary home, and a coast that stays warm into October.

The short answer

## Four reasons, told with numbers
People move here for the same four reasons in different orders. A typical home costs about $342,000 while the states our buyers come from average $418,000 to $669,000 on the same measure. South Carolina taxes are among the friendliest in the country for a primary home: property tax near 0.38 percent in Horry County, Social Security never taxed, no estate tax. The coast works twelve months, with the ocean warm into October and winters mild enough that one of our team rides his motorcycle into December. Jobs, stores, hospitals and neighborhoods are being built at the same time, so arriving does not mean settling for less.
The numbers behind that paragraph: the Census Bureau ranked this metro among the fastest growing in the country in March 2026. The IRS counted about 15,000 households arriving in a single year, with about 2.5 times the income of the households leaving. Employment grew 9.1 percent from 2019 to 2025 against 5.1 percent nationally. Each figure is sourced on its own page, and this page links them all.

From the Northeast

## Why Northeasterners move to Myrtle Beach
New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Connecticut and Massachusetts send us the same story with different numbers: sell a house that costs too much to keep, in a place that taxes too much of everything, and buy the coast outright. A Massachusetts average home sale is close to double a home here. New Jersey property tax bills fall by thousands a year. Connecticut retirees stop watching the income lines that decide whether their Social Security is taxed, because here it never is.
One of our Massachusetts buyers, a retired Boston hotel manager, turned a $450,000 house sale into three oceanfront condos and a working beach life his friends came down to copy; his story is on the Massachusetts page . The full math, state by state: New York , New Jersey , Pennsylvania , Connecticut and Massachusetts .

From the Midwest

## Why Midwesterners move to Myrtle Beach
Ohio buyers, including one of our team, tend to name two things first. The paycheck stops losing its city slice, because South Carolina has no local income tax anywhere, while most Ohio cities take one or two percent of every check. Weather is the other. The nearest long-term weather station here records 111 clear days a year against 66 for Cleveland. Winters here are mild enough that the beach stays a daily option.
One team member's own move, with the vehicle tax that surprised him and the winters that did not, is written out on the Ohio page , and the weather page carries every season in government numbers.

From the Carolinas and the South

## Why Southerners love Myrtle Beach
More people move here from North Carolina than from any other state, and the reason is simple: this is their beach already. Charlotte is about three and a half hours, Raleigh under four, and a family that has vacationed here for twenty years eventually does the math on owning the week instead of renting it. The sale of an inland Carolina home buys more coast here than most people expect.
Virginians arrive with their own version: our Virginia Beach buyers tell us they wanted a smaller, faster growing coast where the money goes further, and they keep their respect for the military and government careers Virginia gave them. The math for both: North Carolina and Virginia .

The part nobody prints

## What movers say after a year here
The quotes we collect from our own buyers say more than the statistics. Nobody here parties like Miami, but people here are enjoying their money. Common questions

## Why Myrtle Beach FAQ

### Why is everyone moving to Myrtle Beach?
The same four reasons, in different orders. A typical home is near $342,000 while the places movers come from average $418,000 to $669,000. South Carolina taxes are among the lowest in the country for a primary home. The coast stays warm into October. There is enough growth that work and new construction keep up. The IRS counted about 15,000 households moving into Horry County in a single year.

### Is Myrtle Beach growing that fast?
Yes. The Census Bureau ranked this metro among the fastest growing in the country in its March 2026 release. Employment here grew 9.1 percent from 2019 to 2025 against 5.1 percent nationally. The households arriving reported about 2.5 times the income of the households leaving on the IRS migration file.

### Where do most people moving to Myrtle Beach come from?
North Carolina is the single biggest source, right next door. After that come New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Maryland, Virginia, Connecticut and Massachusetts. We wrote a full tax and price comparison for each of those moves, state by state.

### Is Myrtle Beach a good place to live year round?
For most of our buyers, yes, and we keep an honest page on exactly that question, including the parts people leave over: summers are humid, a quarter of the jobs follow the tourist season, and you will want a car. The beach, the prices and the taxes are what they stay for.

### Why do retirees move to Myrtle Beach?
Social Security is never taxed in South Carolina at any income, and retirement deductions here have no income test. Military retirement is fully exempt, owner-occupied property tax is among the lowest in the country, and there is no estate or inheritance tax. Then the ocean stays warm enough to swim into October.

### Why are investors buying in Myrtle Beach?
Millions of visitors a year rent somewhere to sleep, and oceanfront condos sell at prices northern buyers compare with parking spaces back home. Our Airbnb income page carries the real revenue ranges from five data vendors, and the building directory shows which buildings finance.
