Common Questions

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I still invest here if my property can’t be a short-term rental?
Yes, and this is one of the most useful workarounds on the Grand Strand. Many Myrtle Beach residential zones (and plenty of HOAs) don’t allow Airbnb-style short-term rentals. South Carolina’s 90-day threshold is a tax rule: stays under 90 days are subject to the state accommodations tax. It does not override local zoning. Cities, counties and HOAs set their own minimum lease terms, and those minimums vary, so a 90-day lease is not automatically permitted where nightly rentals are banned. Mid-term tenants such as traveling nurses, remote workers and October-to-March snowbirds are a common way to cash-flow a property in those zones. Before you count on it, confirm the minimum lease term in that city’s ordinance and the HOA covenants for the specific address. Run any address through the analyzer to compare the long-term and mid-term numbers.

### What does the long-term rental analyzer calculate?
For any Grand Strand address you enter, it estimates property value, market rent , DSCR, cap rate, net operating income, monthly cash flow, cash-on-cash return, and appreciation, and it flags nearby permit activity.

### What is DSCR and why does it matter?
Debt-Service Coverage Ratio is net operating income divided by annual debt service. Investor lenders typically look for 1.20 or higher. It tells you whether the rent comfortably covers the loan.

### What cap rate is realistic for a Myrtle Beach long-term rental?
As of July 2026, a Horry County rental bought in the cheaper third of the market returns 4.2 to 7.5 percent a year after costs with a property manager, and 5.1 to 8.8 percent without one. Dividing the same rent by the typical value of every home in the area gives a much lower number, because most of those homes are not rentals. The rental returns page has the figure for each area.

### Are the numbers an appraisal?
No. They are an actual screening estimate to compare deals quickly. Confirm with comparable sales, inspections, and a licensed agent before making an offer.

Short-Term Rentals

# Short-term rental investing in Myrtle Beach

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Chapter3 Realty · Updated October 4, 2026

Short-term rental investing on the Grand Strand works only where you can legally run one, priced on real seasonal numbers, with the 2026 rule changes by city.

The real numbers

## What Grand Strand short-term rentals earn

The Grand Strand is intensely seasonal. Occupancy on a typical vacation rental is in the teens to low 30s percent in the dead of winter and into the 80s or low 90s at the July peak . The blended annual average is roughly in the 45 to 55 percent range. Average daily rates swing the same way, high in summer, soft in the off-season. The exact curve depends heavily on where you buy. An oceanfront building in Garden City or Surfside spikes hard in summer and empties out in winter. A marsh or golf market like Murrells Inlet or Pawleys Island has a gentler peak with a stronger shoulder season. The published market-wide numbers, by area and percentile, are in our Airbnb income report .

We publish a month-by-month occupancy estimate on every one of our neighborhood pages , and when you are serious about a specific property, we build the real numbers for that exact address. Treat any blended annual figure with suspicion; the season you can book determines whether a deal works.

Legality first

## Short-term rental rules change street by street

Where you can legally run a short-term rental is the single biggest factor in a Grand Strand STR deal, and it changes by town and even by zone. South Carolina defines a short-term rental as any stay under 90 days . Inside the City of Myrtle Beach, most traditional residential neighborhoods are not zoned for short-term rentals at all, with the exception of the RMV (Residential Multifamily Visitor) zone and a small number of grandfathered homes. North Myrtle Beach requires licensing and enforces it, while much of unincorporated Horry County is more permissive.

A beautiful house in the wrong zone is not an Airbnb, no matter how good the numbers look. We confirm the zoning and any HOA short-term-rental rules for a specific property before you ever make an offer.
Two local rules matter here. In the City of Myrtle Beach, a rule covers the commercial zones between Kings Highway and the ocean. There, a unit in a short-term rental building with more than two units cannot be leased for 90 days or more. The exit from nightly rental to a yearly lease is not available there. A unit that held a long-term rental license when the rule was adopted can keep renting long-term while that license stays active. In North Myrtle Beach, a short-term rental needs a city business license, renewed every year. The city does not require a rental permit, an inspection or a local agent.
The most common failure we watch is self-managing from another state and hiring the cheapest cleaner available. At best a bad cleaner costs you reviews. We have seen theft and real damage. Cleaning is trusted, skilled work: check references and pay for reliability, or hire a manager who does.
The rentals that stay booked pick one guest and build for that guest: golf groups, families with young children, traveling workers, or house hunters visiting before a move. The theme shows in the furniture, the photos and the listing text, and the calendar fills because that group has few better options.

The workaround

## Mid-term rentals: the 90-day strategy where nightly rentals are banned

If a property you love sits in a zone where nightly rentals are banned, you are not necessarily out of options. Because South Carolina only counts a stay under 90 days as short-term, renting to mid-term tenants on 90-day-plus leases , traveling nurses, remote workers, and October-to-March snowbirds, stays outside the short-term-rental rules and the accommodations tax. It is a common way to cash-flow a property in a zone where an Airbnb is not allowed. Run any address through our investment analyzer to compare the long-term and mid-term numbers.

Financing

## Financing a short-term rental (and a condotel)

A lot of the best oceanfront STR candidates are condotels or non-warrantable condos that ordinary lenders will not touch, including buildings in active litigation . How these loans work, and what they cost, is covered in our condotel financing guide ; whether the address may legally run as a short-term rental at all is covered in STR rules by city . Our lending partner, BrickWood Mortgage (NMLS #189497) , works with us daily, so we can walk you through the paths that work for these properties. Those include DSCR loans that qualify the property on its rental income instead of your tax returns, and non-warrantable or portfolio financing for the buildings conventional loans decline.

How we check it

For any property you are serious about, we run a full analysis: projected short-term revenue, and average daily rate and occupancy by the month. From those we calculate net operating income, cap rate, cash-on-cash return, and expected appreciation. We also check the zoning and HOA rules that decide whether you can run an STR at all. It is the same building study we run on every deal.

Common Questions

## Frequently asked questions

### Can you Airbnb in Myrtle Beach?
It depends on the exact zone. Most traditional residential neighborhoods inside the City of Myrtle Beach are not zoned for short-term rentals, except the RMV zone and a few grandfathered homes. North Myrtle Beach requires a license, and much of unincorporated Horry County is more permissive. Always confirm the zoning and HOA rules for the specific property.

### How much does a Myrtle Beach short-term rental make?
It is highly seasonal. Occupancy commonly runs from the teens or 20s percent in winter to the 80s or low 90s at the July peak, blending to roughly 45 to 55 percent for the year, and rates swing the same way. The right number is the one built from the specific building and season, which is what we calculate for you.

### What is the 90-day rule?
South Carolina counts a stay under 90 days as a short-term rental. Renting to tenants on 90-day-plus leases (mid-term or snowbird stays) falls outside the short-term-rental rules and the accommodations tax, which is a common way to cash-flow a property in a zone where nightly rentals are banned.

### Can you finance a short-term rental or a condotel?
Yes. Many oceanfront STR candidates are condotels or non-warrantable condos that ordinary lenders decline. Our preferred lender handles DSCR loans that qualify on rental income and non-warrantable or portfolio financing for those buildings.

# Short-term or long-term rental in Myrtle Beach? Two to three times the gross, and the costs.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Chapter3 Realty · Updated October 27, 2026
Short-term rentals in Myrtle Beach gross two to three times more than a long-term lease but cost more to run and finance; long-term rentals net less and are steadier.

## The revenue side: what each strategy produces

A Myrtle Beach short-term rental makes its money through average daily rate times occupancy, and both numbers swing hard with the calendar. Summer weeks on the oceanfront command premium nightly rates, shoulder seasons soften, and winter occupancy thins out everywhere except the snowbird buildings. Gross revenue on a well-located Airbnb or vacation rental can run well past what the same unit would collect on a lease, but gross is not the number that pays the mortgage. Market-wide gross and net figures: the Airbnb income report .

A long-term rental trades that ceiling for a floor. A 12-month lease produces the same deposit every month, tenant demand comes from the year-round economy rather than tourism, and rent growth compounds quietly in the background. There is also a middle path many Grand Strand owners use: furnished monthly rentals to snowbirds from October through March, then weekly vacation rates in peak summer. That hybrid smooths the seasonality curve without committing to either extreme.
Not sure which way a property should run? Send it over and we will model both, and check what the building and the city allow.
Have us model it Call 854.333.2135

## The full expense list for each rental strategy

Short-term rental listings get shared for their revenue, never their operating statement. Between full-service hosting, cleaning and turnover, utilities the owner carries, linens and furnishing replacement, platform fees, and accommodations taxes, all-in expense ratios on Grand Strand short-term rentals commonly land between 45 and 60 percent of gross before debt service.

Long-term rentals carry a lighter load. Taxes, insurance, maintenance, and management typically absorb 35 to 45 percent of collected rent, there are fewer moving parts to break, and a single annual turn replaces fifty checkouts. Net operating income is where the two strategies get honest with each other, and the gap is usually much narrower than the gross numbers suggest.

## Financing: where DSCR loans fit, and the condotel wrinkle

Most Myrtle Beach investment purchases today are financed on DSCR loans, which qualify the property instead of the borrower. The lease income carries the application, no tax returns or DTI calculation enter the picture, and the loan can close in an LLC, which matters to investors building a portfolio or buying through a 1031 exchange. Short-term rental financing exists on similar rails, but the lender is underwriting a revenue projection rather than a signed lease, so reserves, experience, and pricing all get tighter.

The building itself can also pick your financing for you. Many oceanfront towers operate as condotels, and those fall outside conventional and standard DSCR guidelines entirely, which pushes buyers toward specialty lenders or cash regardless of which rental strategy they planned.

## The metrics that settle it: cap rate, cash-on-cash, break-even occupancy

Run the same property through both lenses before writing an offer. Cap rate, the net operating income against the price, compares the property to every other use of the same money without financing noise. Cash-on-cash return tells you what your actual down payment earns once the DSCR loan is layered in. For the short-term scenario, add break-even occupancy: the occupancy level where revenue covers every operating cost plus the mortgage. If a unit needs 70 percent year-round occupancy just to tread water in a market that delivers seasonal troughs, the lease scenario is quietly outperforming it.

## Rules, ordinances, and HOA fine print

Short-term rental permission on the Grand Strand is decided at three layers, and all three need checking before an offer, not after. Municipal ordinances differ between Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach, Surfside Beach, and unincorporated Horry County, including zoning overlays and permit requirements. HOA documents add their own layer: minimum lease terms, rental caps, and owner-occupancy quotas appear in master deeds across the area, and they override whatever the city allows. Buyers trading in through a 1031 exchange should confirm rental-use rules early, since a failed strategy assumption inside an exchange window gets expensive.

## Choosing for a specific property

Strategy debates end at the address level. Run the numbers both ways: the long-term rental analyzer returns DSCR, cap rate, NOI, and cash flow for any Grand Strand address, and the STR revenue atlas shows what short-term rentals gross around it, building by building. When both scenarios are written down, speak to a licensed agent about the specific property and its rules.

Common Questions

## Frequently asked questions

### Which earns more in Myrtle Beach, short-term or long-term rental?
Short-term rentals often produce higher gross revenue in tourist heavy, beach proximate areas, but with seasonality, higher operating costs, and more management. Long-term rentals earn less gross but offer steadier, lower-touch cash flow.

### Is short-term or long-term rental easier to finance?
Long-term rentals are generally simpler to finance, including DSCR loans based on lease income. Short-term rental financing exists, but underwriters look harder at seasonality and management.

### Which strategy carries less risk?
Long-term rentals carry less revenue volatility and fewer regulatory surprises. Short-term rentals can out-earn them but are exposed to tourism swings and to changing local short-term-rental rules.

### How do I decide between them?
Match the strategy to the property, the location&#x27;s short-term-rental rules, your financing, and how hands-on you want to be, then run both scenarios through the analyzers.
One advantage rarely shows up in the numbers: control. A short-term rental turns over every few days, so you or your manager are inside the unit almost every week and find a leak, a failing HVAC unit, or damage within days. A long-term tenant can occupy the same unit for a year with limited access, and small problems compound unseen until move-out. Renting nightly puts someone in the property to clean and check it every week, which protects both its condition and its resale value.

We coordinate between your attorney, the buyer's side, and your lender (if applicable) so there are no surprises at the table. You sign; you get wired.

SC Non-Resident Withholding

When a non-resident sells, the buyer must withhold South Carolina's top individual rate, 5.21% for 2026 , or 5% for a corporation. The closing attorney often does this for the buyer and sends it to the SC Department of Revenue.

This is a significant surprise for many out-of-state owners who discover it at the closing table. We explain it during your pricing consultation so you can plan around it. The withheld amount is credited against your SC income tax liability and is not an additional tax.

Vacation Home, Condotel, and STR Sellers

### "I have rental bookings through next summer. Does that complicate the sale?"

It doesn't have to. Under South Carolina Code Section 27-50-250, a buyer takes title subject to existing vacation rental agreements for periods beginning within 90 days of deed recording. Bookings are transferred or honored; rental income is pro-rated at closing.

Rental history is a strong selling point for investor buyers. We quantify it: trailing 12-month gross revenue, occupancy rate, and ADR. ADR is average daily rate, the average nightly price a rental earns. We put it in front of buyers who are evaluating cap rates along with list price.

- → Condotel financing limitations explained to buyers before offers (FHA/VA ineligible on most)

- → STR revenue data packaged as an investment package for investor outreach

- → HOA financial health and special assessment review before listing

South Carolina Seller Costs

## Know your net before you list.

South Carolina sellers face a specific set of closing costs that differ from most markets. Before you list, we walk through every fee that applies to your specific sale so you know exactly what you will walk away with.

Deed Stamps (Transfer Tax)

$3.70 per $1,000 of sale price, paid by the seller at closing. A $350,000 sale = $1,295 in deed stamps.

Attorney Fees and Title

SC mandatory attorney state. Seller's attorney fees typically $500 to $1,200. Closing attorneys coordinate the title search, deed recording, and proceeds disbursement.

HOA Estoppel and Transfer Fees

Condo HOAs typically charge $100 to $400 for estoppel letters and transfer fees. Some Grand Strand HOAs (Kingston Plantation, Barefoot Resort) charge higher. Confirm before listing.

Non-Resident Seller Withholding

If you live outside SC, the buyer must withhold at South Carolina's top individual rate, 5.21% for 2026, or 5% for a corporation. The closing attorney often does this for the buyer and sends it to the state. This is not an extra tax. It is credited against your SC income tax, and most long-term sellers get part of it back.

Commission Transparency

Listing-side commission is fully negotiable and not set by law. Buyer-side compensation, if offered, is also negotiable and disclosed in writing per the August 2024 NAR settlement requirements. We discuss every option before you sign.

Seller FAQ

## Every question sellers ask us. Answered honestly.

Myrtle Beach's market has specific mechanics most sellers discover too late. These answers cover what you'll need to know before you list.

Find out what your home's worth →

### What is my Myrtle Beach home worth in 2026?
Your home's value depends on property type, exact location, condition, floor or view if applicable, and recent comparable sales in your specific neighborhood or building. The single-family median across the Grand Strand was about $360,000 in mid-2026, and the condo median about $244,000. Oceanfront units command significant premiums. The most accurate way to know is a Comparative Market Analysis from a local listing agent. Zillow and Redfin AVMs are routinely off by 10 to 25% in Myrtle Beach's segmented condo and condotel market because they cannot account for view, floor, building amenities, rental program status, or HOA financial health.

### Is Myrtle Beach a buyer's or seller's market right now?
Myrtle Beach is balanced and leaning buyer-friendly in 2026. Single-family inventory is at approximately 4.3 months of supply, and condos are at about 7.6 months. Average days on market is about 121 days for properties not priced and marketed correctly, and the sale-to-list ratio is around 96%. Sellers who price accurately and market well are still closing. Overpricing by 5 to 10% is the single most common and costly mistake in this market.

### When is the best time to sell a house in Myrtle Beach?
February through July is historically the strongest selling window in Myrtle Beach. Peak buyer activity runs March through June. Listings launched in late winter typically see more showings, faster offers, and better list-to-sale ratios than fall and winter listings. Vacation buyers tour in spring, retirees often plan summer moves, and families want to close before the school year starts.

### How long does it take to sell a house in Myrtle Beach?
The market average is about 121 days on market. That number reflects homes that sit because of overpricing or weak marketing. Well-priced, well-presented homes in the right sub-market regularly sell in 30 to 60 days. Condos take longer on average due to higher inventory at about 7.6 months supply. Pricing it correctly from day one is the single biggest factor in how fast your home sells.

### Can I sell my Myrtle Beach home from out of state without flying down?
Yes. South Carolina permits e-signature on listing agreements and remote online notarization in most residential transactions. Your closing attorney can prepare a Power of Attorney if needed. We coordinate photography, lockbox, showings, repairs, and inspection access. You receive weekly written and video market updates. The vast majority of our listings are from out-of-state owners who never need to travel for the sale.

### What are the closing costs for sellers in South Carolina?
South Carolina sellers typically pay the following. Deed stamps at $3.70 per $1,000 of sale price. Seller's attorney fees, typically $500 to $1,200. Pro-rated property taxes. Mortgage payoff and recording fees. Any HOA estoppel or transfer fees, $100 to $400 at most Grand Strand HOAs. The negotiated listing commission. Out-of-state sellers are also subject to South Carolina nonresident withholding at the state's top individual rate, 5.21% for 2026 sales, or 5% for a corporation. State law puts the duty to withhold on the buyer, and the closing attorney often does it for the buyer. It is credited against the tax on your SC return.

### Do I need an attorney to sell my house in South Carolina?
Yes. South Carolina is a mandatory attorney state. A licensed South Carolina attorney must conduct the closing, perform the title search, and record the deed. This applies whether the buyer pays cash or finances. We work with several experienced Grand Strand closing attorneys and can recommend one based on your transaction type.

### How much commission do I pay to sell my home in 2026?
Real estate commissions are fully negotiable and not set by law. Following the August 2024 NAR settlement, sellers are no longer required to compensate the buyer's agent through the MLS. Sellers and listing brokers negotiate the listing-side commission separately. Any compensation offered to a buyer's broker is disclosed in writing and approved by the seller in advance. We explain every option and the trade-offs for your specific property and market conditions before you sign anything.

### Do I have to pay the buyer's agent commission?
No. Post-NAR settlement, you decide if and how much to offer a buyer's agent at listing time or in response to specific offers. Many sellers in Myrtle Beach still choose to offer buyer-broker compensation as an incentive to widen their buyer pool. This is a strategic decision we walk through with you based on your property type and target buyer profile.

### What is a CMA and how is it different from a Zillow Zestimate?
A Comparative Market Analysis is a price opinion prepared by a local listing agent based on recent comparable sales, active competition, expired listings, your home's specific features and condition, and current market conditions. Zillow and Redfin estimates are algorithmic and routinely off by 10 to 25% in Myrtle Beach because they cannot account for view, floor, building amenities, rental program status, or HOA financial health. In a segmented coastal market, a human CMA is the only reliable way to price correctly.

### Should I sell my Myrtle Beach condo if I'm in a rental program?
Yes, selling with active bookings is routine. Under South Carolina Code Section 27-50-250, the buyer takes title subject to existing vacation rental agreements for periods beginning within 90 days of deed recording. Bookings are typically transferred or honored, and rental income is pro-rated at closing. We package your rental history as an investment asset, not a complication, and target investor buyers who want yield data.

### What do I need to disclose when selling a house in South Carolina?
South Carolina's Residential Property Condition Disclosure Act (SC Code Section 27-50-10) requires sellers to deliver a written disclosure based on actual knowledge before contract execution. This covers structure, roof, plumbing, electrical, HVAC, water systems, environmental hazards, prior repairs, and HOA matters. Knowing omissions or false statements can result in actual damages, court costs, and attorney fees, with a three-year liability window post-sale. Full transparency is always the safer and less expensive path.

### What if I inherited a house in Myrtle Beach?
Inherited property sales are routine. The first step is confirming who has authority to sell, typically the executor named in the will or a court-appointed administrator. We coordinate with your probate attorney, manage access and cleanout remotely, and price based on current market value. Capital gains on inherited property are generally assessed against the stepped-up basis at date of death, which often results in minimal tax for heirs. We recommend confirming this with your estate attorney or CPA before closing.

### Should I make repairs before listing my Myrtle Beach home?
Strategic, not exhaustive, repair is the goal. Over-improvement rarely returns the investment in a buyer's market. We walk every property before listing and recommend a targeted prep list focused on three things. Items a home inspector will flag, cosmetic items with high visual return (paint, flooring, entry landscaping), and condition-of-systems items that affect appraisal (HVAC, water heater age). We do not recommend speculative renovations in this market.

### What happens if my home doesn't sell?
If your home is not generating showings or offers in the first 14 to 30 days, it is a pricing or marketing signal, not a market problem. We re-evaluate weekly, share showing feedback transparently, and discuss repositioning options including price adjustment, marketing refresh, or a temporary withdrawal and relaunch. We do not run passive listings. If the data points to a pricing conversation, we have it, before you lose another 30 days chasing a number the market will not support.

### Can I sell my house as-is in Myrtle Beach?
Yes. Our off-market investor buyers usually prefer as-is: no repairs, no showings, no public listing. If the house passes our investment analysis, an investor typically buys within about half the average time on market. A retail listing usually nets more, so we show you both numbers first.

### How fast can I sell my house in Myrtle Beach?
On the open market it depends on the price and the property type, and we track current days on market for your exact segment. Off market is faster: when a house passes our investment analysis, an investor usually closes in about half the average time on market.

### Should I list my house or sell it off market?
List it when you want the most money and can wait for the right buyer. Sell off market when you want a fast, sure sale. We run your numbers both ways, show you the difference side by side, and you decide.

The Out-of-State Buyer Advantage

## Why they pay more and why that matters to you.

A buyer from New Jersey looking at a $380,000 Myrtle Beach home is comparing it to a $680,000 home in their own market. To them, your property is a bargain. They're not anchored to Grand Strand price history. They're anchored to what this lifestyle costs back home. Selling an inherited Grand Strand property from out of state is common; that process is covered in our inherited house guide . Out-of-state sellers also face a state withholding at closing; the numbers are in our capital gains and withholding guide .

They also move faster. Out-of-state buyers have already done their research, often visited the market once or twice, and are ready to commit. They're not waiting for the perfect price drop. They're waiting for the right property to appear in front of them.

The local buyer problem

Local buyers know every comp. They anchor to last month's sale two streets over. Out-of-state buyers anchor to what they're escaping. That psychological difference shows up directly in offer price and negotiation behavior.

The Season is Closing

## Out-of-state buyers are most active right now, through early fall.

Myrtle Beach's peak real estate season mirrors its tourism season. Buyers from feeder states plan their visits in spring and summer, make decisions on the ground, and want to close before fall. Once October arrives, buyer traffic from the Northeast and Midwest drops sharply, and it doesn't return until the following February.

A property listed in July still in contract negotiation has a buyer. A property that misses the summer window enters the off-season competing for a thinner buyer pool at lower seasonal urgency.

Common Questions

## Out-of-state marketing FAQ.

### Why do out-of-state buyers matter to Grand Strand sellers?
Out-of-state buyers make up a large share of Grand Strand demand. They shop online first and often carry equity from higher-priced markets, which makes broad digital marketing more valuable than local-only exposure.

### Do out-of-state buyers make offers without visiting first?
Yes, and more frequently than most sellers expect. With cinematic video, 3D virtual tours, and detailed neighborhood context, remote buyers routinely submit competitive offers sight-unseen. They often visit once for inspection, then close remotely. In vacation markets like Myrtle Beach where buyers already know the destination, this is especially common.

### Why would an out-of-state buyer pay more than a local buyer?
Out-of-state buyers anchor their price expectations to their home market, not Grand Strand comps. A buyer from Bergen County, NJ where median prices exceed $650K perceives a $380K Myrtle Beach home as underpriced. They also feel urgency that local buyers don't. They're on a trip, have limited time, and don't want to lose a property they've traveled to see.

### How does Chapter3 specifically reach buyers in other states?
We run Meta and Google paid campaigns geographically targeted to the top six feeder states: NC, NY, NJ, PA, OH, and VA. We build custom audiences based on buyers who've searched Myrtle Beach properties or engaged with coastal real estate content. For investor-eligible properties, we also run targeted placement toward buyers researching short-term rental investments, which draws a different buyer profile than residential relocation campaigns.

### Does the season matter for attracting out-of-state buyers?
Significantly. Most out-of-state buyers plan trips to evaluate properties in spring and early summer, then want to close before fall. A property that enters the market in June and attracts a buyer in July is on track. A property that misses the summer window enters fall competing for a buyer pool that has largely returned home and won't resume active search until the following February.

### What makes a listing most appealing to an out-of-state buyer specifically?
Three things above all else: exceptional visual media, a clear lifestyle narrative, and, for investment-eligible properties, quantified income potential. Video beats photos for remote buyers. The lifestyle narrative covers proximity to beach, golf, dining, and boating. Out-of-state buyers are doing research on a screen, not walking the neighborhood. Every additional piece of compelling media is one more reason to write an offer before flying down.

## Start from what you are trying to do
Nine submarkets is a lot to read through. Find the line that matches your plan and start on that page.
I want the highest nightly revenue per property
Start with Murrells Inlet and Surfside Beach . They lead the Strand on average annual revenue and nightly rate, because the south end is mostly whole houses rather than one- and two-bedroom condos.

I want the lowest price to get in
Start with Conway and Little River . Both are yearly-rental markets inland or up the coast, with the lowest entry prices on the Strand and tenant demand that does not depend on the summer.

I want schools and a family neighborhood
Start with Carolina Forest . It is the master-planned inland corridor, the HOAs require long leases rather than nightly stays, and tenant demand follows the school attendance zones.

I want the easiest property to buy, rent and resell
Start with Myrtle Beach or North Myrtle Beach . They hold the great majority of the Strand's listings, so there is always inventory, always comparable sales, and always a buyer when you sell.

I want quiet, and I am buying for myself as much as for yield
Start with Pawleys Island . Higher nightly rates, lower occupancy, an older and higher-end housing stock, and a buyer pool motivated as much by using the place as renting it.

I want to be near the water without oceanfront pricing
Start with Garden City . The peninsula has ocean on one side and the inlet on the other, and creek-side homes with dock access sit well below the oceanfront blocks.

Conway, SC

# Conway, SC: the Grand Strand's inland value market. A river town about 25 minutes from the beach.

- Beach 25 min drive

- Airport 27 min drive

- University In the city

- Hospital 10 min drive

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 2, 2026
In Conway you get Main Street and the Riverwalk downtown, a university and a hospital inside the city, and the biggest lots at its north edge.

The short answer
Conway is a river town with an old downtown on the Waccamaw River, a university and a hospital inside the city, and the beach about 25 minutes away. A house here resells for about $60,000 less than across Horry County.
Most Conway addresses are outside the city itself. Only a few places are in the flood maps, near the river, Crabtree Swamp and Kingston Lake.

## What is it like to live in Conway, SC?
Conway is a small city on the Waccamaw River, said WAH-kuh-maw. Much of downtown was built in the early 1900s, after a fire, and its streets have old live oaks.
The Riverwalk is a path of about 1.5 miles along the river, with benches and a kayak launch. It starts about 3 minutes by car from the center of town. At Riverfront Park beside it are a public boat landing with floating docks, a playground built like an old river steamboat, and rocking chairs under a gazebo.
Photo: Pubdog
The boardwalk along the Waccamaw River, at the edge of downtown Conway.
Conway was laid out in 1732, as Kingston, and later named Conwayborough for General Robert Conway of the state militia.
City Hall on Main Street was finished in 1825 as the county courthouse. Its design is credited to Robert Mills, who designed the Washington Monument.
Photo: Pollinator at en.wikipedia
Conway City Hall on Main Street, once the county courthouse.
Coastal Carolina University is inside the city, about 10 minutes from downtown. It enrolled more than 11,000 students in fall 2024, a record for the school. Horry-Georgetown Technical College has its Conway campus on US 501, and Conway Medical Center is about 10 minutes from downtown.
The city is growing fast. By Census estimates it grew about 22 percent since 2020, the seventh fastest among South Carolina cities and towns of 10,000 people or more.
The beach is about 25 minutes away by car, and the airport about 27.

Drive times by car from downtown Conway, without traffic. Map data: U.S. Census Bureau TIGER/Line; Horry County GIS.

## Is a Conway address inside the city of Conway?
Usually not. Only a little more than 1 in 4 homes with a Conway mailing address is inside the city limits. The rest are in the county, outside any city.
Homes with a Conway mailing address, rounded Where the home is Homes

Inside the city limits 8,300
Outside, in the county 22,000

The same is true of homes for sale. At our last count, only about 1 in 4 houses for sale with a Conway address was inside the city.

### What the city line changes
Inside the city, the property tax is about $670 a year more on a typical house you live in. The City of Conway picks up garbage, recycling and yard waste at the curb once a week for homes in the city, and the city has its own police and fire departments.
Outside the city there is no city pickup. Homes in the county, outside any city, are the only ones allowed to use the county's 25 recycling and convenience centers, where owners bring their own trash.

## Which part of Conway should you look at?
The city's homes fall into five parts. Each has something the others do not. The numbers on the map match the entries below. Each price is what a house or townhouse there usually resold for in the past year, from county deeds.

Map of the city's homes, each dot a group of homes, coloured by part of town. The dark square is Coastal Carolina University and the red cross is Conway Medical Center. Map data: Horry County GIS; U.S. Census Bureau TIGER/Line.
- 1 Downtown

- 2 Near the university, off US 501

- 3 West and south

- 4 Around Crabtree Swamp

- 5 The north edge

### 1 Downtown: a walk to Main Street and the river
Downtown is the old town on the river. Main Street, City Hall, the Riverwalk and Riverfront Park are all here. Kingston Park on Main Street has shaded tables and a fountain, and the Garden Walk off Third Avenue is a walkway with music and lights in the evening.

Photo: Pubdog
An older house under a live oak, in the downtown historic district.

Downtown here means the streets within about a mile of the center of town, on house lots of about a third of an acre. Snowhill, Mayfair, Buckwood, Highland Park and Collinswood are the largest subdivisions. Few homes here come up for sale. Those that did resold for about $275,000.
Get the homes for sale in Downtown Conway

### 2 Near the university, off US 501: the university and the hospital
Along US 501 toward the beach, the city reaches past Coastal Carolina University. Conway Medical Center, on Singleton Ridge Road, and the Conway campus of Horry-Georgetown Technical College are in this part too.

Photo: LittleT889
Kimbel Library at Coastal Carolina University, under a live oak.

Wild Wing, Coastal Point West, Kiskadee Parke and Aviary Village are the largest subdivisions, with about 1,430 homes in all, on lots of about four-tenths of an acre. Homes here resold for about $360,000. Only the north edge was higher.
Get the homes for sale in Conway near the university

### 3 West and south: the most homes, three city parks and the lowest prices
West and south of downtown, toward US 378 and US 701 South, is the largest part of the city. The Billy Gardner Recreation Complex on Mill Pond Road holds the Conway Recreation Center, with an indoor pool and walking track, plus ball fields and a playground built for children of all abilities. Smith Jones Park has an outdoor pool, and Collins Park has tennis and pickleball courts.

Rosehaven, New Castle, Oak Glenn, Woodland Lakes and Jasmine Woods are the largest subdivisions, on lots of about a quarter of an acre. Homes here resold for about $245,000, the lowest of the five parts.
Get the homes for sale in West Conway

### 4 Around Crabtree Swamp: north and northwest of downtown, with a park on Sherwood Drive
North and northwest of downtown, around Crabtree Swamp, are about 2,390 homes, most of them 2 to 4 miles out. Sherwood Park on Sherwood Drive has a playground and a sand volleyball court, and across the street a nine-hole disc golf course inside a walking track.

Midtown Village, Rivertown Row, Elmhurst, Woodcreek, Kingston Bay, Sherwood and Country Club Forest are the largest subdivisions. The lots are the smallest in the city, about a fifth of an acre, and homes resold for about $260,000.
Get the homes for sale in Conway near Crabtree Swamp

### 5 The north edge: the biggest lots in the city
At the city's north edge, 4 to 5 miles from downtown, a typical lot is about three-quarters of an acre, the largest in the city. Ridgewood West, Country Manor and Maple Hill are the largest subdivisions, with about 560 homes in all.

Few homes resold here, and the middle price was about $400,000, the highest of the five parts.
Get the homes for sale in North Conway

## Does Conway, SC flood?
A few parts do. About 95 in 100 homes in the city are outside both FEMA's high-risk zone and the land Florence's water reached in 2018. The rest are near the river, Crabtree Swamp and Kingston Lake.
By part of town, none of the homes near the university are in either flood map. Downtown and at the north edge, about 3 in 100 homes are in one. West and south, it is about 5 in 100, and around Crabtree Swamp about 1 in 10.

- Homes

- FEMA's high-risk flood zone

- Where Florence's water reached

Map of the two flood maps under the city's homes. Map data: Horry County GIS; U.S. Census Bureau TIGER/Line.
The worst flood on record came after Hurricane Florence in 2018. The river gauge at the Conway Marina read about 21 feet, its highest ever. That is the height of the river on the gauge, not the depth of water on a street. Major flooding starts at 14 feet.
Photo: SC National Guard
Floodwater on a street of houses in the Conway area after Florence.

### Why the flood comes late and stays
The flood here comes down the river, days after the storm. Florence came ashore in North Carolina, and the river at Conway was highest 12 days later.
How high the river at Conway rose on its gauge, in feet, after two hurricanes
- Florence, 2018

- Matthew, 2016

- Major flooding, 14 ft

- Flood stage, 11 ft

Daily average height on the river gauge at the Conway Marina. After Florence, the river stayed above flood stage for 29 days, 20 of them in major flood.
During Florence, the county closed 58 streets in and at the edge of the city for flooding. Long Avenue, Third Avenue, Church Street and Marina Drive stayed closed about four weeks.

### Which streets flood at each river height
The National Weather Service lists what floods as the river rises on the gauge:
River height What floods
14 feet Low areas along Long Avenue and Sherwood Drive, near Crabtree Swamp
15 feet The Conway Marina, Elm Street and Marina Drive
17 feet Main Street and Pecan Grove Boulevard may begin to flood
21 feet The US 501 Bypass may flood. Florence reached about 21 feet.

### Where Florence's water reached, by subdivision
Subdivision, and where it is Homes Florence's water reached
Sherwood, around Crabtree Swamp 98 of 126
Midland, just north of downtown 33 of 49
Pecan Grove, west and south 29 of 103
Country Club Forest, around Crabtree Swamp 21 of 57
Lakeland, just north of downtown 18 of 37

By the county's map, Florence's water did not reach large parts of Conway. No home in Rosehaven, Oak Glenn, Woodland Lakes, Rivertown Row, Kingston Bay or Snowhill is in either flood map.

### How often it happens
Of the 14 floods on record that reached major flood stage at Conway, 6 came in the last 11 years.
For Florence, flood insurance paid 109 claims in the city, and the middle claim was about $134,000. After Hurricane Matthew, the city used FEMA grants to buy 86 buildings. Land bought this way must stay open space.
Our page on how to find out if a house flooded shows every record we use.

## Do you need flood insurance in Conway, and what does it cost?
Federal law makes a lender require it only when the house is in FEMA's high-risk zone. A lender can still ask for it anywhere.
Outside the high-risk zone, a flood policy on a house usually costs about $560 to $680 a year, depending on the ZIP code.
Flood policy a year, about ZIP 29526 ZIP 29527
Outside the zone $560 $680
Inside the zone $980 $980

A new federal flood policy takes effect 30 days after the application and payment are complete, unless it is bought when a home loan is made. Buy it with the house, not when a storm is coming.

## What does it cost to own a home in Conway each year?
For a typical $265,000 house you live in inside the city, the property tax is about $1,700 a year, plus a flood policy if you want one.
Each year, for a $265,000 house What you pay Inside the city Just outside it
Property tax, a home you live in About $1,700 About $1,100, with an $89 county fee
Flood policy outside the high-risk zone, if you want one About $560 to $680 About $560 to $680
Tax and flood policy together About $2,300 to $2,400 About $1,600 to $1,700
Property tax instead, as a second home or rental About $4,300 About $3,300

Homeowners insurance is a third bill, on top of these. Its price depends on the house, its roof and the company. Our coastal insurance page explains the policies a house here can need.
South Carolina taxes a home you live in on 4 percent of its value, and a second home or rental on 6 percent. You must apply for the lower rate. Inside the city, that makes a rental's bill about 2.5 times a home's. Our property tax page shows how to apply.

## What do homes cost in Conway, SC?
A house or townhouse that resold inside the city in the past year usually went for about $265,000. Half sold for between about $220,000 and $340,000.
At that price, a house in the city is usually three bedrooms and about 1,400 square feet. That is what we found among the houses for sale inside the city near that price at our last count, about 3 in 4 of them with three bedrooms. Some were new, built in the last two years.
Builders sold about 120 new homes in the city in the same year, for about $295,000 in the middle. Few resales were condos, and those went for about $150,000.

Houses and townhouses resold by their owners, not by a builder, and not condo units. Middle price: half sold for more, half for less. Aynor had only 17 resales.
Conway is not the cheapest town in the county. Homes in Loris and Aynor, two smaller inland towns, resold for less.
At our last count, about 670 houses were for sale with a Conway address, more than half of them new construction, and about 60 on an acre or more. Our no-HOA homes guide and most affordable places include Conway.

## What do homes rent for in Conway?
HUD's fair market rent for a three-bedroom in the Conway ZIP codes is $1,630 a month. HUD counts rent and utilities together, so the rent alone is less. The figure sits a little under the middle of the market.
Bedrooms HUD fair market rent, ZIPs 29526 and 29527
Two $1,320
Three $1,630
Four $1,900

In Carolina Forest's ZIP code, the three-bedroom figure is about $600 more.
In our experience, students near the college look for the cheapest house that fits their group. People moving to be near the college pay more for a nice house close to campus.
In our experience near the college, August is the best month to find a new tenant, because new students arrive. Start marketing a month before the lease ends. Our student rental guide covers renting near Coastal Carolina.
For any address, our rental analyzer gives the rent and the costs. For nightly rentals, see what a nightly rental earns by town and the short-term rental rules by town .

## What are the pros and cons of living in Conway?
The good points are the price, the downtown and the university. The hard ones are flooding in a few places, the city tax and the drive to the beach.

### Pros

- Homes cost less than in the county as a whole, and new homes and land are for sale.

- A downtown on the river, with Main Street, the Riverwalk and Riverfront Park.

- A university and the hospital inside the city, and city trash pickup each week.

### Cons

- A few parts flood, and the river stays high for weeks.

- The city's property tax is higher than just outside it.

- The beach is a drive of about 25 minutes, not a walk.

Common questions

## Conway, SC FAQ

### Is Conway, SC a good place to live?
For a buyer who wants a river town with a downtown and a university, at prices under the county's middle, yes. The trade is the drive: the beach is about 25 minutes away by car.

### How far is Conway from Myrtle Beach?
About 25 minutes by car from downtown Conway to the beach in Myrtle Beach, without traffic, and about 27 minutes to Myrtle Beach International Airport.

### Does Conway, SC flood?
In a few places. About 95 in 100 homes in the city are outside both FEMA's high-risk zone and the land Florence's water reached; most of the rest are near the Waccamaw River, Crabtree Swamp and Kingston Lake.

### What is the property tax rate in Conway, SC?
Inside the city, a home you live in pays about $654 a year for every $100,000 of the county's value for it. Just outside the city, it pays about $368, plus an $89 county stormwater fee. A second home or rental pays about 2.5 times as much inside the city.

### How many people live in Conway, SC?
About 30,600 in 2025, by the Census Bureau's estimate, up from 24,849 at the 2020 Census.

### Is Conway, SC safe?
We do not rate any place as safe or unsafe. Inside the city limits, the City of Conway has its own police department and fire department.

### Which schools serve Conway, SC?
Horry County Schools assigns schools by address, and one of its attendance areas is named Conway. We look up the assigned schools for any house you like.

## Garden City, SC Real Estate: Beach Homes, Rentals, Flood Facts

Garden City, SC

# Garden City, SC: beach rentals with no city ordinance. One beach road between the ocean and the salt marsh.

- Beach road About 5 miles

- Fishing pier 668 feet

- MarshWalk 8 min drive

- Airport 20 min drive

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 2, 2026
Garden City is a beach community south of Myrtle Beach, with a fishing pier, houses on the marsh with docks, and quiet subdivisions inland.

The short answer
Garden City, South Carolina is a beach community between Surfside Beach and Murrells Inlet. It is not a town: the county runs it, and most of its beach road is in Georgetown County, not Horry.
For a condo on the sand, look at the ocean side by the pier. For a house with a dock, look at the marsh and the Georgetown end. For a house lived in all year, out of the high-risk flood zone, look west of Business 17.

Tell us how you will use it. We send the Garden City homes that fit.
Send me Garden City homes

## Where is Garden City, SC, and which county is it in?
Garden City sits on a strip of land between the Atlantic Ocean and a salt marsh, just south of Surfside Beach. Its beach road, Waccamaw Drive, runs down the strip to Garden City Point at the inlet. Business 17 runs inland of the marsh.
The Horry and Georgetown county line crosses the beach about a third of a mile south of the Garden City Pier. Most of Waccamaw Drive is south of the line, in Georgetown County. The county decides your property tax, your rental license and the beach rules.
Most addresses use Murrells Inlet and its ZIP code, 29576. A band at the north edge uses Surfside Beach.

The dashed line is the county line. Aerial photo: USGS, public domain. Roads and the county line: U.S. Census Bureau, Horry County and OpenStreetMap contributors.
- 1 The ocean side of Waccamaw Drive : the beach and the pier

- 2 On the marsh : docks and tidal creeks

- 3 Between the marsh and Business 17 : the most kinds of homes

- 4 West of Business 17 : subdivisions lived in all year

- 5 The Georgetown end : canals, docks and the quietest beach

## Where to buy in Garden City, SC
Garden City has five parts, and each is a different way to live at the beach. The numbers match the map above.

### 1 The ocean side of Waccamaw Drive: the beach and the pier
Here you walk out of your building onto the sand. Condo buildings and a few beach houses stand between Waccamaw Drive and the ocean, from the Surfside Beach line south past the pier. The largest buildings include Royal Garden Resort, Waters Edge Resort, Surfmaster and Atalaya Towers.
The pier is the center of this side. Its café serves breakfast. In summer, its deck bar has karaoke in the afternoons, and bands play every night at both ends of the pier, weather permitting. The arcade is there for a rainy day. A pier pass covers fishing, so no state fishing license is needed, and in summer you can fish around the clock.
U.S. government aerial photo
The ocean side by the pier from above: buildings and beach houses between Waccamaw Drive and the beach, and the salt marsh behind.
Almost every home on this side is a condo. Condos here sold for about $320,000 at the middle in the past year.
Get the condos for sale on Garden City's ocean side

### 2 On the marsh: docks and tidal creeks
Behind the beach strip is salt marsh, cut by tidal creeks that reach the inlet at Garden City Point. The houses along its edges look out over the marsh, and many have a long private dock. On the beach strip they line Dogwood Drive. On the mainland side they are on streets like Creekside Drive and Rum Gully Road.
Photo: U.S. Geological Survey
Beach houses along Waccamaw Drive, seen from over the ocean, with the salt marsh and its creeks behind them and docks on the far shore.
These are the most costly houses east of Business 17. The ones that sold in the past year went for about $1.24 million at the middle, about twice the other houses east of Business 17. Few come up for sale.
Get the marsh-front homes for sale in Garden City

### 3 Between the marsh and Business 17: the most kinds of homes
The rest of the land between the marsh and Business 17 is streets of houses, small condo buildings and manufactured homes. Its neighborhoods include Salters Cove, Mount Gilead, Myrtle Dunes and Woodland Terrace. It also takes in the streets north of where Waccamaw Drive ends, up to the Surfside Beach line.
U.S. government aerial photo
Streets between the marsh and Business 17 from above: houses and yards, a pond, and the salt marsh at the lower right.
This part has the widest range of prices. Away from the marsh, a house sold for about $575,000 at the middle in the past year. Condos and manufactured homes cost less. Where a home is on rented land, the lot rent is not in the price, and we find it out for each home.
Get the homes for sale in Garden City east of Business 17

### 4 West of Business 17: subdivisions lived in all year
West of Business 17 are Garden City's subdivisions, with houses on curving streets around ponds. The largest are Woodlake Village, Mallard Landing, Harbour Village and Jamestowne. Condo communities include Sweetwater at Indian Wells, South Bay Lakes, Southbridge and Tupelo Bay Golf Villas.
U.S. government aerial photo
Subdivisions west of Business 17 from above: houses on curving streets, ponds, a pool and courts, and woods.
More people live here all year: about 3 in 4 houses are taxed as the owner's main home, the most of any part. A house sold for about $340,000 at the middle in the past year and a condo for about $173,000, the lowest prices in Garden City.
Get the homes for sale in Garden City west of Business 17

### 5 The Georgetown end: canals, docks and the quietest beach
South of the county line, Waccamaw Drive runs on to Garden City Point, where the marsh meets the inlet. Houses line the beach, and behind them many sit on canals with private docks.
U.S. government aerial photo
The Georgetown end near Garden City Point from above: houses on canals with private docks, Waccamaw Drive and the beach.
This is the quietest stretch of the beach road. Georgetown County's rules apply here. It requires no business license for a rental, and its lodging tax is lower.
Prices here are the highest in Garden City. The listings here asked about $1.45 million at the middle, more than any other part.
Get the homes for sale at Garden City's Georgetown end

Asking prices are usually higher than sale prices. Before you offer, we pull the recent sales in the same building or on the same street.

## Can you Airbnb in Garden City, SC?
Yes, unless the building's own rules say no. There is no town, so no town rental ordinance applies. Horry County's list of what a nightly-rental owner must file names a business license and three tax accounts, and no rental permit. We go over the filings with you before you close.
A condo association or an HOA (homeowners association) can forbid or limit rentals in its own papers. We read the building's documents and rules before you offer. Our page on HOA rental restrictions explains how those rules work.
Guests pay lodging taxes on top of the rent: about 12 percent on the Horry side and about 11 percent on the Georgetown end. You collect that money and send it on, so it is not part of your income.

### What a Garden City Airbnb earns
AirROI, a rental data company, tracks the Airbnb listings here under the name Garden City Beach. Over the past 12 months:

- $41,200 the average listing's income in a year

- 40% of nights booked

- $371 average nightly rate

- 374 active listings

Each figure is an average across all the listings, so the nights booked times the nightly rate does not come out to the income.
Most of the money comes in summer. A listing earns about 5 times as much in an average July as in January.
What a Garden City Beach Airbnb earns in an average month AirROI's average per active listing over two years, before cleaning, fees and management. Darker columns are May to August, the high season. January, the lowest month, is about $2,090.

## What is there to do in Garden City, SC?
A summer day here starts on the beach and ends on the pier. For dinner, the MarshWalk in Murrells Inlet is about 8 minutes away by car. It is a half-mile wooden boardwalk along the marsh, lined with restaurants such as Drunken Jack's, Dead Dog Saloon, Creek Ratz and The Wicked Tuna, and its live music is free to hear.
For a day out, Huntington Beach State Park is 15 to 20 minutes south. It has 3 miles of beach, a freshwater lake where you are almost sure to see alligators, and what the state calls some of the top bird-watching on the East Coast. The Pawleys Island guide has the park's history and Brookgreen Gardens across the road.
For groceries, Kroger on Business 17 is about 4 minutes from the pier by car, and the Walmart Supercenter on the Garden City Connector about 5.

### The beach rules
Horry County manages the beach from the Surfside Beach town line to the Georgetown County line. Its rules:

- Dogs Off the beach from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., May 1 through Labor Day. Otherwise on a hand-held leash.

- Shade Round umbrellas up to 7 feet 6 inches across, and small pop-up cabanas for infants. No tents or canopies, all year.

- Overnight Nothing may be left on the beach overnight.

- Alcohol None on the beach or the beach accesses.

## Is Garden City, SC busy in winter?
Summer is busy and winter is quiet, most of all on the beach road.

- On the ocean side, more than 9 in 10 homes are second homes or rentals. The county mails most of their tax bills to another state, North Carolina, New York, Pennsylvania and Ohio most often.

- At the last Census, taken in April, about 4 in 5 homes along Waccamaw Drive had no one living in them.

- The pier stays open in winter, with shorter hours for fishing and the deck bar.

- From November 1 to February 28, you may drive a golf cart onto the Horry County beach, with a state permit and a licensed driver.

Example. In the winter cart season, a golf cart with a cooler and buckets drives down onto the sand at Garden City. The beach is empty. There is time for sandcastles, lunch and an hour of watching the waves.

## Does Garden City flood?
East of Business 17, much of Garden City is in FEMA's high-risk flood zone. In that zone a lender requires flood insurance:
Part of Garden City, Horry side Homes in FEMA's high-risk flood zone
The ocean side of Waccamaw Drive Nearly all
Between the marsh and Business 17 About half
West of Business 17 None

Flood insurance costs about five times as much on the beach strip. Along Waccamaw Drive, the middle federal flood policy on a house cost about $3,260 a year. Elsewhere in Garden City's ZIP code it was about $620.
What a federal flood policy on a house costs a year, at the middle Where A year

A house along Waccamaw Drive $3,260
A house in the rest of ZIP 29576 $620

Federal flood policies that began in the past year, ZIP 29576 (FEMA).
A condo building's own flood policy on the strip cost about $17,000 a year at the middle, shared by the owners through their dues.

### What the big storms did
In September 1989, Hurricane Hugo's storm surge wiped out up to 90 percent of Garden City's homes. The pier was destroyed, and sand covered roads three blocks inland.
In 2022, Hurricane Ian's surge broke through the dunes in Garden City Beach and flooded parking lots and streets. It left up to three feet of sand on South Waccamaw Drive.

### High tides are rising
High tides that reach flood level come more often than they used to. At the nearest working tide gauge, in Myrtle Beach, they came about 8 days a year in the last ten years, against 1 or 2 days a year twenty years before.
Days a year the high tide reached flood level at the nearest working tide gauge Years Days a year

1985 to 1994 about 2 days
1995 to 2004 about 2 days
2005 to 2014 about 3 days
2015 to 2024 about 8 days
NOAA's outlook for the coming year 8 to 12 days

NOAA's tide gauge at Springmaid Pier in Myrtle Beach, about 7 miles north. Averages for each ten years.

## What does it cost to own a home in Garden City each year?
South Carolina figures property tax on a share of a home's value: 4 percent of it for the home you live in, and 6 percent for a second home or rental. The home you live in also skips the school operating tax. As a rental, the same condo pays about 3 times the tax it pays as your main home.
For the middle ocean-side condo:

Your own flood policy on the unit, if you buy one $1,560 $1,560
Condo dues, at the middle of the listings $9,480 $9,480

- The flood policy line is the middle federal policy that condo owners along Waccamaw Drive bought for their own unit. The building's own policy is in the condo dues.

- On the Georgetown end, Georgetown County decides the tax rate. The same state rule applies.

- Our property tax calculator has the rate for every part of the county.

## Garden City, Surfside Beach or Murrells Inlet?
The three places sit side by side, and each suits a different buyer.

Vacation-use shares are from the 2020 Census. Garden City's share counts the subdivisions west of Business 17 too, so it is lower than along the beach road. Surfside Beach's pier is about 6 minutes north of the Garden City Pier by car, and the MarshWalk about 8 minutes south.
Surfside Beach is a town, so its own rules on renting apply on top of the county's. Murrells Inlet is lived in all year far more than the two beach places, and the MarshWalk's restaurants are there. Garden City has the pier, the marsh and the Georgetown end's canals.

## Garden City, SC FAQ

### Is Garden City, SC in Horry County or Georgetown County?
Both. The pier is in Horry County, and most of the beach road is in Georgetown County.

### Is Garden City part of Myrtle Beach?
No. Garden City is not part of any city. Most addresses use Murrells Inlet, ZIP code 29576.

### Can you drive a golf cart on Garden City Beach?
On the Horry County beach, from November 1 to February 28, with a state permit and a licensed driver.

### Are dogs allowed on Garden City Beach?
Not from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., May 1 through Labor Day, on the Horry County beach. At other times, on a hand-held leash no longer than 7 feet.

### Is Garden City, SC safe?
We do not rate any place as safe or unsafe. On the Horry side, the Horry County Police Department, the county's main law enforcement agency, answers calls. On the Georgetown end, the Georgetown County Sheriff's Office does.

### What schools serve Garden City, SC?
Schools are assigned by address. Homes on the Horry side are in Horry County Schools, and homes on the Georgetown end are in the Georgetown County School District. We look up the assigned schools for any home you like.

# Little River, SC: the boating end of the Grand Strand. About two of every three deeded boat slips in the county are here.

- Deeded slips About 220

- Beach 11 min drive

- Typical house $357,000

By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 2, 2026
An unincorporated waterway community at the North Carolina line, with deeded boat slips, public ramps and people who live here all year.

The short answer
Little River is the year-round waterway community at the north end of the Grand Strand, at the North Carolina line. If the boat comes first, look at the old village, where all three marinas with deeded slips are. For golf and dry ground, look north-west toward the Waccamaw River; for the hospital and the highest-priced neighborhoods, look west.
A resold house here usually sells for about $357,000. Little River is not a town, so Horry County makes the rules and there is no city tax.

## What is it like to live in Little River, SC?
Little River sits on the Intracoastal Waterway, the boat channel behind the Grand Strand's beaches. The old village meets the water at the end of Mineola Avenue, with docks, boats and restaurants on the water, about a minute from US 17.
U.S. government aerial photo
The waterfront at the end of Mineola Avenue, and the slip basin at Mariner's Pointe, from above (NAIP aerial, 2023).
Each May, on the weekend after Mother's Day, the Blue Crab Festival fills that waterfront with seafood from local restaurants, live music and crafters. It has been held for more than 40 years, and a water taxi brings people in from the water.
The beach at Cherry Grove Pier in North Myrtle Beach, Calabash in North Carolina and McLeod Seacoast hospital are all within about 11 minutes by car, as the map shows. The airport is the long drive, about 41 minutes.

Drive times by car from the old village, without traffic. Map data: U.S. Census Bureau TIGER/Line; Horry County GIS.
A swing bridge built in 1935 still carries Sea Mountain Highway over the waterway. It turns on a center pier to let boats through, and it is one of the oldest swing bridges on SCDOT's highways. Boaters signal it to open, and at weekday rush hours it opens only on the hour and half hour.
Vereen Memorial Historical Gardens, a county park on the waterway, has about 3 miles of trails and boardwalks through forest and marsh. A piece of the colonial Kings Highway, the road from Boston to Charleston, still runs at the front of the park.
Little River is a place people live all year. When the Census last counted, about one in five of its homes was kept for seasonal use. In North Myrtle Beach, which borders it, it was nearly half.
Share of homes kept for seasonal use, 2020 Census Place Seasonal homes

North Myrtle Beach 48%
Garden City 39%
Little River 19%
All of Horry County 18%
Murrells Inlet 14%
Carolina Forest 5%
Conway 2%

Homes no one lived in on Census Day that were kept for seasonal or occasional use, such as vacation homes and many nightly rentals.

## Is Little River, SC a town?
No. Little River has no town government and no town limits, so Horry County makes its rules and collects its tax. A home here pays the county's property tax and no city tax on top.
One corner is different. A small part of the Little River ZIP code along the waterway is inside the city of North Myrtle Beach. Its homes, about 250 and mostly condos, have a Little River address and pay North Myrtle Beach's city tax. We check which side of the line a house is on.

## Living on the water in Little River: boat slips, ramps and waterfront homes
Most marinas rent their slips. At Little River's three marinas you can buy one: a deeded slip is its own piece of real estate, with its own deed and its own county tax bill. The 12 slip sales recorded here in the past year were each for a slip alone, at $10,000 to $95,000, without a condo.

- Mariner's Pointe

- Coquina Harbour

- Lightkeepers Village

- T. Craig Campbell Landing and, across the waterway, Johnny Causey Landing

- FEMA's high-risk flood zone

- The city of North Myrtle Beach

The dark line is the Little River ZIP code. Marker sizes follow the number of deeded slips. The two landings on the Waccamaw River are north-west of this map. Map data: Horry County GIS; FEMA flood map as the county carries it; U.S. Census Bureau TIGER/Line.

The slips come in sizes. The table gives the length of most slips at each marina, from the county's parcel map. Coquina Harbour's are about 30 to 45 feet. The county's parcel records do not give the depth of the water, so we check it at low tide for any slip you like.
Deeded boat slips and what they sold for, from county deeds Marina Most slips Sales, past year Prices Middle price
Mariner's Pointe About 30 to 35 feet 11 $10,000 to $38,000 About $16,500
Lightkeepers Village About 45 to 65 feet 1 $95,000 $95,000
Dock Holidays Marina, in North Myrtle Beach About 40 to 50 feet 10 $65,000 to $115,000 About $92,500

Coquina Harbour, with about 80 deeded slips, had no slip sales in the past year.
The county taxes a slip like a second home, on its own value for the slip. It values most Mariner's Pointe slips at $38,000 or more, above nearly every price paid there in the past year. On the county's full $38,000 value, a slip pays about $460 a year in property tax; a slip that has not sold in years may be taxed on a lower, capped value. The marina's association charges a fee on top, and its recorded papers say who may own a slip. We read both before you make an offer.

### Where to launch a boat
Horry County runs two public boat landings in the Little River ZIP. T. Craig Campbell Landing is on the Intracoastal Waterway at the US 17 bridge, about 7 minutes from the old village, with two ramps, a dock and a paved lot. Johnny Causey Landing faces it across the waterway, just inside North Myrtle Beach, with two more ramps and a larger lot.
On the Waccamaw River, Worthams Ferry Landing has one ramp and an unpaved lot. Chris Anderson Landing, on the river near Longs, has two ramps.

### Homes on the water
Few houses here sit on the water: fewer than 2 in every 100 have a lot on the Intracoastal Waterway, a canal off it, or the Waccamaw River. Those few cost far more. Only 5 resold in the past year, and the middle one sold for about $1.3 million.
Most homes right by the water are condos, and about half of them are in three communities: Carolina Yacht Landing, Mariner's Pointe and Lightkeepers Village. A condo by the water usually sold for about $263,000 in the past year, and one away from it for about $180,000.
A typical resold house and a Mariner's Pointe slip come to about $375,000 together. If you would rather keep the boat on a trailer at home, our guide to homes with no HOA covers where that is allowed.

Little River's homes fall into five parts, and each gives you something the others do not. The numbers on the map match the entries below.

### The old village and the harbors: all three marinas within a mile
This is the part to choose if the boat comes first. The waterfront at the end of Mineola Avenue, its restaurants and all three marinas with deeded slips are within about a mile of the village center. At Mariner's Pointe, the condo buildings ring the slip basin.
U.S. government aerial photo
Coquina Harbour and Lightkeepers Village share one basin between US 17 and the waterway, with a golf course beside it (NAIP aerial, 2023).
Golf is here too. Hidden Lakes Village borders the River Hills golf course, and Eastport's homes line a course beside Coquina Harbour. Cypress Village, with houses and townhouses, is the largest subdivision in this part.
Homes in Cypress Village resold for about $385,000 at the middle in the past year, and in Hidden Lakes Village for about $318,000. Flood risk is highest at the water's edge: about half the condos at Mariner's Pointe and most homes at Eastport are in FEMA's high-risk zone.
Get the homes for sale in Little River's old village

### North and east, toward Calabash: Heather Glen and Vereen Gardens
Heather Glen is the biggest neighborhood in Little River, with more than 1,100 houses north-east of the old village, and the busiest: more of its houses resold in the past year than in any other. Heather Lakes is east of it.
This is the side nearest Calabash, North Carolina. Vereen Memorial Historical Gardens is in this part too, between US 17 and the waterway, with its trails along the marsh.
Houses in Heather Glen and Heather Lakes usually resold for about $375,000. Windjammer Village, the third large neighborhood here, has some homes in the high-risk flood zone.
Get the homes for sale in east Little River

### North-west, toward the Waccamaw: golf, dry ground and a river ramp
River Hills is built along the River Hills golf course. Lafayette Park has more than 400 houses on lots of about a quarter of an acre.
Worthams Ferry Landing, the county's ramp on the Waccamaw River, is north of this part, for a boat you keep on a trailer.
Houses resold for about $385,000 at the middle in River Hills and about $348,000 in Lafayette Park. The marinas are back toward the old village, a drive rather than a walk.
Get the homes for sale in north-west Little River

### West, around the hospital: the landing and condos on the water
McLeod Seacoast hospital is in this part, about 6 minutes from the old village. T. Craig Campbell Landing, the county's ramp at the US 17 bridge, is at its south edge.
Carolina Yacht Landing, a condo community on the waterway west of that landing, has about half its units within about 50 feet of the water. Bay Tree, near the hospital, has condos and townhouses.
Among Little River subdivisions with at least five resales, the two highest prices are here: Sawgrass Village at Bridgewater, at about $585,000, and Waterside Village, at about $560,000. Condos at Carolina Yacht Landing resold for about $252,000.
Get the homes for sale in west Little River

### Far west, at SC 9: a shorter drive to Myrtle Beach
This part suits a buyer who drives south to Myrtle Beach often. SC 31, the Carolina Bays Parkway, starts at its edge. From its subdivisions, Coastal Grand Mall in Myrtle Beach is about 30 to 35 minutes by car and the airport about 35 to 40, a few minutes sooner than from the old village.
It is the part farthest from the water: the old village's waterfront is about 12 to 15 minutes back east by car, and McLeod Seacoast hospital about 9. Its three largest subdivisions, Hidden Brooke, Palm Lakes Plantation and Waterfall, are neighborhoods of houses.
In the past year, houses resold for about $340,000 at the middle in Palm Lakes Plantation, $390,000 in Hidden Brooke and $555,000 in Waterfall.

## Does Little River flood?
Most of it does not. About 96 in 100 Little River homes are outside FEMA's high-risk flood zone. Homes right by the water are the exception: close to half of them are inside it.
Share of Little River homes inside FEMA's high-risk flood zone Homes In the zone

Homes within about 50 feet of the water 45%
All homes in the ZIP 3.6%
Homes away from the water 2.2%

Hurricane Hazel came ashore near Little River, at the North Carolina and South Carolina line, in October 1954 as a Category 4 hurricane. It hit at the year's highest tide, and the storm surge reached as high as 18 feet at Calabash.
Few houses for sale at our last count were in the high-risk zone. We check the flood map, the elevation and the seller's flood disclosure for every house before you make an offer. Our page on how to find out if a house flooded shows every record we use.

### Do you need flood insurance in Little River?
A lender must require flood insurance when the building is in FEMA's high-risk zone, and can ask for it anywhere.
In the Little River ZIP, a flood policy on a house outside the zone usually costs about $480 a year, and inside it about $1,250. A new policy starts 30 days after you apply and pay, unless you buy it with your home loan.

## What does it cost to own a home in Little River each year?
A typical resold house you live in costs about $3,000 to $4,300 a year in property tax, a flood policy and homeowners insurance, before wind and hail cover.

Together About $3,000 to $4,300

That insurance range is for a house insured for $350,000. It leaves out wind and hail, which is priced on its own here. We get that quote for any house before you make an offer.
South Carolina taxes a home you live in on 4 percent of its value, and a second home or rental on 6 percent, so the same house as a rental pays about $4,400. The owner must apply for the lower rate; our property tax page shows how. Where there is an HOA, its fee comes on top, and we read its budget and rules with you. ## What do homes rent for in Little River?
HUD's Small Area Fair Market Rent for a three-bedroom in the Little River ZIP is $2,100 a month, with utilities. That is above North Myrtle Beach's ZIP and Myrtle Beach's, and close to Carolina Forest's.

Rents people pay here are higher than the county's: the Census survey's middle rent in Little River is about $1,530 a month, against about $1,260 countywide, apartments included.

### A worked example
Take a typical resold house. At HUD's three-bedroom figure of $2,100 a month, a year comes to about $25,000, about 7 percent of the price. As a rental, the house pays about $4,400 a year in property tax, about 17 percent of that rent.
Insurance, upkeep, management and empty months come out of the rent too. Our rental analyzer works them out for any address.

### Short-term rentals
Little River has no city ordinance, so county rules apply. A home in Little River outside North Myrtle Beach that is rented short term needs:

- a Horry County business license;

- a county hospitality and accommodations account;

- a South Carolina sales and accommodations tax account;

- a yearly county personal property return for its furnishings, due April 30.

An HOA's rules can forbid short stays, and we read them first. See the short-term rental rules by town and what a nightly rental earns by town .

## Is the Carolina Bays Parkway being extended through Little River?
The extension is planned but not built. The Carolina Bays Parkway, SC 31, would be extended from SC 9 north-east, passing north and northwest of Little River's old village. It would cross the state line to US 17 near Shallotte, North Carolina. It would be a multi-lane freeway, partly on new ground.
South Carolina's part is in SCDOT's current program. North Carolina has not funded land buying or building for its part. The whole project is estimated at $797 million.
The two states have named a preferred route. The final choice comes after they review the comments from the public hearings. If you like a house in the north-west part, we show you where it sits against the preferred route's map.

## What are the pros and cons of living in Little River?
The good points are the water, the price and a year-round town. The hard ones are the few houses on the water, flooding at the water's edge, and the drive to the airport.

### Pros

- Deeded boat slips you can own, and public ramps on the waterway and the Waccamaw River.

- No city tax, golf in the neighborhoods, and the beach about 11 minutes away.

- A year-round community, with the waterfront, the Blue Crab Festival, the swing bridge and Vereen Gardens.

### Cons

- Few houses are on the water, and those cost far more. We pair a house with a deeded slip instead.

- Homes right at the water's edge have the most flood risk. We check the flood map and the elevation first.

- The airport is about 41 minutes away by car.
