## What happens if you stop paying HOA dues?
The bill grows, a lien goes on the home, and the association can sue to have it sold. The months below are from one South Carolina case, Winrose, in Richland County. The time to answer, usually 30 days, is in the court's rules, and the summons states it.

- 1 The start Dues go unpaid Your community's rules say what is added. In the Winrose case, dues unpaid for 30 days began to earn interest, and a court judgment would add a reasonable attorney's fee and the court costs.

- 2 Winrose: 3 months in A lien goes on the home The lien is the association's claim against the home itself. In Winrose, the HOA filed it three months after the owners fell behind.

- 3 Winrose: about 3 years in The lawsuit The association sues to foreclose. A notice of the lawsuit, called a lis pendens, may be filed with the county clerk, so it shows on the home's title.

- 4 Usually 30 days Your answer is due You usually have 30 days from the day you are served to answer the lawsuit in writing. The time is in the court's rules , and the summons states it.

- 5 No answer: no notice of the rest An owner who does not answer usually gets no notice of the hearings that follow. In the Winrose case, one owner put the lawsuit papers in a drawer and forgot them. The owners did not answer and got no further notice of the judgment or the sale. A sale notice still runs in the newspaper. In Horry County it runs three times over three weeks.

- 6 Winrose: 5 months after the suit The judgment The judge enters a judgment and orders the home sold. It adds the interest, the fees and the court costs to the dues.

- 7 Winrose: 2 weeks later The auction In Horry County, the Master in Equity holds the sale at 11 a.m. on the first Monday of each month, or on the Tuesday when that Monday is a holiday. The sale is on the third floor of the Government and Justice Center in Conway. The winning bidder pays 5 percent of the bid by noon the next day.

- 8 The buyer's deed The highest bidder gets a deed to the home. What happens to a mortgage on it is below .

Photo: Pollinator at English Wikipedia

In all 4 association cases on the county's list, the bidding closes at the auction . It does not stay open 30 days for higher bids. Plan to settle or sell before that day.

## How does a small HOA bill turn into thousands?
Mostly through lawyers' fees and court costs. In the Winrose case , the court's judgment was almost $2,900 on $250 of unpaid dues, about 12 times the dues.

Five years later, the South Carolina Supreme Court set the sale aside. The winning bid was about 5 cents for each dollar of the owners' equity in the house, and the court called the price grossly inadequate. It wrote:
"A foreclosure proceeding is a last resort, not a business model to be swiftly invoked for the purpose of exploiting property owners."
South Carolina Supreme Court, Winrose Homeowners' Association v. Hale
The steps that stop a bill like this are in what to do if you are behind .

## Does an HOA lien come before your mortgage?
No, not before a mortgage that was recorded first. South Carolina has no law that puts an association's lien ahead of a first mortgage, the rule called a super lien.
Who is paid first, in a South Carolina condo

- Property taxes

- Recorded mortgages and other recorded liens

- The condo association's unpaid dues Then ahead of any other lien on the unit

From South Carolina's condo law, for the lien and for the money from a sale.
For an HOA that is not a condo, no law ranks the HOA's lien. In a 1994 case , a mortgage recorded before the dues fell due came first. That HOA's papers did not say the HOA came first.
The order works both ways:

- The association forecloses The mortgage stays The buyer at the sale takes the home with the first mortgage still on it, when that mortgage ranks ahead. If you are bidding, read our guide to buying at the courthouse sale .

- The bank forecloses a condo Your neighbors pay the gap When a bank forecloses on a condo, the new owner does not pay the dues the last owner left unpaid after the mortgage was recorded. Every owner in the building pays that share instead.

- While a condo case goes on The owner owes rent Once the association sues to foreclose a condo, the owner must pay a reasonable rent for the unit while the case goes on.

## Behind on HOA dues? What to do before the sale
Start with the lawsuit papers.

- Answer the lawsuit within the time on the summons, usually 30 days. An answer is your written reply to the association's complaint. Serve it on the association's lawyer, whose name and address are on the summons, and file it with the clerk of court. A lawyer can write it with you; the $50 line below is a start.

- Have the case dismissed when you pay. In Winrose, the owners paid $250 and got a letter that the lien was satisfied. The HOA did not withdraw its suit. Ask the association's lawyer to dismiss the lawsuit and to file a cancellation of the lawsuit notice with the clerk. Under state law , whoever filed that notice can cancel it once the case is settled or dismissed.

- A fight over the amount can go to small claims. A money dispute with your HOA of $7,500 or less can go to magistrate court, the county's small claims court. A foreclosure cannot. It goes to the circuit court.

- A lawyer for $50. The SC Bar's Lawyer Referral Service , (803) 799-7100, connects you with a local lawyer. The first 30 minutes cost no more than $50.

- Sell before the auction. The lawsuit notice on your title does not stop a sale. It warns any buyer, and a buyer who closes while the case is open is bound by it. Plan for the sale to pay the association and end the case. Unpaid dues usually come out of the seller's money at closing, before you are paid.

Selling to pay the association
A Chapter3 agent finds out before closing what the association says is owed, so that amount is paid from the sale. We tell you what your home could sell for, and what would be left after the association and the mortgage are paid.
Plan a sale

## Buying a condo or HOA home: will the seller's unpaid dues follow you?
In a condo, only up to what the association puts in writing. A condo buyer is liable with the seller for unpaid dues, but only up to the amount in the statement the association must issue on request. The unpaid dues are paid from the sale price at closing, after taxes and recorded mortgages. That limit does not cover a buyer at a foreclosure sale.
When a sale leaves no profit to pay them, the association could go after the new buyer for the fees, or waive them. Our agents check for unpaid fees before closing. A title search shows a lien the association has recorded and any notice of a lawsuit. Dues owed but not recorded show only in the association's statement, also called an estoppel letter .

### Owners behind on dues can affect your loan

- Can block the loan More than 15 in 100 units behind Fannie Mae buys home loans from lenders. When it reviews a whole building, it will not buy a loan on a unit there if that many units are 60 days or more behind on dues.

- Does not by itself The association suing an owner An association that sues an owner for past-due dues, or forecloses on one, does not by itself make the building ineligible.

A building's savings matter for the same reason. Our guide to condo reserves shows how we read them.

## Is South Carolina changing its HOA foreclosure law?
Not yet. Three bills before the legislature would limit HOA foreclosure. None has become law.

- S. 366 No HOA foreclosure clauses Any clause in an HOA's papers that allows foreclosure could not be enforced. A primary home would be protected from a court sale brought only by an HOA. The HOA could still place a lien. In the Senate Judiciary Committee

- H. 3447 A hearing first An HOA would need a court hearing before it could advertise a foreclosure sale against an owner who did not answer. Passed the House 110 to 2; now in the Senate Judiciary Committee

- H. 5204 A minimum debt No foreclosure for less than $10,000 in dues, or $1,000 per home in the association if that is less. Also 90 days' notice, mediation and a cap on attorney's fees. In a House committee

Common questions

## HOA liens and foreclosure FAQ

### Does an HOA have to agree to a payment plan?
No. South Carolina's HOA and condo laws do not make an association offer one. If it agrees to a plan, get the plan in writing, including what happens to the lawsuit.

### Can you get your house back after an HOA foreclosure sale?
Not by paying the association afterward. In a Murrells Inlet case, the owner offered the full fees as soon as he learned of the sale, and the association's lawyers turned it down because someone had already bid. The Supreme Court set the Winrose sale aside because the price was far too low, but that took five years.

### Can I stop paying HOA dues if the HOA is not doing its job?
No. A condo owner cannot avoid the dues by not using the shared areas or by leaving the unit. In an HOA, paying the dues is a duty in the community's recorded rules. Holding them back starts the late charges, the lien and the lawsuit.

### Can an HOA put a lien on your house for fines?
Only if your community's papers make fines part of the dues the lien covers. South Carolina's HOA law does not say.

### Does bankruptcy wipe out HOA dues?
Not the dues that fall due after you file. Those stay owed for as long as you still own the home.

## South Carolina HOA Laws: The 2018 Act Explained | Chapter3
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/south-carolina-hoa-laws/
Summary: What the South Carolina Homeowners Association Act requires, the rights it gives owners, and why no state agency will overturn your HOA's decision.

Home / HOA Guide / South Carolina HOA Law
The 2018 Act, and its limits

# South Carolina HOA laws.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated October 28, 2026
What South Carolina HOA law requires of an association, the rights it gives you, and the part most owners get wrong: no state agency enforces it for you.
Ask us about a community Call 854.333.2135

The direct answer

## What the Act does
The South Carolina Homeowners Association Act became law in May 2018 and sits at Title 27, Chapter 30 of the state code. It applies to communities and horizontal property regimes where owners are required to pay assessments.

- &#10003; Governing documents must be recorded. Documents must be recorded in the public records of the county where the property is located to be enforceable, and associations already in existence were given a deadline to file.

- &#10003; Notice before a budget increase. In an HOA that is not a nonprofit corporation, homeowners must be given notice at least 48 hours before the meeting at which a decision to raise the annual budget is made. A nonprofit HOA follows its bylaws.

- &#10003; Access to documents. Owners can inspect and copy the association's annual budget and membership list after a written request at least five business days ahead.

- &#10003; Magistrate court jurisdiction. Magistrates were given jurisdiction over certain monetary disputes between associations and homeowners.

- &#10003; Seller disclosure. The residential property condition disclosure was amended to require a seller to disclose that a property is governed by a homeowners association.

- &#10003; Complaint data collection. The Department of Consumer Affairs must collect data from HOA complaints and report to the Governor, the General Assembly and the public by January 31 each year.

Who regulates HOAs in South Carolina

## No agency will overturn your HOA's decision
This is the most common misunderstanding we hear, and the honest answer matters.
You can file a complaint about an association with the South Carolina Department of Consumer Affairs, and it will be counted. But the Department states plainly that it does not administer or enforce the Homeowners Association Act. Its complaint process is voluntary mediation : it cannot force an association or a homeowner to take part, cannot require a particular outcome, and does not arbitrate the dispute.
The numbers show what that means. In the 2026 report, about 68 percent of the complaints included were closed because the business responded adequately. Roughly 19 percent were closed undetermined because the facts were disputed. Consumers were recorded as satisfied with the outcome in under one percent of cases.
There is a place to file. There is not a regulator who will make your association do what you want. Your real routes are the association's own process, magistrate court for certain monetary disputes, or a South Carolina attorney. Which is precisely why the reading happens before you buy.

What owners are asking for

## The changes homeowners themselves recommend
The state's report also records what complainants say should change. State agency oversight was the leading recommendation for enforcing governing documents at 31 percent, followed by a dispute resolution process inside the association at 26 percent, enforcement through magistrate court at 16.8 percent and an HOA ombudsman at 16.6 percent.
On the documents themselves, the top requests were open meetings and notice requirements, clearer rules for viewing and copying records, and forbidding associations from placing liens or foreclosing. Useful context if you want to know where this law may go next.

Common questions

## South Carolina HOA law FAQ

### What is the South Carolina Homeowners Association Act?
A 2018 law, S.C. Code Title 27 Chapter 30, that applies to communities and horizontal property regimes where owners must pay assessments. It requires governing documents to be recorded to be enforceable, sets certain meeting notice requirements, gives owners access to the budget and membership list, and requires the Department of Consumer Affairs to collect HOA complaint data.

### Who regulates HOAs in South Carolina?
No agency regulates them in the way most owners expect. The Department of Consumer Affairs collects HOA complaints because the statute requires it and publishes an annual report, but it does not administer or enforce the Act. Its process is voluntary mediation and it cannot compel participation or dictate an outcome.

### Can I complain about my HOA to the state?
You can file a complaint with the South Carolina Department of Consumer Affairs, and it will be counted in the annual report. Understand what it is: voluntary mediation. In the 2026 report only about one percent of complainants were recorded as satisfied with the outcome.

### Do HOA governing documents have to be recorded in South Carolina?
Yes. Under the Act, governing documents must be recorded in the public records of the county where the property sits to be enforceable, and associations existing when the law took effect were given a deadline to record.

### Does an HOA have to give notice before raising the budget?
Only some must. An HOA that is not a nonprofit corporation must give homeowners notice at least 48 hours before the meeting at which a decision to increase the annual budget is made. An HOA incorporated as a nonprofit follows its bylaws instead, and state law requires no notice to owners before its board meets.

### Does a seller have to disclose an HOA in South Carolina?
Yes. The residential property condition disclosure requires a seller to disclose that the property is governed by a homeowners association.

# HOA, POA or condo regime in South Carolina.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated October 28, 2026
HOA, POA or condo regime: the label on a Grand Strand invoice tells you little. Which documents govern, what you own, who insures what, and whether a second association exists.
Ask us what governs a property Call 854.333.2135

The direct answer

## The label matters less than the documents
Homeowners association, property owners association, regime, master association. Buyers ask which is which, and the honest answer is that these words get used loosely. Two neighborhoods can use different names for the same thing, so the name on your bill does not tell you much.
Your dues and the rules you must follow are set by the document recorded at the county for that specific property, called the declaration or master deed. South Carolina then has two different laws that can apply: one for regular neighborhoods and one for condo buildings. Which law applies changes who repairs what and who insures what, so find out which one you are buying into.

What changes

## The differences that affect you

- &#10003; What you own. In a condo regime you own the unit plus an undivided share of the common elements. In a single-family HOA community you own the lot and the structure on it.

- &#10003; Who maintains the building. A condo regime maintains the roof, exterior and common areas. In most single-family HOAs your roof is your problem.

- &#10003; Who insures what. A condo regime carries a master policy and you insure the interior. In a single-family HOA you insure your home. See coastal insurance costs .

- &#10003; What the assessment buys. This follows directly from the two points above, and it is why condo dues are usually higher. See what HOA fees cover .

- &#10003; How many associations there are. Master-planned communities often have a master association and a sub-association, which can mean two sets of rules and two bills.

Why it matters

## Where Grand Strand buyers get surprised
Three places, consistently. They compare a condo regime fee to a single-family HOA fee as though the numbers mean the same thing, when one includes a roof and insurance and the other does not. They insure the wrong things because they assumed the association covered it. They find a second association after closing.
All three are avoidable by identifying what governs the property before you offer, which is the first thing we check. What the association's financial condition looks like is covered on our reserves page , and what the rules will let you do on our restrictions page .

Common questions

## HOA vs POA FAQ

### What is the difference between an HOA and a POA?
The terms are used loosely and both describe an association of owners funded by assessments. What matters is which documents govern your property, what you own, and what the association is responsible for. Read the declaration, not the name.

### What is a regime fee in South Carolina?
Regime fee is the common local term for the assessment paid by owners in a horizontal property regime, which is what South Carolina calls a condominium. Functionally it is condo dues.

### What do I own in a condo?
Your unit, plus an undivided interest in the common elements shared with every other owner. That is different from a single-family lot in an HOA community, where you own the lot and the structure and the association maintains shared areas.

### Who insures what in a condo versus a single-family HOA?
In a condo regime the association carries a master policy on the building and owners carry an individual policy for the interior and their belongings. In a single-family HOA you insure your own home and the association insures the common property. Our coastal insurance page covers how the pieces stack.

### Can a community have more than one association?
Yes. Master-planned communities often have a master association plus sub-associations for individual neighborhoods or buildings, which means two sets of documents and sometimes two assessments. Check for both.

# Non-warrantable condos in Myrtle Beach: when the label means a good deal.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated October 27, 2026

The direct answer

## What is a non-warrantable condo?
A warrantable condo is one that qualifies for a normal conventional loan, the kind most buyers use. A non-warrantable condo is one that does not, because the building fails one or more of their project rules. You can still buy it, and you can still finance it. You just use a different type of loan.
This matters more in Myrtle Beach than almost anywhere else, because so much of what people want here is a condo, and a large share of the oceanfront buildings are non-warrantable. If you are shopping condos on the Grand Strand, this is not a rare edge case. It is something you will run into, and it is worth understanding before you fall in love with a unit.
Some reasons behind the label are minor and easy to finance around. One is a hard stop. One common reason can mean you are looking at a good deal. The rest of this page walks through them, what each one costs you, and how to check a building before you commit.

The reasons

## Why a Myrtle Beach condo gets classified non-warrantable
Lenders check every condo building against the project rules behind conventional loans; the rule text itself is linked in the sources. One failed rule is enough to flag the whole building. The reasons below are the ones we see most on the Grand Strand.

- &#10003; Hotel-style operations. A front desk, nightly or weekly rentals, central booking, or units marketed as lodging. This is the condotel trigger, and it covers much of the oceanfront. Full detail on condotel financing .

- &#10003; Master insurance that no longer meets the rules. A recent conventional-lending rule change is pushing many coastal buildings into non-warrantable status right now. This is the fastest-growing reason here, and it gets its own section below.

- &#10003; Structural litigation. If the HOA is in a lawsuit over the safety or structure of the building, that is the hard stop, and you have to wait for it to finish. More on buying a condo in litigation .

- &#10003; Weak reserves or unpaid dues. The budget sets aside too little for repairs, or too many owners are behind on their HOA payments. How to read those reserves is on our reserves page .

- &#10003; Too many investors. One owner holds too many units, or too much of the building is rented rather than owner-occupied. This one is worth a second look, because it is a lending label, not a broken building.

- &#10003; Too much commercial space, or deferred maintenance. Restaurants and shops past a certain share of the building, or needed repairs the building has not made, a concern regulators tightened after the 2021 Surfside collapse.

These are not all equal. Structural litigation means you wait. But too many investors is a lending problem, not a building problem, and it often comes with a lower price. That can be an opportunity, which we come back to below.

What changed

## The insurance rule making more coastal condos non-warrantable
This is the reason surprising the most buildings right now. Every condo building carries one big insurance policy for the whole property, called the master policy. In early 2024 the conventional-loan rules for that policy tightened. The coverage must be enough to fully rebuild the building. The deductible, the part the building pays itself before insurance pays anything, cannot be more than 5 percent of that rebuild amount.
Put round numbers on it. If a building would cost 20 million dollars to rebuild, its deductible cannot be higher than 1 million dollars. The problem is that beach insurers often refuse to sell storm coverage with a deductible that low. The building takes the only policy it can get, that policy breaks the rule, and the whole building gets flagged. From that moment, no unit inside it can close with a conventional loan, even units owned by people who did nothing wrong.
Many HOAs have not updated their documents yet. That is why buildings that financed fine a year ago are being declined today. It is fixable. The HOA can restructure its master policy to meet the rule. Our team has done exactly that in the middle of a deal, working with an association to get its policy rewritten so a purchase could close. You can read how condo insurance works on the coast on our coastal insurance page .
The rules also keep moving. A newer change taking effect in July 2026 softens part of this: the share of the building's deductible tied to your own unit gets capped at 50,000 dollars, and your own small condo policy, called an HO-6, covers that gap. Warrantability has to be checked at the time you buy, not assumed from what was true last year.

The loans that work

## How to finance a non-warrantable condo
Conventional loans are out, by definition. Government loans, meaning FHA, VA, and USDA, are also out, because they require the building to be on an approved list. What is left is a set of loans that lenders keep on their own books or sell outside the agencies.

- &#10003; Portfolio loans. The lender keeps the loan and sets its own building rules, so a non-warrantable condo becomes a judgment call instead of an automatic no.

- &#10003; DSCR loans. The loan qualifies on the unit's rental income instead of your tax returns. A common choice for investors. Full guide: DSCR loans .

- &#10003; Bank statement and other non-QM loans. Built for self-employed buyers and situations that do not fit the conventional box.

Two honest points about cost. A non-warrantable condo takes a larger down payment than a standard condo, and the interest rate is usually higher, because the loan cannot be sold to Fannie or Freddie. How much higher depends on why the building is non-warrantable and which loan fits, so the only real number is the one we quote you for your building and your situation.
In some cases this path is easier. If you are self-employed, you may not qualify for a conventional loan anyway. On a non-warrantable condo you would use a bank statement or portfolio loan, which is often the same loan you would need on a warrantable building. In that case, the building being non-warrantable costs you little.

Should you buy one

## Is a non-warrantable condo a good buy?
Sometimes it is one of the best buys on the market, and sometimes it is a bad buy. The deciding factor is, once again, the reason.
A non-warrantable condo is usually cheaper than a comparable warrantable one, for a simple reason: fewer people can finance it, so there is less competition for it. If the building is non-warrantable because of something like heavy investor ownership, and the HOA is healthy and the building is sound, that lower price can be a real advantage. You are getting a discount created by a paperwork label, not by a broken building.
The drawbacks deserve the same attention. Financing is harder, and resale is less liquid, because your future buyer faces the same smaller pool of lenders you did. The price and the numbers have to make up for that. If the reason it is non-warrantable is a failing HOA, a crippled building, or unresolved structural litigation, walk away. If the reason is minor and the price reflects it, it can be a smart primary home or a strong investment. It is a case-by-case call, and it is exactly the kind of call we help you make. You can run a specific unit through our rental analyzer , or read whether Myrtle Beach condos are a good investment .

Now you have lost time, money, and the home. The whole problem is that this usually surfaces after you are already committed.

Common questions

## Non-warrantable condo FAQ

### What is a non-warrantable condo?
A warrantable condo is one that qualifies for a normal conventional loan backed by Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac. A non-warrantable condo is one that does not, because the building fails one or more of their project rules. You can still buy and finance a non-warrantable condo, but you use a different type of loan.

### What makes a condo non-warrantable in Myrtle Beach?
The most common reasons on the Grand Strand are hotel-style rental operations, a master insurance policy that no longer meets the conventional-loan rules, and active structural litigation. Others are low reserves or unpaid dues, one owner holding too many units, too much commercial space, or needed repairs the building has not made. The reason matters, because it decides which loan you can use and whether the building is still a smart buy.

### Can you get a loan on a non-warrantable condo?
Yes. Conventional and government loans will not work, but portfolio loans, non-QM loans, DSCR loans, and bank statement loans can. Plan on a larger down payment than a standard condo and a higher rate. Your exact terms depend on why the building is non-warrantable and which loan fits.

### Can I use an FHA or VA loan on a non-warrantable condo?
No. FHA, VA, and USDA loans require the condo project to be on their approved list, and a non-warrantable building is not. Normal conventional loans do not work either. That leaves portfolio and non-QM loans, which is what most non-warrantable condos close with.

### Why are more Myrtle Beach oceanfront condos non-warrantable now?
A conventional-lending rule updated in early 2024 requires a condo's master insurance policy to cover 100 percent of replacement cost and to carry a deductible no higher than 5 percent of that coverage. Many coastal buildings can only buy wind or named-storm coverage with deductibles above 5 percent, so their master policy fails and Fannie flags the whole building ineligible. Buildings that have not updated their policy are being flagged by this.

### How do I find out if a condo building is warrantable before I make an offer?
Have a lender review the building before you write the offer, not after. Our licensed agents pull the HOA documents and our licensed mortgage team reads them and tells you whether the building is likely to be ruled non-warrantable. The underwriter makes the final call. A building's recent sales are a strong signal. If a buyer closed a conventional loan there last week, you likely can too.

### Is a non-warrantable condo a bad investment?
Not always. A non-warrantable condo is often cheaper because financing is harder, which means fewer buyers and less competition. If the reason it is non-warrantable is something like too many investor-owned units, and the HOA and building are healthy, it can be a strong buy. The drawbacks are harder financing and less resale liquidity, so the price has to make up for that. It is a case-by-case decision.

### Can a non-warrantable condo become warrantable again?
Yes. Warrantability is a point-in-time status, not a permanent label. A building can become warrantable again once it fixes what caused the problem, such as updating its master insurance policy, resolving litigation, or rebuilding reserves. That is why we check a building's current status rather than relying on what was true a year ago.

### Can I buy a non-warrantable condo as a second home or investment property?
Yes. Non-warrantable financing works for primary homes, second homes, and investment properties. The main difference is the loan product and the terms, not whether you are allowed to buy it.

## How accurate are online home estimates in Myrtle Beach?
Redfin publishes how close its own estimate comes in Horry County. For homes that were not for sale, the middle miss was 6.6 percent: about $23,000 on a $350,000 house. Half of the homes were further off, and about 1 in 7 was off by more than 20 percent.
No online estimate, Zillow's Zestimate included, tells you whether your home is one of the close ones or one of the far ones.
Once a home is listed for sale, Redfin's middle miss here falls to 1.65 percent. It is closer then because there is more data about a home for sale. A listing adds what the county's records do not show: the rooms, the updates, the photos and an asking price. Our agent looks at those things with you before you list, and sends the number with the sales behind it.

## Is the county's value or the nearest sales a good guess at my price?
Two quick numbers are often used as a price: the middle price of the six nearest sales, and the county's value, which is the market value on the home's county property record. We checked both against the prices of houses sold this year.
How far off two quick numbers were on a typical house Quick number how far off

Middle price of the six nearest sales 16% off
The county's value 9% off

The county's value was closer, but it is a mass estimate, made for every home at once, for tax. It is above the price on most condos and below it on most houses: about 7 in 10 condos sold for less than it, and 6 in 10 houses sold for more.
Your tax bill is a worse guide. About 2 in 3 Horry County homes are taxed on less than the county's value. A sale resets the value as of December 31 of the year the home sold, so your buyer's tax bill can be higher than yours.

## How is a home's value worked out in Myrtle Beach?
We start from the sales most like your home. The nearest sales, or the sales on your street, can be far off. Here is one Carolina Forest house from the county's records.
One Carolina Forest house, from county records. Gray dots are sales. The black line is the middle of the six nearest. The dashed line is what the house sold for.

- The six nearest sales had a middle price of about $556,000, about $74,000 more than the house sold for. Only one of the six was in its neighborhood.

- The other 4 house sales in its own neighborhood in the year went for $356,000 to $425,000.

- The house sold for about $482,000, more than any of them.

The county's records do not say why this house sold for more than its neighbors. A comparative market analysis, or CMA, finds out. It does five things the quick numbers cannot:

- It keeps only sales like the home in size, age, lot and condition, from the same neighborhood or the next one over. For a condo, that means sales in the same building. For a home on the water or a golf course, sales on the same water or course.

- It adjusts each of those sales for what differs from the home.

- It looks at the home's condition, updates and view, with the owner.

- It compares the home with the homes for sale near it now.

- It ends in a price range and a list price.

A condo's price also depends on whether lenders will lend in its building. Where many will not, fewer buyers can get a loan. Our guide to condos most lenders will not lend on explains which buildings and why.

### Is a CMA the same as an appraisal?
No. An appraisal is a licensed appraiser's opinion of value. In South Carolina, appraisal work and the title of appraiser need an appraiser's license, and an agent's valuation may not be called an appraisal.
Our agents see low appraisals only rarely here. When a buyer's appraisal comes in low, our agents ask the appraiser to look again, and send recent sales of homes like yours. Once, the value went up, and the buyer brought less cash to closing.

Condos within 0.1 mile of the ocean ask about twice as much per square foot as condos more than 2 miles away.

### New houses for sale near you
Your house competes with new ones . Builders sold new houses in the same 12 months for a middle price close to the resale one. More than 2 miles from the ocean, new houses for sale ask about $194 a square foot, and older ones about $200. A buyer at your price may also be touring new houses.

### The time of year
More houses sell in the warm months. From May to October the county recorded about 1.5 times as many house resales a month as in January and February. The price moved less: the middle stayed within about 5 percent of $350,000 in every month.

### The flood line
About 13 percent of the county's resales were inside FEMA's high-risk flood zone , most of them condos. Being inside it did not lower the price. In neighborhoods with house sales on both sides of the line, the houses inside it did not sell for less than the others.

## How much will I keep when I sell in Myrtle Beach?
On a $350,000 sale, these come off the price:

- The deed fee, $1,295. It is a state fee, and the seller pays it.

- The commission you agree with your broker.

- What you still owe on your loan.

- Tax on your gain, often none. If you owned the home and lived in it for 2 of the last 5 years, up to $250,000 of gain can be left out of your income, or $500,000 for a married couple filing jointly who both lived there. It does not apply if you used it on another home in the 2 years before. Bought for $200,000 and sold for $350,000, your gain is less than $150,000, inside the limit.

- A hold-back if you live in another state. The buyer must hold back part of the price at closing for South Carolina income tax, unless the sale is exempt, for example a main home whose gain is inside that limit. With your signed statement of the gain, it is figured on the gain, not the whole price.

Common questions

## Home value FAQ

### What is my home worth in Myrtle Beach?
Across Horry County, houses and other homes resold for a middle price of about $350,000 in the latest 12 months of county deeds, and condos for about $215,000. In the city of Conway the middle house sold for about $265,000, and inside North Myrtle Beach for about $535,000.

### How accurate are online home estimates in Myrtle Beach?
Close on some homes and far off on others. Redfin's figures for Horry County put its middle miss at 6.6 percent on homes not for sale, and 1.65 percent once a home is listed.

### What is the difference between a CMA and an appraisal?
A CMA, a comparative market analysis, is an agent's pricing of your home from the sales most like it. An appraisal is a licensed appraiser's opinion of value. In South Carolina an agent's valuation must not be called an appraisal.

### Why is my county assessed value different from my market value?
The county values every home at once, for tax, so it cannot see what one home has. The taxable value is often lower still: under state law it can rise only so far between sales. A sale resets it.

### Are Myrtle Beach home prices dropping?
No. By the Federal Housing Finance Agency's house price index, house prices in Horry County were about flat in the year to mid-2026, after rising about half from mid-2021 to mid-2025.

### Does a home valuation cost anything?
No. Our valuation is free, and you do not have to list your home with us.

## What it costs to sell a house in South Carolina
Selling a South Carolina home has six main costs. The agent commission. Deed stamps, a state and county transfer fee of 1.85 dollars per 500 dollars of the price. The closing attorney's fee, because South Carolina requires an attorney to conduct closings. An owner's title policy. Any HOA transfer or estoppel fees. Whatever repairs or credits you agree to during the deal. Your mortgage payoff is not a cost, but it comes out of the same check.
On most sales the commission is the biggest line and deed stamps are second. Everything else is smaller, but it adds up, which is what the calculator below is for. The transfer tax

## Deed stamps, explained in one paragraph
South Carolina charges 1.85 dollars for every 500 dollars of the sale price when the deed records, 1.30 to the state and 0.55 to the county. That works out to about 0.37 percent. On a 300,000 dollar sale it is 1,110 dollars. The seller pays it, and it is set by law, so it is the same no matter who lists the home. The calculator above figures it for you automatically.

## Cost to sell FAQ

### How much does it cost to sell a house in South Carolina?
Plan for the agent commission, deed stamps of 1.85 dollars per 500 dollars of price, an attorney closing fee, a title policy, any HOA transfer fees, your prorated property taxes, and whatever you agree to credit the buyer. On most sales the commission is the largest line and deed stamps are second.

### What are deed stamps in South Carolina?
A state and county recording fee charged when the deed transfers: 1.85 dollars per 500 dollars of the sale price, about 0.37 percent. On a 300,000 dollar sale that is 1,110 dollars. The seller pays it by law and by custom.

### Does the seller need an attorney in South Carolina?
Yes. South Carolina requires a licensed attorney to conduct real estate closings, so the attorney fee is part of every sale, agent-listed or not.

### Do I pay capital gains tax when I sell?
Sometimes. A primary home usually gets a large federal exclusion, and rentals and second homes are taxed differently. Out-of-state sellers also face South Carolina withholding at closing. Our capital gains page walks through all of it.

## Can you sell your own house in South Carolina?
Yes. No law requires a listing agent. You will still need a licensed South Carolina attorney to close, because closings here are the practice of law. You still owe the buyer the state property condition disclosure and, on homes built before 1978, the federal lead paint disclosure.
About 5 percent of national sales were for sale by owner in the National Association of Realtors' 2025 profile, the lowest share ever recorded, and 91 percent of sellers used an agent. The rest of this page covers both paths honestly, and a third option most sellers have never been offered.

The checklist

## Selling FSBO in South Carolina: do it well

- &#10003; Price from sold comps, not asking prices. Asking prices show what sellers hope for. Sold prices show what buyers paid. We will build your pricing analysis free even if you never list with us: get the number here .

- &#10003; Never wire money on emailed instructions. Confirm wiring details by phone with the attorney's office at a number you looked up yourself.

Every item on this list is part of the coaching. If the workload stops being worth it, that is normal, not failure. About one in five FSBO sellers hands it to an agent. We pick it up from wherever you are.

The law

## What South Carolina requires from a FSBO seller

- &#10003; The property condition disclosure. South Carolina law requires sellers to give buyers a completed Residential Property Condition Disclosure Statement before or at contract signing. Getting it wrong is the classic FSBO lawsuit.

- &#10003; Lead paint disclosure. Federal law requires it on any home built before 1978, with the EPA pamphlet and a 10-day inspection window.

- &#10003; An attorney closing. South Carolina requires a licensed attorney to conduct the closing. This is not optional for FSBO sellers.

- &#10003; A real purchase contract. Deadlines, earnest money, financing and inspection terms, and what happens when one side misses. This is where deals fall apart or get expensive.

The numbers

## What the data says about FSBO prices
The National Association of Realtors' 2025 profile puts the median FSBO sale price at 360,000 dollars, against 425,000 dollars for agent-listed homes.
Part of that gap is not about agents at all. 38 percent of FSBO sellers sold to someone they already knew, a relative, friend, or neighbor, and pre-arranged sales are rarely full-price sales. The honest read is that FSBO works best when you already have your buyer. On the open market, the gap shows up in the sale price.
Pricing is the number one difficulty FSBO sellers report to NAR. In Clever Real Estate's 2024 home-selling survey, 51 percent of FSBO sellers said they did not sell for the profit they wanted, against 31 percent of agent-assisted sellers. In the same survey, 43 percent said they made legal mistakes by not using an agent, about one in five ended up hiring an agent anyway, and 47 percent said the process brought them to tears.

## Buying new construction in Myrtle Beach
New homes are going up across the Grand Strand: Carolina Forest and its roughly 30 neighborhoods, the Market Common district on a spec home Air Force base, Grande Dunes, and fast-growing corridors through Longs, Little River, Conway, and Surfside. If you are shopping here, new construction is on your list whether you planned it or not.
A new build changes the process, not the stakes. The contract is the builder's contract, the sales agent in the model home works for the builder, and the warranty is whatever the paperwork says it is.

Representation

## Bring your own agent to the first visit
The sales agent in the model home is the builder's representative. They can be helpful, but everything you tell them serves the builder's side of the negotiation.
Most builders require your agent to register with you on or before your first visit. Walk in alone first and many builders will refuse to recognize your agent afterward, which leaves you unrepresented for the entire purchase.
Since August 2024, buyers sign a written agreement with their agent before touring homes, so the cost of representation is settled in writing up front. In most Grand Strand communities the builder pays the buyer agent fee from its sales and marketing budget, and we confirm exactly what applies, in writing, before you tour. Builders almost never lower the price for an unrepresented buyer, because a visible discount would undercut the comps in their own community.
Want us to look at it for you?
Set up my builder tour Call 854.333.2135

Incentives

## Builder incentives and the preferred lender
Builders usually offer incentives instead of price cuts: closing cost credits, design center money, and interest rate buydowns. A price cut lowers the appraised comps for every future sale in the neighborhood, so builders protect the list price and give value in other ways.
Most incentives are tied to using the builder's preferred lender. Sometimes that is still the best deal. Sometimes the credit is built into the loan terms. The only way to know is to compare complete loan estimates side by side. The advertised rate alone does not show the cost. An investor buyer rarely gets these incentives. Inspections

## Yes, you inspect a brand-new house
New homes are built fast, by many crews, under one superintendent. Independent inspections find what the county checklist does not, and on a new build the timing matters as much as the inspection itself.

- &#10003; Pre-drywall inspection. Framing, plumbing, and wiring get checked while they are still visible. Once drywall goes up, problems hide for years.

- &#10003; Final inspection before closing. The punch list becomes part of the deal, in writing, while you can still require fixes before closing.

- &#10003; The 11-month inspection. Most workmanship warranties run one year. An inspection in month eleven puts repairs at the builder's cost instead of yours.

If a builder discourages an independent inspection, treat that as information.

Warranties and defects

## Warranties, and the defect problem nobody advertises
South Carolina has no statutory new-home warranty. You get the builder's written warranty, commonly one year on workmanship, two on systems, and ten on structure, plus the implied warranties South Carolina courts recognize.
Construction defect complaints have been rising across South Carolina, and the coast is part of it. In early 2025, roughly sixty defect lawsuits were filed against a single national builder across three counties, including Horry. The most common coastal problems are water intrusion, flashing and stucco issues, and rushed HVAC work.
South Carolina generally allows three years from discovering a defect to bring a claim, with an eight-year outer limit. That is why the eleventh-month inspection matters, and why we track punch lists and warranty deadlines for our buyers. Every new house has some defects. The goal is finding them while they are still the builder's to fix.

Set up my builder tour Call 854.333.2135

Spec vs to-be-built

## Spec home or to-be-built
A spec home is already built or nearly built. It closes fast, you can walk it before you buy it, and specs sitting at quarter end often carry the strongest incentives.
A to-be-built gives you the lot and the finishes, and it takes months, during which prices and rates can move. Deposits and design center spending are larger than in a resale purchase, and upgrade pricing is where builders make back their incentives.
Either way, upgrades, lot premiums, and credits move more than base price, so that is where we focus for our buyers.

Common questions

## New construction FAQ

### Do I need a realtor to buy new construction?
You are allowed to buy without one, but the sales agent in the model home represents the builder. Your own agent reviews the contract, the lot, the incentives, and the inspection findings for your side. In most Grand Strand communities the builder pays the buyer agent fee from its sales budget, and we confirm in writing what, if anything, you would pay before you tour.

### Does using my own agent make a new build cost more?
Builders almost never discount the price for unrepresented buyers, because doing so would undercut the comps in their own community. Since August 2024, representation terms are set in writing up front, so you know the cost before you tour, and in most local communities the builder covers it.

### Do I have to use the builder's lender?
No. Incentives are often tied to the builder's preferred lender, so compare complete loan estimates side by side. A credit at closing does not automatically beat a better loan.

### Should I get an inspection on a new build?
Yes, and ideally three: before drywall goes up, before closing, and again around month eleven, before the one-year workmanship warranty runs out.

### What warranty comes with a new home in South Carolina?
South Carolina has no statutory new-home warranty. Most builders offer a written warranty, commonly one year on workmanship, two on systems, and ten on structure, plus the implied warranties South Carolina courts recognize. Read it before you sign, not after.

### Are builder incentives worth it?
Sometimes. Price the incentive against the rest of the purchase: the lot premium, the upgrade pricing, the loan terms behind it, and what resales in the community sell for.

### What should I know about construction defects?
Defect complaints have been rising in South Carolina, including the coast, with water intrusion the most common issue near the beach. South Carolina generally allows three years from discovery to bring a claim, with an eight-year outer limit. That is why the eleventh-month inspection matters.

### Should I buy a spec home or to-be-built?
A spec home is finished or nearly finished, closes fast, and you can walk the finished house before you buy it. A to-be-built gives you the lot and finishes but takes months and carries timeline risk. Pricing and incentives differ between the two, and quarter-end spec homes often carry the best deals.

## What it costs to own a home in Myrtle Beach
Five lines decide it: the loan payment, property taxes, insurance, HOA dues, and upkeep. Two of them surprise almost everyone who moves here. Property tax on the same house is roughly three times higher when it is not your legal residence. Coastal insurance is often several policies, not one.

Common questions

## Cost to own FAQ

### How much does it cost to own a home in Myrtle Beach each month?
Add five lines: the loan payment, property taxes, insurance, HOA dues, and upkeep. The mix moves a lot between a condo and a house and between a primary home and a rental, which is what the calculator on this page is for.

### What is PITI?
Principal, interest, taxes, and insurance, the four pieces most lenders count in your housing payment. HOA dues and upkeep sit on top of PITI, and on the coast they matter.

### How does the calculator figure property taxes?
It uses Horry County's 2026 certified millage for the location you pick and the 4 percent or 6 percent assessment based on how you will own the home. It also applies the Act 388 school exemption for legal residences and the Myrtle Beach TDF credit. It is the same model as our property tax page, where the full detail lives.

### What should I enter for insurance?
Your best current estimate for the specific home, because coastal quotes vary widely by distance to water, elevation, and roof age. Wind, hail, and flood can be separate policies. Our coastal insurance page explains the pieces, and quotes during due diligence give you the real number.

### Is a condo cheaper to own than a house?
Often the purchase price is lower but the HOA dues are higher, because the dues carry the building insurance and exterior upkeep. A house trades dues for direct insurance and maintenance costs. Run both through the calculator before deciding.

### How much should I budget for maintenance?
Budget about 1 percent of the home value a year, more for older homes and salt-air exposure. It is a planning number, not a bill, but the money gets spent eventually.

The direct answer

## What waterfront means on the Grand Strand
Waterfront in a Myrtle Beach listing can mean five different things: oceanfront, Intracoastal Waterway frontage, tidal channel or creek frontage, riverfront, or a lake and pond lot. They price differently, insure differently, and boat differently. The first question on any waterfront listing is which one it is.
The second question is what you want the water for. Looking at it, fishing it, and running a boat to the ocean are three different purchases, and plenty of buyers pay for the third and get the first.

The five kinds

## The five kinds of waterfront, and where they are

- &#10003; Oceanfront. Mostly condo buildings. True oceanfront houses are scarce and cluster toward Cherry Grove in the north and the Pawleys Island and Litchfield stretch in the south.

- &#10003; Intracoastal Waterway. The main boating corridor: Socastee, the Carolina Forest edge, and up through Little River. Protected water, dock potential, and long no-wake stretches.

- &#10003; Tidal channels and creeks. Cherry Grove's channel grid and the Murrells Inlet creeks. Depth changes with the tide, so the low-tide number is the one that matters.

- &#10003; Riverfront. The Waccamaw and the Conway riverwalk side. Freshwater, quieter, further from the inlets.

- &#10003; Lakes and ponds. Water to look at, not to boat. Priced accordingly, and there is nothing wrong with that if the view is what you want.

Docks

## Docks and dock permits, the part that decides value
On the Intracoastal and the tidal creeks, a private dock usually needs a state permit through DHEC's coastal management office, plus whatever your HOA allows. Not every lot qualifies, and some neighborhoods use shared day docks instead of private ones.
Permitting commonly takes a few months, often around four, before construction starts, and most permitted residential docks here cost somewhere between 15,000 and 45,000 dollars to build. That wait and that cost are why a home with an existing permitted dock carries a premium. They are also why we verify the permit status and transferability of every dock during due diligence instead of taking the advertisement's word for it.

Flood and insurance

## Flood zones and insurance, the honest version
Most of the high-risk flood map here is zones AE and VE. VE is the coastal high-hazard zone where wave action is part of the calculation, and it is the most expensive water to insure.
Averages mislead on this. Across Horry County, flood policies average a few hundred dollars a year, but true waterfront in AE or VE commonly runs between one and three thousand dollars a year, and sometimes more. Wind and hail coverage is a separate question on top.
Get an exact flood quote on the specific address during due diligence. We can recommend local insurance agents who write flood coverage here, just ask. How the policies stack is covered in our coastal insurance guide , and you can check whether the house has flooded before .

Boat access

## Six questions to ask before you buy for the boat

- &#10003; How deep is the water at low tide? At the dock, not the channel. This is the number that decides what boat you can keep.

- &#10003; What bridges sit between you and open water? Fixed bridge clearance against your boat's height, at high tide.

- &#10003; How long is the no-wake ride to the inlet? Minutes on the map are not minutes on the water.

- &#10003; Is the dock permit current and transferable? An unpermitted dock is a liability, not a feature.

- &#10003; Who owns and maintains the bulkhead? Bulkhead repairs are expensive, and responsibility varies by lot and HOA.

- &#10003; What does the HOA allow? Boat lifts, dock size, overnight tie-ups, and rentals all vary by neighborhood.

The ocean runs through the inlets, most directly Little River Inlet in the north and Murrells Inlet in the south. The route, not the distance, decides how long the ride takes.

Where boaters buy

## Where boaters buy on the Grand Strand
Little River has the most marinas and the quickest big-water access. Cherry Grove in North Myrtle Beach runs on its tidal channel grid with ocean access through the inlet. The Intracoastal corridor through Socastee and Carolina Forest offers protected water with long no-wake stretches. Murrells Inlet pairs creek frontage with the MarshWalk and the southern inlet. The Pawleys Island and Litchfield marsh side in Georgetown County is further from the inlets and quieter.

Common questions

## Waterfront FAQ

### What counts as waterfront in Myrtle Beach listings?
Five different things: oceanfront, Intracoastal Waterway frontage, tidal channel or creek frontage, riverfront, and lake or pond lots. They price differently, insure differently, and boat differently, so always ask which one a listing means.

### Can I build a private dock?
On the Intracoastal and tidal creeks, usually yes, with a state permit through DHEC's coastal management office plus whatever your HOA allows. Not every lot qualifies, and some neighborhoods use shared day docks instead of private ones.

### How long does a dock permit take?
Commonly a few months, often around four, before construction can start. A home that already has a permitted dock skips that wait, which is part of why existing docks add real value.

### How much does a dock cost to build?
Most permitted residential docks on the coast land somewhere between 15,000 and 45,000 dollars built, depending on length, height, and finishes.

### How much is flood insurance on the water?
Away from the water, Horry County flood policies average a few hundred dollars a year. True waterfront in the higher-risk AE and VE zones often runs between one and three thousand dollars a year, sometimes more. Get an exact quote on the specific address during due diligence, and we can recommend local agents who write flood coverage here.

### Can I reach the ocean by boat from the Intracoastal?
Yes, through the inlets, most directly Little River Inlet in the north and Murrells Inlet in the south. Check fixed bridge clearances and no-wake stretches on your route, because they decide how long the ride takes.

### What should I check before buying a waterfront home?
Water depth at low tide, dock permit status and transferability, bulkhead condition and ownership, the flood zone and real insurance quotes, HOA water rules, and the route to open water. We check all of it as part of the offer work.

Short-term rental regulations

# Where short-term rentals are legal in Myrtle Beach, city by city.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Rules verified July 19, 2026 · Updated October 27, 2026
Seven jurisdictions, seven different sets of rules. Where short-term rentals are allowed, what they license, and what they tax.
Have us check an address's STR status

The direct answer

## Where short-term rentals are legal on the Grand Strand
The Grand Strand looks like one beach town. Legally it is seven jurisdictions: two cities, two towns, and two counties' unincorporated areas, each with its own short-term rental rules. Move the same house half a mile into the next jurisdiction and it can go from allowed to prohibited.
The one-paragraph map: the City of Myrtle Beach is the strictest, banning STRs in nearly all residential districts. North Myrtle Beach allows them citywide with a license, and is the market watching new rules most closely. Surfside Beach confines them to two districts. Unincorporated Horry County , which includes much of what people call Myrtle Beach, has no STR ordinance at all. Conway has no dedicated STR ordinance either. Pawleys Island allows vacation rentals everywhere and does not even require a business license. In every one of them, an HOA can still say no.
South Carolina taxes stays under 90 days; rent to one person for 90 or more continuous days and the stay is not taxed as lodging. A bill to stop cities from banning STRs statewide was introduced in 2025 and has not passed. Details per jurisdiction below, then the tax table.

Jurisdiction by jurisdiction

## Short-term rental rules by city

### Myrtle Beach short-term rental rules: legal in resort zones, banned in residential neighborhoods
The city defines short-term as under 90 days and prohibits STRs in every residential "R" district except RMV, with fewer than 30 grandfathered houses citywide. They operate legally in the commercial and resort districts along the oceanside corridor east of Kings Highway, which is where the city's condo and condotel inventory lives. Violations are misdemeanors at up to $500 a day. Every rental needs a city business license. In December 2024 the city went further and created a conversion overlay east of Kings Highway from 29th Avenue South to 82nd Avenue North. Units that have operated commercially as short-term rentals there generally cannot convert to long-term leases. The city wants that stock to stay short-term, citing $7.6 million in lost revenue per 1,000 converted rooms. Area prices and rental data: our Myrtle Beach investing guide .

### North Myrtle Beach short-term rental rules: allowed citywide, new ordinance pending
STRs are allowed in any district that permits residential use, roughly 5,400 of them licensed, each needing an annual city business license. No special permit beyond that today. Watch this one: since 2024 the city has been workshopping a "responsible local agent" ordinance, an annual permit with inspection, a public registry, and a 24/7 local contact able to reach the property within an hour. It has not been adopted as of July 2026, but the city did pass a nuisance party ordinance in February 2026 aimed squarely at out-of-control rentals, and a June 2026 incident renewed the pressure. If you are buying an STR in North Myrtle Beach, buy assuming a local-agent requirement is coming. Area prices and rental data: our North Myrtle Beach investing guide . The city code is on Municode .

### Surfside Beach short-term rental rules: two zoning districts only
Rentals under 30 days are permitted only in the R3 and C3 zoning districts and prohibited in the R1 and R2 single-family districts. Every rental is a business in the town's eyes: the STR license runs $90 minimum plus $2.27 per $1,000 of gross income, and the minimums double for non-resident owners. Unpaid license tax becomes a lien on the property. The regime has been stable for years; the common mistake is assuming a Surfside address allows what the neighboring unincorporated Garden City street allows. Area prices and rental data: our Surfside Beach investing guide .

### Unincorporated Horry County short-term rentals: no county ordinance, the HOA decides
Carolina Forest, Socastee, Little River, the north sides of Garden City and Murrells Inlet, Longs: no county STR permit, no STR zoning restrictions, no occupancy caps. What the county does expect: a county business license, a state retail license for the taxes, a county hospitality account, and a personal property return on your furnishings every April. The binding restriction out here is the HOA covenant, which can prohibit or restrict short-term rentals even though the county does not. That document gets read before you offer, not after. The biggest unincorporated rental pockets are Garden City and Little River .

### Conway short-term rental rules: no dedicated ordinance
Conway has never adopted a short-term rental ordinance and has actively encouraged STR projects downtown. You need a city business license, and the district's zoning has to permit transient lodging, which we confirm with city planning parcel by parcel. Conway is a long-term rental market. Our Conway guide covers why the investment case here is tenants, not tourists.

### Pawleys Island and Georgetown County short-term rentals: no regulation
Vacation rentals are the Town of Pawleys Island's main economy, and it is the only coastal town here with no business license at all, and unincorporated Georgetown County requires none either. Its 3 percent accommodations tax pays for beach renourishment. Unincorporated Georgetown County, which includes Litchfield and the south side of Murrells Inlet, treats short-term and long-term rentals as the same residential use and has chosen not to regulate them. The one exception: accessory dwelling units cannot be rented for less than 90 days. Neither is on Airbnb's automatic tax collection list, so owners remit the local 3 percent themselves. Area prices and rental data: our Pawleys Island investing guide .

The taxes

## Short-term rental taxes by jurisdiction, mid-2026
Every short-term stay carries South Carolina's 5 percent sales tax and 2 percent accommodations tax, plus county and city add-ons that differ by line on the map. What guests pay in total: State accommodations tax rules: SC Department of Revenue .
Jurisdiction Total lodging tax
City of Myrtle Beach (includes its 1% tourism fee) 13%
North Myrtle Beach 12%
Surfside Beach 12%
Unincorporated Horry County 12%
Conway 12%
Town of Pawleys Island 11%
Unincorporated Georgetown County 11%

Airbnb automatically collects the state-administered taxes and several local ones, including Horry County's hospitality fee and the Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach, and Surfside city taxes. It collects nothing for Pawleys Island or Georgetown County. Most owners still owe at least one direct monthly filing, due the 20th. Guests do not pay these taxes on stays of 90 days or more. The full rate and license picture is on our accommodations tax page . Renting your own legal residence more than 72 days a year also costs you the 4 percent property tax rate; the full property tax math is on our Horry County property taxes page.

Before you buy

## Our pre-offer short-term rental checklist

- 1. Confirm the jurisdiction and the zoning district , parcel by parcel, not by mailing address. "Myrtle Beach" on the envelope often means unincorporated Horry County on the map, and the rules above flip accordingly.

- 2. Read the HOA covenants and master deed for rental minimums, rental caps, or required rental programs. The HOA's rules override the city's permission everywhere.

- 3. Price the licenses and tax filings : local business license, state retail license, county hospitality account, and the furnishings return in Horry County.

- 4. Insure it as a short-term rental , not a home. Coverage and flood pricing both change with rental use; the details are on our coastal insurance page.

- 5. Run the revenue honestly. Whether the numbers work as a short-term rental at all, versus a long-term lease, is its own analysis: STR vs LTR , our STR data tools , and the Grand Investor Tool do that math.

Bought one? Setting up a short-term rental after closing covers the licenses, the tax accounts, the alarms and the insurance, in order.

Common questions

## Grand Strand short-term rental FAQ

### Are Airbnbs legal in Myrtle Beach?
Depends which Myrtle Beach. Inside the city, short-term rentals are prohibited in every residential zoning district except one (RMV), with fewer than 30 grandfathered houses; they operate legally in the commercial and resort districts along the oceanside corridor. Most of what people call Myrtle Beach is unincorporated Horry County, where there is no county STR ordinance at all and the HOA is usually the only restriction. The parcel's jurisdiction is the first thing we check.

### Do I need a license to run a short-term rental on the Grand Strand?
In every jurisdiction except the Town of Pawleys Island, yes: a local business license (city or county), plus a South Carolina retail license from the Department of Revenue to remit accommodations taxes. Surfside Beach doubles its license rates for non-resident owners. Horry County also expects a personal property return on your furnishings each April.

### What taxes does a short-term rental collect in Myrtle Beach?
Total lodging tax runs 11 to 13 percent depending on jurisdiction. City of Myrtle Beach is highest at 13 percent, North Myrtle Beach, Surfside Beach, Conway, and unincorporated Horry County are 12, and Pawleys Island and unincorporated Georgetown County are 11. The tax applies to stays under 90 days; rentals of 90 or more continuous days to the same person are exempt.

### Does Airbnb collect the taxes for me?
Only some of them. Airbnb automatically collects the state-administered taxes and several local ones, including Horry County's hospitality fee and the Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach, and Surfside city taxes. It does not collect for Pawleys Island or Georgetown County, and platform coverage differs by tax line, so most owners still owe at least one direct filing. We map the exact filings for the specific address before you buy.

### Can an HOA ban short-term rentals even where the city allows them?
Yes. Covenants and master deeds override what zoning permits, and in unincorporated Horry County, where the county imposes no STR rules, the HOA document is usually the only thing that decides the question. Reading it is part of the building and neighborhood review we run before any offer.

## Myrtle Beach Accommodations Tax & Business License | Chapter3
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/invest/accommodations-tax/
Summary: Which Grand Strand rentals owe accommodations tax, what the state and your county charge, what Airbnb pays for you, and the business license every rental needs.

Home / Invest / Accommodations tax
What a rental owes, by county

# Accommodations tax and business licenses, county by county.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated September 7, 2026
Short-term rentals in Horry and Georgetown County owe accommodations tax that long-term rentals do not. This page lists what counts as short-term, what you owe, and who collects it.
Have us check my address

The short answer
Accommodations tax is a tax on rent from short stays. A short stay is under 90 days in Horry County and under 30 days in Georgetown County. A lease of 90 days or more owes none of it. The guest pays the tax. Whoever takes the payment collects it and sends it in. South Carolina charges 7 percent. Your county or city adds 1 to 3 percent on top. Every rental also needs a business license, short-term or long-term, priced on gross rent.

## Which rentals owe accommodations tax?
Only rentals with short stays. The tax is charged on the rent for each stay that is shorter than the county limit. The limit is 90 days in Horry County and 30 days in Georgetown County.
Where A stay owes the tax if it is
South Carolina, state tax Under 90 days
Horry County hospitality fee Under 90 days
Conway Under 90 days
Georgetown County Under 30 days

A long-term lease owes none of these taxes. A vacation rental owes all of them. A furnished rental with monthly tenants owes them in Georgetown County only if the stay is under 30 days.
The guest pays the tax. It is added to the bill. You, or the platform that takes the payment, collect it and send it to the state, the county, or the city. Each has its own office.

## What does South Carolina charge?
The state charges 7 percent on the rent from every short stay. That is 5 percent sales tax plus 2 percent accommodations tax. The sales tax rate on rent is 5 percent, not the 6 percent charged in stores.
What Rate
Sales tax on accommodations 5%
State accommodations tax 2%
State total 7%
Highest local add-on allowed 3%

There is one exemption, set by the state revenue department . It applies if you live in the property, it has six bedrooms or fewer, and you do not use Airbnb, VRBO or a rental agency. Almost every investor uses a platform, so almost no investor qualifies.

## What does your county or city add?
What taxes you owe and how much they add up to depends on your county. Below is a chart of the taxes for each area for short-term rentals.
Where the property is Local tax on rent How often you pay
Unincorporated Horry County 3% hospitality fee Monthly, by the 20th
Inside a Horry County city 1.5% hospitality fee Monthly, by the 20th
Conway 1% hospitality fee Monthly if over $50 a month
Georgetown County 3% accommodations tax Monthly, quarterly or yearly, by size

Horry County publishes its rates on its treasurer page . Georgetown County publishes its rate on its finance page . Georgetown County also has a 2 percent hospitality tax. That one is on food and drink, not on rent. Do not add it to your rent estimate.
Georgetown County lets small owners file less often. If you collect under $25 a month in tax, you file once a year.

## When does a stay stop being taxable?
At 90 days in Horry County and at 30 days in Georgetown County. That single difference is the most common mistake we see people make when they are investing from out of state because they mix up the counties.
An example. A guest books 45 nights in a Murrells Inlet condo in Georgetown County. The stay is over 30 days, so the county tax stops. The stay is under 90 days, so the 7 percent state tax still applies. The same booking in Surfside Beach is under both limits and owes everything.
This page is about the tax on rent. A different rule decides how your rental income is taxed. That rule also uses the length of stays, but it uses a seven-day average. If you rent by the night, read our short-term rental tax treatment page next. It tells you whether your rental losses can reduce the tax on your other income.
Your own stays in the unit are a third count. That one is on our 14-day rule page . Our seasonal worker page covers long leases that owe none of the tax on this page.
Want to talk out your strategy with a local investment expert?
Our specialized investment agents can help you buy in the correct county so that you avoid extra taxes.
Talk to a local investor specialist

## What taxes does Airbnb pay for you?
A booking platform collects some of this but not all of it. The rest is your obligation.
If Airbnb or VRBO take the payment, they are responsible for the taxes on that booking. If you take the payment, you are responsible for the taxes. That is the rule set by the state revenue department .
Airbnb sends in the state taxes, the Horry County hospitality fee, and the Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach and Surfside city taxes. It sends in nothing for Pawleys Island or Georgetown County. Direct bookings, repeat guests who pay you outside the platform, and second listing sites are yours to file.
If a property manager takes your bookings, get it in writing that they send in the tax. Ask which offices they send it to. The property owes the tax even when someone else collected the money.

## Do you need a business license?
Yes. Every rental needs one, short-term or long-term. The fee is based on gross rent, not on profit. An owner who lost money for the year still owes it. Myrtle Beach requires one of all owners of rental property. Surfside treats every real estate rental as a business.
Where Rental needs a license Year ends Late penalty
City of Myrtle Beach Yes April 30 5% per month or part month
North Myrtle Beach Yes April 30 5%, rising 5% each month
Surfside Beach Yes April 30 5% per month from June 1
Unincorporated Horry County Yes, county license Differs, ask the county Differs, ask the county
Town of Pawleys Island No town or county license n/a n/a
Unincorporated Georgetown County No license. A yearly furniture tax return instead n/a n/a

Georgetown County does not require a business license in its unincorporated areas or in Pawleys Island. Rentals there file a different form each year, below.
Myrtle Beach and North Myrtle Beach publish their renewal dates and penalties. Horry County publishes the county requirement for anyone outside city limits. North Myrtle Beach mails renewals in mid-March.
Georgetown County has a yearly furniture tax instead. If you rent a furnished home there, you file a personal property return with the state each year and pay a small tax on the furniture. It is a tax on the contents, not on the building. Georgetown County says so on its own page. The form goes to the state, so ask your CPA whether a Horry County unit owes it too.

## What should you check before you buy?
Four things. All four can be checked before you write an offer. We check them for you.
Check this Why
Which county and city the parcel is in The city boundary does not follow the mailing address. It sets which office you file with.
Whether the building allows short stays Some buildings and HOAs ban them. See our short-term rental rules page .
What the license will cost It is priced on gross rent. Put it in your numbers before you offer.
Whether your stays are above or below the county limit 90 days in Horry County. 30 days in Georgetown County.

Two other taxes are separate from this page. Renting your own legal residence more than a set number of days a year costs you the 4 percent property tax rate. The count is on our Horry County property taxes page . Depreciation is on our cost segregation page .

Common questions

## Grand Strand accommodations tax FAQ

### Does a long-term rental owe accommodations tax?
No. A lease of 90 days or more owes no accommodations tax and no hospitality fee. In Georgetown County the county tax stops at 30 days. A long-term rental still needs a business license.

### Does Airbnb pay the accommodations tax for me?
Partly. Airbnb sends in the state taxes, the Horry County hospitality fee, and the Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach and Surfside city taxes. It sends in nothing for Pawleys Island or Georgetown County. Bookings you take directly are yours to file.

### How long does a guest have to stay before the tax stops?
90 continuous days for the state tax, the Horry County hospitality fee and Conway. 30 continuous days in Georgetown County.

### What happens if I miss the business license renewal?
Myrtle Beach charges 5 percent of the license fee for each month or part of a month. North Myrtle Beach starts at 5 percent and adds 5 percent every month after.

### Is the license fee based on my profit?
No. It is based on gross rent. An owner who lost money for the year still owes it.
Sources: SC Department of Revenue, accommodations , Horry County hospitality fee , Georgetown County accommodations tax , City of Myrtle Beach business license , North Myrtle Beach business license . Rates read September 3, 2026. Local rates change. Confirm with the office before you file. Educational only, not tax advice.
