## What will happen to flood insurance on the Grand Strand next?
The past record points to another short extension or a short lapse in the next year or two. Over five years and more, it points to more short extensions.

- Short run: the next year or two What happened before A short extension at most deadlines since late 2017, and five short lapses. Every lapse so far ended with an extension.
What it points to here Another short extension near Dec. 11, or a lapse of hours to weeks, as before.
What has to happen first Both chambers of the Congress in office now pass an extension, and the president signs it.

- Premiums, every year What the law says now A premium can rise each year up to the limits in the table above.

## Flood insurance and the election: questions

### What is the latest NFIP reauthorization update?
Federal flood insurance runs until Dec. 11 under the stopgap spending law signed on Sept. 2. Congress must extend it by then, or FEMA cannot sell new flood policies until it does.

### What happens to my flood insurance if the program lapses on Dec. 11?
Your current policy stays in force to the end of its one-year term, and FEMA keeps paying claims. FEMA cannot sell new policies until Congress acts. A buyer who needs a new policy waits or uses private flood insurance.

### Will Annie Andrews vote on the Dec. 11 flood insurance deadline?
No. The new Senate term starts Jan. 3, after the deadline. Sen. Darline Graham holds the seat until then. Andrews votes on any extension or flood bill after she takes office.

### Can a home closing happen during a flood insurance lapse?
Yes, with a private flood policy the lender accepts. Some lenders also waived the requirement in the lapse that ran from October to November 2025. In the June 2010 lapse, an estimated 1,400 closings a day were canceled or delayed nationwide.

### Can the governor of South Carolina change flood insurance?
No. Only Congress can change federal flood insurance. Alan Wilson's insurance item, as reported, is about state audits of rate increases, with yearly public reports from major carriers.

## Wilson's Act 388 Rental Tax Cut: What It Means in Myrtle Beach
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/invest/rental-property-tax-cut/

# Governor-Elect Alan Wilson Wants to Cut the Tax on Rentals. What It Would Mean for Myrtle Beach Investors

- $5,347 a year on a $350,000 city rental at 6%

- A third or more off if rentals moved to 4%

- 83 of 124 House votes a change needs

By Devin Day , Chief Operating Officer, and Abdulla Hijazi , Chief Marketing Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 4, 2026
A $350,000 rental inside Myrtle Beach pays $5,347 a year in property tax. What a lower rate would save, and the votes it needs.

The short answer
Alan Wilson plans to look at reforming Act 388, the 2006 law behind part of the higher property tax on rentals. A $350,000 rental inside Myrtle Beach pays $5,347 a year at 6%. At 4%, it would pay $3,564, or $2,037 if it were taxed like an owner's home.
No bill exists yet. The change needs two-thirds of each house of the legislature. By the unofficial count, Republicans are 4 votes short of that in the House.

## What did Alan Wilson say about the tax on rentals?
Alan Wilson won the governor's race in the unofficial count , 51.71% to 47.00%. Jermaine Johnson conceded on election night. The Associated Press had not called the race when he did.
In an interview before the election, Wilson named the gap he wants to close:
"Owner-occupied homes are taxed at a much lower rate" while "second, third, and fourth homes, which are usually rental properties, are taxed at a higher rate."
"...looking at Act 388 and reforming how we assess property taxes on those types of properties."
Alan Wilson, in a full interview with WIS before the election

His affordability agenda, as Fox Carolina and HERE Columbia reported it, lists "Reforming Act 388 to remove higher property taxes for rental properties". He has published no bill text, no new rate and no cost.
Photo: Loadmaster
Oceanfront towers in Myrtle Beach. A unit in them that its owner rents out pays the 6% rate today.

### His other property tax plans
The same agenda, as reported, also lists these:

- Enroll seniors automatically in their property tax break for older owners.

- Expand the property tax break for disabled veterans.

- Lower personal property taxes for commercial businesses.

- Eliminate the state income tax and overhaul property taxes.

His campaign site adds a pledge to "eliminate the car property tax for seniors and veterans". Our guide to the 2026 election covers his other plans and the rest of the results.

## How much property tax does a Myrtle Beach rental pay now, and at 4%?
At 4%, a Myrtle Beach rental would pay a third to three fifths less than it does at 6%. How much depends on whether a change also drops the school operating tax.

At 4%, still paying the school tax $3,564
At 4%, taxed like an owner's home $2,037

Horry County's 2026 tax rates, 254.6 mills inside the city: county, schools and city. Before credits, fees and any special district.
Two rules make the gap. The state constitution taxes a rental on 6% of its value and an owner's home on 4%. Since Act 388, an owner's home also pays no school operating tax.
Wilson has not said which of the two he means, so the chart shows both. Our page on what Act 388 changes would mean has the law's history.

### If you buy a rental
When a rental sells, the county exempts 25% of its value at the sale. The exemption cannot bring the taxable value below the county's current value of the parcel. The buyer applies to the county assessor before January 31 of the first tax year.

## Can the governor cut the tax on rentals by himself?
No. Lawmakers can change the 6% rate without a statewide vote, but only with two-thirds of the members of each house. That is 83 House votes and 31 Senate votes.
Seats in each house, and the two-thirds a new rate needs
House seats are the unofficial 2026 count. Senate seats were not on the ballot, except one special election.
Republicans won 79 House seats in the unofficial count. Even with every Republican voting yes, a change needs 4 Democratic votes in the House. In the Senate, Republicans hold more seats than the two-thirds needs.
Two House races were close enough for a recount under state law, one led by each party. The Republican count could still move by a seat either way.
There are two ways to make the change:

- Route 1: a new law
- House: two-thirds of its members vote yes.

- Senate: two-thirds of the senators agree.

- The new rate goes into state law. No statewide vote is needed.

- Route 2: an amendment
- Two-thirds of the members elected to each house vote yes.

- A majority of voters approve it at the next general election, in November 2028.

- The next legislature votes to ratify it.

One pending bill, S. 815 , would amend the constitution so lawmakers could set the classes and rates by ordinary law. It is in the Senate Finance Committee.

## What would a rental tax cut cost Horry County and its schools?
Suppose every home now taxed at 6% moved to 4%. At 2018 shares, that would take about a sixth of the taxable value off the real property the county assessor values. The county, the cities and the schools would collect less, unless someone else paid more.
Horry County: each kind of property's share of value, and of the tax base
Gray: share of the value the county assessor counts. Brass: share of the taxable value, after the 4% and 6% rates. 2018, from the Lincoln Institute of Land Policy study. Rental property is the study's "other residential" class, which it describes as typically rental property at 6%.
In 2018, rental property was 36.4% of the value the county assessor counts, but 47.2% of the taxable value. At 4%, rentals' taxable value would fall by a third.
The study behind these shares is by the Lincoln Institute of Land Policy. The South Carolina Chamber Foundation and South Carolina Realtors picked the ten counties it studied. It found the tax had shifted "from owner-occupied residential properties to non-owner-occupied residential properties as well as commercial, manufacturing, and utility properties."
Where the $5,347 on the $350,000 city rental goes Who gets it a year

School operating tax $2,291
City of Myrtle Beach $1,751
Horry County $1,094
School debt $210

Horry County's 2026 tax rates, at the 6% rental rate. A home its owner lives in pays no school operating tax.
The school operating tax is the largest part of a rental's bill. For homes their owners live in, a state fund filled by Act 388's 1% sales tax pays the school districts back. Wilson has not said whether the state would do the same for rentals.

### Who says the gap is unfair, and who backs it
A 2025 student note in a University of South Carolina law journal argues the higher rate shifts the tax onto renters. It says the rate "can also prevent the development of affordable housing". The Lincoln study puts the yearly tax in South Carolina at about 0.5% of value for a home its owner lives in. For an apartment renter's property, it is slightly above 1.5%.
On the other side, groups such as nohometax.org back Act 388 as it is. The same note cites the group's page, titled "We Support Act 388".

## What could a rental tax cut do to cash flow and prices?
In the first year or two, a cut would raise cash flow on the tax line, by a third or more of the bill. Over five years or more, past examples point to other owners paying a larger share, unless the state paid the difference.

- First Nothing changes until lawmakers vote.
- No bill exists. A change needs two-thirds of each house, or an amendment that voters approve in November 2028.

- Until then, a rental's bill stays at 6%.

- Short run: the first 1 to 2 years More cash flow, from the tax line only.
- Our $350,000 city rental would keep $1,782 to $3,310 a year more.

- Rents: no study we found measured how much of a tax cut reaches tenants here. A USC law student's note argues the 6% rate has pushed rents up.

- Prices: a rental that nets more is worth more to a buyer. How much of the saving shows up in prices, no study here has measured.

- Long run: 5 years or more Other owners pay a larger share, unless the state steps in.
- The two rates and Act 388's school exemption shifted the tax toward rentals and businesses, the Lincoln study found.

- A cut would move tax the opposite way. About a sixth of the taxable value of the real property the county assessor values would come off, at 2018 shares. Homes their owners live in and businesses would pay a larger share, unless the state replaced it or spending fell.

- Over time, a lower yearly tax could lift what buyers pay for rentals. We give no figure, because no study here has measured it.

What happened where this was tried before
Past example What happened What it points to here
Act 388, South Carolina, 2006 Homes their owners live in stopped paying school operating tax. A 1% sales tax paid the schools back. Rentals and businesses kept paying it. When one kind of property pays less, the others pay a larger share. A rental cut would move part of the tax back onto homes and businesses.
Florida's cap on non-homestead homes Florida caps the yearly rise in taxable value at 10% for a home of nine units or fewer that is not the owner's homestead. The cap covers every tax but the school tax. A homestead: 3% or inflation, whichever is lower. A state can slow the growth of a rental's bill without cutting its rate. We found no study of what the cap did to Florida rents or prices.
H. 3841, South Carolina, 2026 A property tax bill on the 4% rate passed the House 109-0 and the Senate 43-0. Two-thirds is reachable when both parties agree. That bill was narrow; a rental rate change is larger.

None of this is a forecast of what lawmakers will pass. It is what the same mechanism did before, with the size of the change our arithmetic gives.

Common questions

## Rental property tax questions

### Does the 6% rate apply to a condo I rent out?
Yes. The 4% rate is only for the home the owner lives in and applies for. A condo, house or townhouse you rent out is taxed at 6%, whether it rents by the week or by the year.

### Would a second home that is never rented get the cut?
Lawmakers have not decided. Today the 6% rate covers every home its owner does not live in, rented or not. Lawmakers would decide which homes a change covers when they write the bill.

### Does the 4% rate stay on a home after its owner dies?
For a time, under a 2026 law. The home keeps the 4% rate until the estate closes or a deed out of it is recorded. At the latest, it keeps it until December 31 of the year after the death. It loses the rate if it is rented for more than 72 days.

### Would a cut change the taxes a short-term rental collects from guests?
No. The plan is about property tax. A weekly rental still collects the state's 7% accommodations tax and any local tax of up to 3%. A few rentals are exempt, such as a home rented for 14 days or fewer in a year.

## What is Act 388 in South Carolina?
Act 388 is the 2006 state law that took school operating taxes off homes their owners live in. Everyone else still pays them, including second homes, rentals and businesses.

### Homes their owners live in
They stopped paying the school operating tax. They still pay the school debt tax, the county's tax and the city's.

### An extra 1% sales tax
The state sales tax rose by 1%, but not on hotel and rental stays. The money goes to a separate fund that pays school districts back.

### The 15% limit
At each countywide reassessment, a property's taxable value can rise no more than 15% over five years. It took effect after a change to the state constitution was ratified.

In Horry County the school operating tax is the largest single part of a second home's bill.

### What has changed since?
2006 Act 388 passes. Homes their owners live in stop paying school operating tax.
2007 The 1% sales tax starts, and the change to the constitution behind the 15% limit is ratified.
2011 Act No. 57. When a 6% property sells, 25% of its value at the sale is exempt.
2019 Horry County reassessment.
2024 The next Horry County reassessment , as the county scheduled it.
2026 S. 815 is filed, and Act 140 is signed. Wilson wins the governor's race; Jermaine Johnson concedes.
2028 The next general election. The earliest statewide vote on a change to the constitution.
2029 Horry County's next reassessment , expected. Our estimate from the five-year rule.

## Why does a second home or rental in Myrtle Beach pay more property tax?
A home you do not live in pays more for two reasons. The state constitution taxes it on 6% of its value instead of 4%, and it still pays the school operating tax.

- The 4% rate is for the home you live in and up to five acres around it. You apply to the county for it. Without the application, the home is taxed at 6%.

- The 6% rate is for all other real property: a second home, a rental, a lot, or a shop.

Photo: BullDawg2021
Beach houses behind the dunes in Surfside Beach. A house here that is not the owner's home is taxed on 6% of its value.

On the same house inside Myrtle Beach, the rate and the school tax together make the second-home bill more than twice the homeowner's. Our page for rental investors works each bill at 6% and 4% .
The example house pays about 0.6% of its value a year as a home you live in, and about 1.5% as a second home. A statewide study by the Lincoln Institute found about the same: half a percent for homeowners, a little over one and a half for apartments.
Our Horry County property tax guide shows how the bill is figured and when it is due.

## How does the 15% cap work, and when does it reset?
The 15% cap limits how much a reassessment can raise your taxable value while you own the home. A sale or an addition ends the limit for that property.
From late 2019 to late 2024, home prices in the Myrtle Beach metro rose 69% on the federal housing agency's index. An owner who did not sell or add on saw a taxable value rise of 15% at most.
The buyer starts at market value. The 2011 law reduces that for a second home or rental. A quarter of the value at the sale is exempt. It still cannot go below what the seller paid tax on.

### One house, four owners
Take a house on the roll at $200,000 at one reassessment. At the next, the cap lets it rise to $230,000 at most. It sells for $350,000. The chart gives the 2026 bill for each kind of owner.
One $350,000 house inside Myrtle Beach, four owners, the 2026 bill. Dark bars are taxed at 4%, brass bars at 6%. Our example, before credits, fees and any special district.
The four bills, worked out Owner Taxable value Rate Yearly tax
Lives there, long-time owner $230,000 4%, no school operating tax $1,338.60
Lives there, new buyer $350,000 4%, no school operating tax $2,037.00
Rents it out, owned before 2011 $230,000 6%, with school operating tax $3,513.48
Second home or rental, new buyer $262,500 6%, with school operating tax $4,009.95

The new second-home buyer pays about 3 times what the long-time owner who lives there pays, on the same house. The buyer who moves in pays more than the long-time owner too, but at the lower rate.

Owner-occupied homes "are taxed at a much lower rate," he said. "Second, third, and fourth homes, which are usually rental properties, are taxed at a higher rate," he added.

### What his agenda lists
His agenda lists "Reforming Act 388 to remove higher property taxes for rental properties," as Fox Carolina reported it. The agenda also lists automatic sign-up for the senior exemption, a larger exemption for disabled veterans, and lower personal property taxes for businesses.

## Which Act 388 bills are in the South Carolina legislature now?
One became law and the rest are in committee. We read each bill's page at the Statehouse, and none of them lowers the 6% rate.
Bill What it does Where it stands
H. 3841, now Act 140 A home keeps the 4% rate after the owner dies, until the estate closes, a deed out of the estate is recorded, or Dec. 31 of the year after the death. It ends if the home is rented more than 72 days. Signed into law. House 107-0 and 109-0, Senate 43-0.
S. 815 A change to the constitution: the legislature could choose the classes of property and their rates by law. Senate Finance Committee.
S. 768 Raises the senior homestead exemption from $50,000 of value to $150,000 for those who qualified in 2025 and residents of 10 years, and to $75,000 for residents of five years. Passed the Senate 44-0. House Ways and Means Committee.
H. 3445 A spouse may claim the 4% rate. House Ways and Means Committee.
H. 3352 The assessor may not demand confidential tax records for the 4% rate. House Ways and Means Committee.
H. 4608 The 4% rate for family dwellings on the same lot. House Ways and Means Committee.

Two Horry County representatives, Kevin Hardee and William Bailey, were among the sponsors of Act 140. No one voted against it in either house.

## What would it take to lower the 6% rate on second homes and rentals?
Two-thirds of the members of each house must vote for it. The governor can propose a change, but the vote is the legislature's.
83 House votes needed, of 124
79 House seats Republicans won, unofficial
31 Senate votes needed, of 46
34 Senate seats Republicans have

The Senate was not on the ballot this year, except one special race. In the House, Republicans would need at least four Democratic votes. Two close House races go to a recount by law. Whichever way they go, Republicans would have 78 to 80 seats.
The House districts on Horry County ballots elected eight Republicans and three Democrats. Cutting the school tax break for the home you live in also takes a two-thirds roll-call vote in each house.

### The longer route: S. 815
S. 815 would change the constitution itself. That takes two-thirds of each house and then a majority of voters at the next general election, in November 2028. The next legislature must then ratify it.

## When is Horry County's next reassessment?
Tax year 2029 is our estimate, or 2030 if the county postpones. State law requires a reassessment every fifth year, and a county may put one off by a year.
The county reassessed for tax year 2019 and scheduled the next for 2024. We checked the county's assessor guide: it gives no date for the one after.

- If you have not sold or added on, the 15% cap limits your rise in taxable value at that reassessment.

- If you bought after the last one, your value already started at the price you paid.

- If voters approved the amendment in 2028, the next legislature would ratify it about when the reassessment is due. Any new rates would still need a law.

## Who would pay more or less under each change?
A lower rate for rentals would cut their bills by about a third or more, and no plan names who would make up the money. The bills already passed or pending help homeowners and heirs.
Each change, by kind of owner Change Home you live in Second home Rental Business
Rentals taxed at 4% (Wilson's idea) Larger share if money not replaced Unknown until a bill is written About a third off, or more Larger share if money not replaced
S. 815 (rates chosen by law) No change by itself No change by itself No change by itself No change by itself
Act 140 (law now) Heirs keep 4% for a time No change Heirs lose 4% if rented over 72 days No change
S. 768 (larger homestead exemption) Larger exemption, if you qualify No change No change No change
Business personal property cut No change No change No change Lower, if a bill passes

### Who would make up the money?
In 2006 the state named a new source, the extra sales tax, for the money homeowners stopped paying. No plan to lower the rental rate names one.
If none were named, the same dollars would have to come from the rest of the tax roll. For a tax every kind of property pays, such as the county's own tax, each kind pays its share of taxable value.
Of the real property the county assessor values, homes their owners live in were taxed on 30.8% in 2018. With every 6% home moved to 4% and the same dollars raised, that would rise to about 37%.
Share of taxable value, property the Horry County assessor values Kind of property Share, 2018 With 6% homes at 4%
Homes their owners live in 30.8% about 37%
Other homes, mostly rentals 47.2% about 37%
Commercial property 21.1% about 25%

- Every 6% home moves. The calculation moves the whole higher-rate class to the lower rate, second homes included. If only rentals moved, the shift would be smaller.

- The rest is held fixed. The rest of the roll, under one percent, is held as it was.

- What is not counted. Property the state values, such as factories and utilities, and vehicles are not in these figures.

The figures are a calculation, not a forecast. The school operating tax works differently: homes their owners live in do not pay it, so that part would fall on second homes, rentals and businesses.

## What does the evidence say about Act 388, for and against?
The main study says the state's system moved the tax off homes their owners live in and onto other property. Lawmakers have kept widening the homeowner side, with no votes against.

### The case that it shifted the tax
The Lincoln Institute of Land Policy wrote the study in 2020. The South Carolina Chamber Foundation and South Carolina Realtors picked the ten counties it studied, Horry among them. Its subtitle calls the system "Complex, Inequitable and Uncompetitive."
It found the burden has shifted "from owner-occupied residential properties to non-owner-occupied residential properties." It names commercial, manufacturing and utility property too. In Horry County the figures look like this:
Horry County, 2018: who owns the value, and who is taxed on it Kind of property Share

Homes their owners live in, share of market value 35.5%
Homes their owners live in, share of taxable value 30.8%
Other homes, mostly rentals, share of market value 36.4%
Other homes, mostly rentals, share of taxable value 47.2%
Commercial property, share of market value 21.4%
Commercial property, share of taxable value 21.1%

Gray bars: share of market value. Brass bars: share of taxable value. Real property the county assessor values only; property the state values and vehicles are not in it. Taxable value is the assessed value, after the 4% or 6% rate. Other homes are, in the study's words, typically rental property at the 6% rate.
A 2025 student note in a University of South Carolina law journal adds two claims. It says the rental rate has led to "rising rent costs" in South Carolina. It says the rate "can also prevent the development of affordable housing" as well. The note cites other sources and is not a measured study.

### The case for keeping it
A group at nohometax.org publishes a page titled "We Support Act 388." The legislature's own votes point the same way.

- Act 140 passed the House twice and the Senate with no votes against.

- S. 768 , the larger senior exemption, passed the Senate with no votes against.

- The school tax break for the home you live in can be cut only by a two-thirds roll-call vote of each house.

## What could happen to each kind of owner in the short run and the long run?
For homeowners, little changes in the first two years. For second homes and rentals, the range is from no change to about a third off a city bill, and only after a two-thirds vote.

### Home you live in
First 1 to 2 years Nothing pending raises your 4% assessment. If every second home and rental moved to the lower rate with no new money, homes like yours would pay a larger share. The table under "Who would make up the money?" gives it.
Five years and more The 15% cap keeps your taxable value under the market while you own the home. It applies again at the next reassessment.
Where this was tried before In 2006 lawmakers paired the homeowner cut with a new sales tax, so school districts were paid back.

### Second home
First 1 to 2 years Wilson named "second, third, and fourth homes." Whether a cut would include a second home you never rent depends on a bill no one has written.
Five years and more When you sell, your buyer's value starts at the price, less the 25% exemption.
Where this was tried before That exemption came five years after Act 388. It applies at each sale of a home taxed at 6%.

### Rental
First 1 to 2 years No change until both houses pass a lower rate by two-thirds. Our short-term rental rules guide covers what else the Statehouse can change.
Five years and more Florida chose a different rule. It limits the yearly rise in assessment on a home that is not the owner's residence to 10%. The limit leaves out school taxes and buildings over nine units. We found no measured study of what that did to Florida rents or prices.
Rents Whether a lower tax would reach tenants is not known. The student note says the high rate has raised rents, without measuring it.

### Business property
First 1 to 2 years Wilson's agenda, as reported, lists lower personal property taxes for businesses. No bill was published.
Five years and more Commercial property was about a fifth of the taxable value of property the county assessor values. If every second home and rental moved to the lower rate with the same dollars raised, that share would rise toward a quarter.
Where this was tried before The Lincoln study found the shift fell partly on business property.

Common questions

## Act 388 questions

### Does a Myrtle Beach home get the 4% rate automatically?
No. The owner must apply to the county for the 4% rate before the first penalty date. Without the application, the home is taxed at 6%, like a second home.

### Can I get the 25% exemption on a second home I buy?
Yes, if the home is taxed as a second home or rental and changed hands after 2010. The owner must notify the assessor before Jan. 31 of the first tax year claimed. The taxable value cannot fall below the seller's value on the roll.

### Does a home keep the 4% rate after the owner dies?
Yes, for a time, under Act 140. The rate stays until the estate closes, a deed out of the estate is recorded, or Dec. 31 of the year after the death, whichever comes first. It ends if the home is rented more than 72 days.

### Did Annie Andrews' win change property taxes in Horry County?
No. The two rates are in the South Carolina Constitution. Only the state legislature, or the legislature and the state's voters together, can change them. A U.S. senator has no vote on them.

### Will my property tax go up at the next Horry County reassessment?
If you have not sold or added on, your taxable value can rise no more than 15% at that reassessment. The tax rate can still change. We expect the next one for tax year 2029, from the state's five-year rule.

## Grand Strand Short-Term Rental Rules After the 2026 Election
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/invest/short-term-rental-rules-statehouse/
Summary: Myrtle Beach and North Myrtle Beach decide where short-term rentals go. What a state law like H. 3861 would change, and what the new House split means.

Short-term rentals

# Short-Term Rentals on the Grand Strand: Which Rules Can a New Statehouse Change?

- Who decides today Each city and the county

- State ban on local bans None in law

- H. 3861 Died in committee

- Candidate positions None found

By Devin Day , Chief Operating Officer, and Abdulla Hijazi , Chief Marketing Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 4, 2026
Myrtle Beach and North Myrtle Beach write their own short-term rental rules. Only a new state law could take that power away, and none has passed.

The short answer
In South Carolina, each city and county decides where short-term rentals may operate. No state law says a city may not ban them. The new Statehouse could change that only by passing a bill like H. 3861, which died in a House committee, and no winner of the 2026 election has said they would.
Nothing changed for a Myrtle Beach rental on election day. Stays of under 90 days are still barred in the city's zones that begin with R, except RMV. The state's part is the tax: 7% of the rent, plus up to 3% in local tax.

## Who decides the short-term rental rules on the Grand Strand today?
Cities and counties decide where a short-term rental may go, through zoning. Under state law, a county or city with a comprehensive plan can adopt a zoning ordinance . It governs "the use of buildings, structures, and land." The legislature decides the taxes.
Who decides each short-term rental rule Rule Who decides What it says now
Where a short-term rental may operate Each city, and the county outside the cities Myrtle Beach bars them in most residential zones. North Myrtle Beach asks only for a license.
A ban on local bans The legislature None. H. 3861 would have made one.
State tax on the rent The legislature 7% of the rent, with three exceptions
Local accommodations tax City and county councils Up to 3%
Business license Each city and the county Every rental in Myrtle Beach and North Myrtle Beach needs one

We checked the state code's chapters on local government, zoning and property and sales tax for a limit on local bans under another name, and found none. The one rule on rental websites asks them to post a notice about local licensing.
Election day changed none of these local rules. Horry County, Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach and Surfside Beach had no question on the Nov. 3 ballot.

## What are Myrtle Beach's short-term rental rules?
Myrtle Beach keeps short-term rentals out of most of its residential neighborhoods. In the city, a short-term rental is a stay of under 90 days.

- Residential zones. No zone that begins with R allows them, except RMV (Residential Multifamily Visitor). Most traditional neighborhoods are in R zones.

- Grandfathered houses. Fewer than 30 houses in those zones, citywide, can keep renting short-term under the old rules.

- License and fines. Every rental needs a city business license. A violation can bring a fine of up to $500, 30 days in jail, or both, on conviction.

Photo: Loadmaster
Hotel and condo towers on the oceanfront in Myrtle Beach.

The city added one more rule in December 2024. City council voted unanimously for a conversion overlay on commercial districts east of Kings Highway, on the ocean side. Under it, short-term rentals there may not convert to long-term rentals. It took effect at once, and a temporary moratorium was set to expire.
Two kinds of units are exempt from the overlay. One is a unit that already has a long-term rental license. The other is a former primary residence or second home that was never rented.

## What are the rules in North Myrtle Beach, Surfside Beach and the rest of Horry County?
North Myrtle Beach allows short-term rentals with a city business license , renewed every year. The city requires no special zoning or permit beyond the license. Each rental collects accommodations tax for the city, the county and the state.
Surfside Beach and Horry County, outside the cities, each decide their own rules too. Our agents check the zone of any Surfside Beach or county address with the town or county before you make an offer. Our short-term rental rules guide lists the rules town by town on the Grand Strand.
Want to buy a rental?
We show you rentals in the zones where short stays are allowed, in Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach and Surfside Beach.
Have us find you your next investment

## How much tax does a Grand Strand short-term rental collect, and who decides it?
The state charges 7% of the rent on rooms and homes rented to short-stay guests. A city or county can add a local accommodations tax of up to 3%. A county may not charge more than 1.5% inside a city unless the city agrees.
Three kinds of rentals owe no state accommodations tax:

- Renting fewer than six rooms in the home you live in.

- A home rented out for 14 days or fewer in a year, the 14-day rule in federal tax law.

- A stay of 90 days or more in a row by the same guest.

Both rates are in state law, so the legislature can change them with an ordinary bill. Our accommodations tax guide gives the full rate for each Grand Strand city and county.

## What would H. 3861 have done to Myrtle Beach's rules?
H. 3861 said no city or county may make or enforce a rule that bans renting a home to short-term guests. Myrtle Beach could no longer have kept stays of fewer than 29 days out of its R zones.

- What counts as short-term. The bill applies to stays of fewer than 29 days in a row. Myrtle Beach's rule applies to stays under 90 days. A stay of 29 to 89 days would still have been the city's to rule on.

- The penalty. A city or county that kept a ban could not collect tax at the 6% ratio on "qualifying property," in the bill's words. The State Treasurer would also hold back its state aid until it repealed the ban.

- Who filed it. Reps. Hewitt, Bailey, Brewer, Murphy and Bannister. Rep. William Bailey represents Horry County's District 104.

- What happened to it. It was introduced in January 2025 and sent to the House Medical, Military, Public and Municipal Affairs Committee. We checked the bill's record: the committee never voted on it.

A rental is taxed on 6% of its value, and a home you live in on 4%. Our page on the proposed rental property tax cut shows what it costs on a Myrtle Beach rental.

## Could the new South Carolina House pass a bill like H. 3861?
Yes. If all 124 members vote, it would take 63 House votes, the same as in the old House. A bill like H. 3861 is an ordinary bill. It does not need two-thirds. Each house must read it three times , on three separate days, and pass it. In the House, a tie fails.
South Carolina House, 124 seats 63 83
Before the election 89 Republicans, 35 Democrats

After, unofficial count 79 Republicans, 45 Democrats

- Republican seats

- Democratic seats

- 63: the yes votes a bill needs if all 124 members vote. 83: the votes to override a veto.

- The House. In the unofficial count, Republicans led in 79 races and Democrats in 45. Before the election it had 89 Republicans and 35 Democrats.

- The Senate. It was not on the ballot except for one special race. It still has 34 Republicans and 12 Democrats.

- The recounts. Two House races were within 1 point and qualify for an automatic recount. If one recount changed the result, Republicans would hold 78 or 80 seats. If both did, they would hold 79. Each is more than 63 and fewer than 83.

### What changed: the votes to override a veto
After a governor's veto , two-thirds of each house must vote again to pass the bill. If all members vote, that is 83 in the House and 31 in the Senate.
Republicans held 89 House seats before, enough to override alone. With 79, a House override would need some Democratic votes.

### What did the candidates say about short-term rentals?
Nothing we found. Alan Wilson won the governor's race after Jermaine Johnson conceded. We checked Wilson's priorities page and found no short-term rental item, and we found no statement from Johnson. Annie Andrews, the AP's winner of the U.S. Senate race, has none on her issue pages, and state zoning is not a federal vote.
Of the 11 House districts on Horry County's ballot, Republicans led in 8 and Democrats in 3. Rep. Bailey, a sponsor of H. 3861, won District 104 with 66.88% in the unofficial count. Our 2026 election guide has every result that matters for a home here.

## What happened when Arizona's and Florida's legislatures took this power from cities?
Both legislatures took away the power to ban. Arizona later changed its law. Florida's legislature passed a change in 2024, and the governor vetoed it. In order:

- 2016 Arizona bars local bans SB 1350 : "A city or town may not prohibit vacation rentals or short-term rentals."

- 2022 Arizona gives cities some rules back SB 1168 kept the ban on bans. Cities can now require a permit, with a fee of no more than $250 or the cost, whichever is less. They can also require an emergency contact, notice to neighbors, and liability coverage of $500,000, which the booking platform's coverage can meet. They can suspend a permit for repeat violations.

- 2024 Florida's governor vetoes a vacation rental bill The bill, CS/SB 280 , would have made platforms collect and pay the taxes and moved licensing to the state.

- 2025 South Carolina's H. 3861 is introduced It never left committee.

- Now Florida keeps its older local rules Florida law today says local governments may not ban vacation rentals or limit how long or how often they are rented. Local rules adopted on or before June 1, 2011 still stand.

In Arizona, cities lost the power to ban in 2016. Six years later the legislature let them require permits, contacts and insurance. In Florida, local rules from before the cutoff still stand. We found no study that measured what either change did to home prices or rents.

## Do short-term rental limits change home prices and rents?
In the one peer-reviewed study we found, by a small amount. In Los Angeles County, 18 of 88 cities adopted home-sharing rules. The study , in the Journal of Urban Economics in 2021, measured what followed in those cities:
18 of 88 cities adopted limits
50% fewer short-term listings
About 2% lower home prices
About 2% lower rents

Myrtle Beach is a different market, and a state law like H. 3861 would work in the other direction, opening zones instead of closing them. The study shows how large the effect was there. It is not a forecast for the Grand Strand.

## What could happen to Grand Strand short-term rentals in the next two years, and after five?
Three paths, each from a past example. None is a forecast of what the new legislature will pass.

### No new state law
Where it happened: H. 3861 got no committee vote in 2025 and 2026.
Next two years: Myrtle Beach's R-zone rule, its overlay and North Myrtle Beach's license rule stay as they are.
After five: any change comes from a city or county council vote.

### A ban on local bans
Where it happened: Arizona in 2016, and the H. 3861 text.
Next two years: Myrtle Beach could not enforce its R-zone rule on stays under 29 days. Reading the Los Angeles study in reverse, prices and rents in those zones could rise by up to about 2%, or not at all. That is our inference, not a forecast.
After five: in Arizona, six years later, the legislature let cities require permits, emergency contacts and insurance.

### A law that keeps older local rules
Where it happened: Florida. Its law keeps local rules adopted on or before June 1, 2011.
Next two years: a cutoff like Florida's keeps the local rules adopted before it. Myrtle Beach's R-zone rule could stay if it came before the cutoff, and new local bans would be barred.
After five: in Florida, the legislature passed a bill moving licensing to the state in 2024, and the governor vetoed it.

Any new law needs the same steps first. A bill is filed and usually passes a committee. It wins 63 House votes if all 124 members vote, then a Senate majority. Then the governor signs it or lets it become law without a signature.
If all members vote, a veto would then need 83 House votes and 31 Senate votes to override.

## Short-term rental rule questions

### Can Myrtle Beach ban short-term rentals?
Yes. No South Carolina law stops a city from barring them through zoning. Myrtle Beach bars stays of under 90 days in every zone that begins with R, except RMV. Fewer than 30 houses citywide are grandfathered.

### Did the 2026 election change short-term rental rules on the Grand Strand?
No. Horry County, Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach and Surfside Beach had no local ballot question. No state law on the subject passed. The rules change only by a council vote or a new state law.

### What was H. 3861?
A 2025 South Carolina House bill that would have barred cities and counties from banning short-term rentals of fewer than 29 days. A government that kept a ban would have lost its state aid. It never got a committee vote.

The state charges 7% of the rent. A city or county may add up to 3%. Rentals of 90 days or more to the same guest owe no accommodations tax.

# Growth, Roads and Permits: What the New Leaders Mean for Building in Horry County
By Devin Day , Chief Operating Officer, and Abdulla Hijazi , Chief Marketing Officer · Reviewed by Tim Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated November 4, 2026
The 2026 election changed no rule for building in Horry County. The road tax, the impact fees and the flood rules are the same as before the vote.

The short answer
Voters approved the road money, the RIDE IV sales tax, in 2024. The county council approved the current impact fee schedule before the election, and no road or growth question was on the Horry ballot.
Interstate 73 has no start date, because funding for most of its $1.6 billion cost has not been identified. The leaders who won have road plans, and none of those plans is a law yet.

## How many new homes is Horry County permitting each year?
Horry County's 2025 count was 6,418 single-family homes permitted, down from 7,269 in 2024. The 2024 count is the most of any year from 2005 to 2025. Since 2021 the county has permitted between 6,356 and 7,269 a year.
Single-family homes permitted in Horry County, by year From 6,484 in 2006 to 1,388 in 2010, then up in most years to the most of any year shown, 7,269 in 2024. Census county permit counts.
In the last housing slowdown, permits dropped by about four in five from 2006 to 2010, and the county did not pass 6,000 again until 2021.
Almost all of today's building is single-family homes. Units in buildings of five or more, such as apartments and condos, were 5,132 in 2005 and 77 in the latest year. For the monthly count and the communities being built now, see what is being built on the Grand Strand .

## What did the 2026 election change for building in Horry County?
Every county council seat on the ballot went to a Republican, 4 of the 7 without an opponent.

## What is RIDE IV, the Horry County road tax?
RIDE IV is a 1% sales tax for road projects in Horry County, approved by voters in November 2024.
56.78% of Horry voters said yes in 2024
25 years or $6.35 billion, whichever comes first
$450 million for I-73 , as WIS reported the list

One item is a local match for I-73 : up to half the cost of building it from SC 22 to the Horry County line. That money can be spent only after SCDOT, the state Department of Transportation, has signed contracts to finish I-73 from Horry County to I-95 . The WIS report on I-73 gives the $450 million figure.

## When will I-73 be built in South Carolina?
No start date has been announced. Work cannot begin until SCDOT identifies where the money comes from. The South Carolina section is estimated at $1.6 billion, and funding for most of that cost has not been identified.
I-73 in South Carolina: what has happened When What happened
November 2024 What happened Horry voters approved RIDE IV. Its I-73 match can be spent only once SCDOT has signed contracts to finish the road to I-95 .
2024 to 2026 What happened Gov. Henry McMaster left I-73 out of his executive budget in each of the three years.
February 2026 What happened SCDOT reported the right of way 99% bought between I-95 and US 501 , and 95% between US 501 and the Little Pee Dee River.
August 2026 What happened President Trump said "they're going to have the funding that's necessary." He named no source for the money.

### What has to happen before building starts

- The money Funding for the rest of the $1.6 billion has to be identified.

- The contracts SCDOT signs the contracts to finish I-73 to I-95 . After that, the RIDE IV match can be spent.

Governor-elect Wilson will propose the next executive budgets. Neither leader's plan names a road project.

## What are Horry County impact fees on a new home?
A single-family home of about 1,500 square feet pays $1,615 in total in Horry County impact fees. The fee depends on the kind of building and its size. The county council approved this schedule unanimously in July 2026, as Ordinance 30-2026. Horry County has charged impact fees since 2021.
$1,615 for a single-family home of about 1,500 square feet

Impact fees are a county power under the state's Development Impact Fee Act . Before charging them on homes, a county must estimate the effect on affordable housing, and the ordinance needs a positive majority of the council. Any change to the fee is a vote of the county council, including the members elected this year.
On a new home, we ask the builder whether the fee is already in the price, so you compare homes on the same terms. Our guide to buying new construction covers the rest of the process.

## What are the flood building rules for a new home in Horry County?
In a flood zone, the lowest floor of a new home must be built above the expected flood level. The extra height is called freeboard. In June 2021 the county council advanced an ordinance raising the freeboard for new homes in flood zones from 1 foot to 3 feet. Its final vote was scheduled for July 13, 2021.
Floor height above the flood level for a new home in a flood zone Left, the old rule of 1 foot. Right, the 3 feet in the ordinance the council advanced in 2021. Our drawing.
We confirm the current height rule with the county for any lot in a flood zone before you buy, because it changes the cost of the build. What a flood zone means for insurance is on our page on flood insurance after the election and our coastal insurance guide .

## What could happen to new home and land prices in Horry County, short and long term?
In the next year or two, we expect the pattern of the last five years to continue unless the national market turns. Over five years or more, Horry prices have fallen about 26% (2008 to 2012) and risen to about 2.4 times the low (2012 to 2026).
What happened in Horry County before Period What happened Source

2021 to 2025 What happened Permits stayed between 6,356 and 7,269 a year. Source Census permits

### The next one to two years
Local prices rose in the year after each of the last five elections, whichever party won. The latest yearly change, 0.8%, is inside the index's error of about 2%, so it reads as flat. If the national market holds, we expect permits to stay in the 2021 to 2025 range in the table. If it turns as it did from 2006 to 2010, plan for that slowdown, the first row of the table.

## What does Chapter3 check before you buy land or a new home in Horry County?
Our agents check four things for the lot you want, from the county's own records and the road plans:

- Permits around the lot We pull the building permits near it, so you see what is being built around it before you buy.

- The flood height We confirm the county's current floor-height rule for the lot's flood zone, and what it means for the build.

- Road plans We check the RIDE IV project list and the I-73 route for work near the lot.

- The fees We ask the builder whether the impact fee is in the price.

Common questions

## Horry County growth and roads questions

### When will I-73 be complete in South Carolina?
No date has been announced. SCDOT has not identified the money for most of the estimated 1.6 billion dollar cost, and work cannot begin until it does.

### How much are Horry County impact fees?
A single-family home of about 1,500 square feet pays 1,615 dollars in total under the county's current schedule. A larger home or another type of building pays a different amount.

### Was a road tax on the Horry County ballot in 2026?
No. The 2026 Horry County ballot had no ballot question. Voters approved the RIDE IV sales tax in 2024, with 56.78 percent voting yes.

### Who can change impact fees in Horry County?
The county council, by ordinance with a positive majority, after a report on the effect on affordable housing. The state Development Impact Fee Act allows the fees.

### Is Horry County still building as many homes?
Yes. The county's 2025 count was 6,418 single-family homes, after 7,269 in 2024, the most of any year from 2005 to 2025.
